Two are the heads of view, four are the pure heads, and the head-roots are in groups of three; one should analyze these eighteen.

Ete hi sassatucchedavasena vuttā dve diṭṭhisīsā nāma, “asmi, bhavissaṃ siyaṃ, apāhaṃ siya”nti ete cattāro suddhasīsā nāma, “itthamasmī”tiādayo [M 2.0018] tayo tayoti dvādasa sīsamūlakā nāmāti veditabbaṃ. Idha pāḷiyaṃ rūpārammaṇādivasena taṇhā āgatāti āha “ajjhattikarūpādinissitānī”ti. Aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritānīti ānetvā sambandho. Iminā asmīti iminā abhisekasenāpaccādinā “khattiyo aha”nti mūlabhāvato “asmī”ti hoti. Sesaṃ pubbe vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Saṅgaheti taṇhāya yathāvuttavibhāgassa saṃkhipanavasena saṅgaṇhane kariyamāne. “Chayime, bhikkhave, taṇhākāyā”tiādi niddeso. “Rūpe taṇhā rūpataṇhā”tiādi niddesattho. “Kāmarāgabhāvenā”tiādiko, “ajjhattikassupādāyā”tiādiko ca niddesavitthāro. “Rūpādīsu ārammaṇesu chaḷevā”tiādiko saṅgaho.

For the two stated by way of eternalism and annihilationism are the 'view-heads.' These four—'I am,' 'I will be,' 'I might be,' and 'May I be'—are the 'pure heads.' It should be understood that the twelve beginning with 'I am thus,' taken three by three, are the 'head-roots.' Here in the Pāḷi text, craving is presented by way of form-object, etc.; hence it says, 'dependent on internal form, etc.' The connection is made by supplying 'eighteen proliferations of craving.' By this thought 'I am a khattiya,' which is the root state arising from this anointing, army, provisions, etc., there comes to be the thought 'I am.' The rest should be understood in the way previously explained. As to the summary: when the aforesaid analysis of craving is summarized by way of condensation, the exposition is: 'Monks, there are these six bodies of craving,' etc. The meaning of the exposition is: 'Craving in regard to form is craving for form,' etc. The detailed explanation is: 'by way of sensual lust,' etc., and 'having clung to the internal,' etc. The summary is: 'in objects such as form, there are just six,' etc.

Yasmā cakkhudvārādīsu ekekasmiṃ dvāre uppajjanakaviññāṇāni viya anekā eva vedanā, tasmā tā rāsivasena ekajjhaṃ gahetvā “cha vedanākāyā”ti vuttanti āha “vedanāsamūhā”ti. Nissayabhāvena uppattidvārabhāvena nānāpaccayā honti cakkhudhātuādayo, tā kucchinā dhārentiyo viya posentiyo viya ca hontīti tāsaṃ mātusadisatā vuttā. Cakkhusamphassahetūti nissayādicakkhusamphassapaccayā. Ayanti ayaṃ vedanā “cakkhusamphassajā vedanā”tiādinā sādhāraṇato vuttā. Etthāti etasmiṃ vedanāpade. Sabbasaṅgāhikāti kusalākusalavipākakiriyānaṃ vasena sabbasaṅgāhikā. Evaṃ vibhaṅge āgatanayena sādhāraṇato vatvāpi idhādhippetavedanameva dassetuṃ “vipākavasena panā”tiādimāha. Cakkhumhi samphassoti cakkhumhi nissayabhūte uppannaphasso. Esa nayo sesesu. Yasmā cakkhādīni visuddhimagge khandhaniddese lakkhaṇādivibhāgato, āyatananiddese visesato, sāmaññato ca saddatthadassanādivasena vibhāvitāni, tasmā “yaṃ vattabbaṃ…pe… vuttamevā”ti āha.

Because many feelings arise at each single door, such as the eye-door, just like the consciousnesses that arise there, they are taken together as a heap and called the 'six bodies of feeling'; thus it says 'collections of feeling.' The eye-element and others are various conditions, by way of being a basis and a door of origin. They are like those who bear in the womb and nourish, and thus their similarity to a mother is stated. 'With eye-contact as cause' means conditioned by eye-contact as support, etc. This feeling is stated generally as 'feeling born of eye-contact,' etc. 'Here' means in this section on feeling. 'All-inclusive' means it is all-inclusive by way of wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional states. Although it has been stated generally in this way, according to the method found in the Vibhaṅga, in order to show only the feeling intended here, it says, 'but by way of resultant,' etc. 'Contact at the eye' means contact that has arisen with the eye as its basis. This is the method for the rest. Because the eye and other faculties have been explained in the Visuddhimagga—in the exposition of the aggregates by way of their division into characteristic, etc.; in the exposition of the bases, specifically; and generally by way of showing the meaning of the words, etc.—therefore, it is said: 'Whatever should be said... etc. ... has already been said.'

Namanalakkhaṇanti ārammaṇābhimukhaṃ hutvā namanasabhāvaṃ tena vinā appavattanato. Ruppanalakkhaṇaṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Vedanākkhandho pana ekāva vedanā. Sabbadubbalacittāni nāma pañcaviññāṇāni[V 2.0017]. Nanu tattha jīvitacittaṭṭhitiyo [M 2.0019] ca santīti? Saccaṃ, tāsaṃ pana kiccaṃ na tathā pākaṭaṃ, yathā cetanādīnanti te evettha pāḷiyaṃ uddhaṭā. Yena mahantapātubhāvādinā kāraṇena. Etthāti etasmiṃ mahābhūtaniddese. Añño vinicchayanayoti “vacanatthato kalāpato”tiādinā lakkhaṇādinicchayato añño vinicchayanayo. Nanu so catudhātuvavatthāne vutto, na rūpakkhandhaniddeseti? Tattha vuttepi “catudhātuvavatthāne vuttānī”ti atidesavasena vuttattā “rūpakkhandhaniddese vutto”ti vuttaṃ. Upādāyāti paṭicca. Bhūtāni hi paṭicca uppajjamānaṃ upādārūpaṃ “tāni gahetvā”ti vuttaṃ avissajjanato. Nissāyātipi eke tesaṃ nissayapaccayabhāvato. Pubbakālakiriyā nāma ekaṃsato aparakālakiriyāpekkhāti pāṭhasesena atthaṃ vadati. Vibhattivipallāsena vinā eva atthaṃ dassetuṃ “samūhatthe vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Samūhasambandhe sāminiddesena samūhattho dīpitoti taṃ dassento āha “samūhaṃ upādāyā”ti. Dhammasaṅgaṇiyaṃ (dha. sa. 584) āgatanayena “tevīsatividha”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha hi hadayavatthu na niddiṭṭhaṃ, “yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāyā”ti vā paṭṭhāne (paṭṭhāna. 1.1.8) āgatattā hadayavatthumpi gahetvā jātirūpabhāvena upacayasantatiyo ekato katvā “tevīsatividha”nti vuttaṃ.

The characteristic of bending is the nature of inclining towards an object, because without that it does not occur. The characteristic of being afflicted is as stated above. The feeling aggregate, however, is just feeling. The five sense-consciousnesses are called all the weak consciousnesses. But are not life, mind, and duration also present there? True, but their function is not as manifest as that of volition and so on; hence these are cited here in the Pāli text for the reason of their great manifestation and so on. Here means in this exposition of the great elements. Another method of analysis means a method of analysis different from the determination by way of characteristics, etc., namely, the one beginning ‘by way of literal meaning, by way of grouping.’ But was that not stated in the analysis of the four elements, not in the exposition of the form aggregate? Though stated there, because it is mentioned by way of extension as ‘stated in the analysis of the four elements,’ it is said to be ‘stated in the exposition of the form aggregate.’ Dependent means dependently arising. For derived form, arising dependently on the primary elements, is said to be ‘having taken them’ because it does not relinquish them. Some say it means ‘relying on,’ because they are a support condition. The past-time action is so called because it is necessarily related to a subsequent action; this is the meaning he states by supplying the rest of the reading. To show the meaning without any change of grammatical case, it is said, ‘or in the sense of a collection,’ and so on. Since the meaning of collection is indicated by the genitive case in the sense of a collective relationship, showing this he says, ‘dependent on the collection.’ According to the method that comes in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī (Dhs. 584), it is said to be ‘twenty-threefold.’ For there the heart-base is not specified. Or, because it comes in the Paṭṭhāna (Paṭṭh. 1.1.8) as ‘relying on which form,’ the heart-base is also included, and by combining growth and continuity into one as origination-form, it is said to be ‘twenty-threefold.’

Cakkhussa viññāṇanti vā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ. Asādhāraṇakāraṇena cāyaṃ niddeso. “Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”nti ettha sabbalokiyavipākaviññāṇassa gahetabbattā “tebhūmakavipākacittassetaṃ adhivacana”nti vuttaṃ.

Eye-consciousness means consciousness of the eye. And this explanation is due to the uncommon cause. In the statement ‘Conditioned by formations is consciousness,’ since all mundane resultant consciousness should be taken, it is said: ‘This is a designation for the resultant consciousness belonging to the three planes.’

Abhisaṅkharaṇalakkhaṇoti āyūhanasabhāvo. Copanavasenāti viññattisaṃcopanavasena, kāyaviññattiyā samuṭṭhāpanavasenāti attho. Vacanabhedavasenāti vacībheduppādavasena, vacīviññattiyā samuṭṭhāpanavasenāti attho. Evaṃ copanaṃ na bhaveyyāti dassetuṃ “raho nisīditvā cintentassā”ti vuttaṃ. Ekūnatiṃsāti ettha abhiññācetanāvinimuttā eva ekūnatiṃsa cetanā veditabbā tassā vipākaviññāṇassa paccayattābhāvato.

The characteristic of forming is the nature of accumulating. By way of instigation means by way of instigating intimation; the meaning is by way of producing bodily intimation. By way of verbal utterance means by way of producing verbal utterance; the meaning is by way of producing verbal intimation. To show that such instigation would not occur, it is said, ‘of one sitting alone and thinking.’ Regarding twenty-nine: here, the twenty-nine volitions apart from the volition of direct knowledge should be understood, because that is not a condition for resultant consciousness.

Dukkheti ekampi idaṃ bhummavacanaṃ saṃsilesananissayavisayabyāpanavasena attānaṃ bhinditvā viniyogaṃ gacchatīti “catūhi kāraṇehī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ekopi [M 2.0020] hi vibhattiniddeso anekadhā viniyogaṃ gacchati yathā taddhitatthe uttarapadasamāhāreti. Tanti aññāṇaṃ. Dukkhasaccanti hadayavatthulakkhaṇaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ. Assāti aññāṇassa. Nissayapaccayabhāvenāti purejātanissayabhāvena. Sahajātanissayapaccayabhāvena pana taṃsahajātā phassādayo vattabbā. Ārammaṇapaccayabhāvena dukkhasaccaṃ assa ārammaṇanti yojanā. Dukkhasaccanti upayogaekavacanaṃ[V 2.0018]. Etanti aññāṇaṃ. Tassāti dukkhasaccassa. “Paṭicchādetī”ti ettha vuttaṃ paṭicchādanākāraṃ dassetuṃ “yāthāvā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ñāṇavippayuttacittenapi ekadesena yāthāvato lakkhaṇapaṭivedho hotiyevāti “yāthāvalakkhaṇapaṭivedhanivāraṇenā”ti vatvā “ñāṇapavattiyā cettha appadānenā”ti vuttanti vadanti. Purimaṃ pana paṭivedhañāṇuppattiyā nisedhakathādassanaṃ, pacchimaṃ anubodhañāṇuppattiyā. Evamettha attho veditabbo. Etthāti dukkhasacce.

In the word dukkha: this single locative expression is divided in its application by way of connection, support, domain, and pervasion, and thus it is said, ‘by four reasons,’ and so on. For even a single specification of a grammatical case is applied in many ways, as in the case of a taddhita suffix, a final member of a compound, or a collective compound. That means ignorance. The truth of suffering means the truth of suffering characterized by the heart-base. Of that means of ignorance. By way of support condition means by way of prenascent support. But by way of conascent support condition, contact and so on, which are co-nascent with it, should be mentioned. By way of object condition: the truth of suffering is its object—this is the construction. The truth of suffering: this is a singular of specific application. This means ignorance. Of that means of the truth of suffering. To show the mode of concealing stated here in the word ‘conceals,’ it is said, ‘as it really is,’ and so on. They say that since even with a mind dissociated from knowledge there is in one respect a penetration of the characteristic as it really is, after saying ‘by preventing the penetration of the characteristic as it really is,’ it is also said, ‘and by not granting the occurrence of knowledge here.’ The former shows the statement of prohibition with respect to the arising of the knowledge of penetration, the latter with respect to the arising of the knowledge of comprehension. Thus the meaning should be understood here. Here means in the truth of suffering.

Sahajātassa aññāṇassa samudayasaccaṃ vatthu hoti nissayapaccayabhāvatoti vuttaṃ “vatthuto”ti. Ārammaṇatoti ārammaṇapaccayabhāvena. Yasmā samudayasaccaṃ aññāṇassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti, tasmā “dukkhasamudaye aññāṇa”nti vuttanti attho. Paṭicchādanaṃ dukkhasacce vuttanayameva ekeneva kāraṇena itaresaṃ tiṇṇaṃ asambhavato, kiṃ pana etaṃ ekaṃ kāraṇanti āha “paṭicchādanato”ti. Idaṃ vitthārato vibhāvetuṃ “nirodhapaṭipadānaṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tadārabbhāti taṃ ārabbha taṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā. Pacchimañhi saccadvayanti nirodho maggo. Tañhi nayagambhīrattā. Duddasanti saṇhasukhumadhammattā sabhāveneva gambhīratāya duddasaṃ duviññeyyaṃ duravaggāhaṃ. Tatthāti purime saccadvaye. Andhabhūtanti andhakārabhūtaṃ. Na pavattati ārammaṇaṃ kātuṃ na visahati. Vacanīyattenāti vācakabhāvena tathā upaṭṭhānato. Sabhāvalakkhaṇassa duddasattāti pīḷanādiāyūhanādivasena “idaṃ dukkhaṃ, ayaṃ samudayo”ti (ma. ni. 484; 3.104) yāthāvato sabhāvalakkhaṇassa duddasattā duviññeyyattā purimadvayaṃ gambhīraṃ. Tatthāti purimasmiṃ saccadvaye. Vipallāsaggāhavasena pavattatīti subhādiviparītaggāhānaṃ paccayabhāvavasena aññāṇaṃ pavattati.

The truth of the origin is the basis for conascent ignorance because it is a support condition; thus it is said, ‘from the basis.’ From the object means by way of object condition. Because the truth of the origin is the object of ignorance, therefore it is said, ‘ignorance in regard to the origin of suffering’—this is the meaning. Concealing is in the same way as was stated for the truth of suffering, by one reason alone, because the other three are impossible. But what is this one reason? He says: ‘from its concealing.’ To explain this in detail, it is said, ‘For of cessation and the path,’ and so on. Having taken that as object means having taken it, having made it the object. For the latter pair of truths are cessation and the path. For that is because of the profundity of the method. Hard to see: because they are subtle and fine states, they are by their very nature profound, hard to see, difficult to understand, difficult to penetrate. Therein means in the former pair of truths. Become blind means become darkness. It does not proceed; it is unable to take it as object. By its expressibility means because of its being the designator, since it is present as such. Because its specific characteristic is hard to see: by way of affliction, accumulation, and so on, the specific characteristic ‘this is suffering, this is the origin’ is, as it really is, hard to see, difficult to understand; thus the former pair is profound. Therein means in the former pair of truths. It proceeds by way of distorted grasping means ignorance proceeds by way of being a condition for the inverted grasp of things as beautiful, etc.

Idāni [M 2.0021] “dukkhe aññāṇa”ntiādīsu pakārantarenapi atthaṃ dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dukkheti ettāvatāti “aññāṇanti vuccamānāya avijjāya dukkhe”ti ettakena. Saṅgahatoti samodhānato. Kiccatoti asampaṭivedhakiccato. Aññāṇamivāti visayasabhāvaṃ yāthāvato paṭivijjhituṃ appadānakiccamiva. “Dukkhe”tiādinā tattha avijjā pavattati, visesato niddiṭṭhaṃ hotīti katvā sabbattheva tathā avisiṭṭhasabhāvadassanaṃ idanti dassetuṃ “avisesato panā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Now, to show the meaning in the phrases beginning ‘ignorance in regard to suffering’ in another way, it is said, ‘furthermore,’ and so on. Therein, in regard to suffering is this much: by this much, ‘in regard to suffering, of ignorance which is called nescience.’ By inclusion means by combination. By function means by the function of non-penetration. Like ignorance means like the function of not granting the penetration of the specific nature of the object as it really is. By the phrase beginning ‘in regard to suffering,’ it is shown that ignorance operates there, that it is specifically indicated; and to show that this is a way of seeing its nature as undifferentiated in all cases, it is said, ‘but without distinction,’ and so on.

Khaṇikanirodhassa idha anadhippetattā ayujjamānattā virāgaggahaṇato ca avijjādīnaṃ paṭipakkhavasena paṭibāhanaṃ idha “nirodho”ti adhippeto, so ca nesaṃ sabbaso anuppajjanamevāti [V 2.0019] āha “nirodho hotīti anuppādo hotī”ti. “Avijjā nirujjhati etthāti avijjānirodho, saṅkhārā nirujjhanti etthāti saṅkhāranirodho”ti evaṃ sabbehi etehi nirodhapadehi nibbānassa desitattā daṭṭhabbā. Tenāha “nibbānaṃ hī”tiādi. Vaṭṭavivaṭṭanti vaṭṭañca vivaṭṭañca. “Dvādasahī”ti idaṃ paccekaṃ yojetabbaṃ “anulomato dvādasahi padehi vaṭṭaṃ, paṭilomato dvādasahi vivaṭṭaṃ idha dassita”nti.

Here, since momentary cessation is not intended and is not applicable, and since dispassion is included, the warding off of ignorance and so on by way of opposition is intended here by ‘cessation.’ And since that is their non-arising altogether, he says, ‘cessation occurs means non-arising occurs.’ ‘Ignorance ceases herein, thus it is cessation of ignorance; formations cease herein, thus it is cessation of formations’—in this way, it should be seen that Nibbāna is taught by all these terms for cessation. Therefore he says, ‘For Nibbāna is,’ and so on. Vaṭṭavivaṭṭa means the round and the ending of the round. ‘By twelve’: this should be connected with each part thus: ‘Here the round is shown by twelve terms in direct order, and the ending of the round by twelve terms in reverse order.’

Vibhaṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Vibhaṅga Sutta is completed.

3. Paṭipadāsuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Discourse on the Path

3. Micchā paṭipajjati etāyāti micchāpaṭipadā, vaṭṭagāmimaggo dukkhāvahattā. Taṃ micchāpaṭipadaṃ. Tenāha “aniyyānikapaṭipadā”ti. So puññābhisaṅkhāro kathaṃ micchāpaṭipadā hotīti? Sampattibhave sukhāvahova hotīti adhippāyo. Vaṭṭasīsattāti vaṭṭapakkhiyānaṃ uttamaṅgabhāvato. Antamasoti ukkaṃsapariyantaṃ sandhāya vadati avakaṃsapariyantato. “Idaṃ me puññaṃ nibbānādhigamāya paccayo hotū”ti evaṃ nibbānaṃ patthetvā pavattitaṃ. Paṇṇamuṭṭhidānamattanti sākapaṇṇamuṭṭhidānamattaṃ. Appatvāti antogadhahetu esa niddeso, apāpetvāti attho. Yadaggena [M 2.0022] vā paṭipajjanato arahattaṃ pattoti vuccati, tadaggena tadāvahā paṭipadāpi pattāti vuccatīti “appatvā”ti vuttaṃ. Anulomavasenāti anulomapaṭiccasamuppādavasena. Paṭilomavasenāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Paṭipadā pucchitāti etena paṭipadā desetuṃ āraddhāti ayampi attho saṅgahito yathāraddhassa atthassa kathetukamyatāpucchāya idhāgatattā. Anulomapaṭiccasamuppādadesanāyampettha byatirekamukhena avijjādinirodhā pana vijjāya sati hoti saṅkhārānaṃ asambhavoti vuttaṃ “nibbānaṃ bhājita”nti. Sarūpena pana tāya vaṭṭameva pakāsitaṃ. Vakkhati hi pariyosāne “vaṭṭavivaṭṭameva kathita”nti. Niyyātaneti nigamane. Phalenāti pattabbaphalena paṭipadāya sampāpakahetuno dassitattā. Yathā hi tividho hetu ñāpako, nibbattako, sampāpakoti, evaṃ tividhaṃ phalaṃ ñāpetabbaṃ, nibbattetabbaṃ, sampāpetabbanti. Tasmā pattabbaphalena nibbānena taṃsampāpakahetubhūtāya paṭipadāya dassitattāti attho. Tenāha “phalena hetthā”tiādi. Ayaṃ vuccatīti evaṃ nibbānaphalā ayaṃ “sammāpaṭipadā”ti vuccati. Asesavirāgā asesanirodhāti samucchedappahānavasena avijjāya asesavirajjanato asesanirujjhanato ca. Padadvayenapi anuppādanirodhameva vadati. Tañhi nibbānaṃ. Dutiyavikappe ayaṃ ettha adhippāyo – yena maggena karaṇabhūtena asesanirodho hoti, avijjāya asesanirodho yaṃ āgamma hoti, taṃ maggaṃ dassetunti. Evañhi satīti evaṃ padabhājanassa [V 2.0020] nibbānassa padatthe sati. Sānubhāvā paṭipadā vibhattā hotīti avijjāya asesanirodhahetupaṭipadā tattha sātisayasāmatthiyasamāyogato sānubhāvā vibhattā hoti. Micchāpaṭipadāgahaṇenettha vaṭṭassapi vibhattattā vuttaṃ “vaṭṭavivaṭṭameva kathita”nti.

3. One proceeds wrongly by this; thus, it is wrong practice—the path leading to the cycle, because it brings suffering. That is wrong practice. Hence, it is said, 'the path that does not lead out.' How does the meritorious formation become wrong practice? The intention is that it brings happiness in a fortunate existence. Due to being the head of the cycle—because it is the highest part for those on the side of the cycle. 'Even the least' is said with reference to the highest limit, excluding the lowest limit. 'May this merit of mine be a condition for attaining Nibbāna'—thus, it is undertaken with the aspiration for Nibbāna. 'Even a handful of leaves'—this refers to the mere offering of a handful of vegetable leaves. 'Without reaching'—this explanation has an implicit cause; the meaning is 'without causing to reach.' Or, since by the practice through which one is said to have attained arahantship, that practice which brings it is also said to have been attained, 'without reaching' is said. 'In forward order' means by way of dependent origination in forward order. 'In reverse order'—here too, the same method applies. 'The path is questioned'—this means the explanation of the path is begun. This meaning is also included, as the desire to speak has arisen from the question about the intended subject. Here, in the teaching on dependent origination in forward order, it is also presented by way of exclusion—'but from the cessation of ignorance, when there is knowledge, formations do not occur.' Thus, it is said, 'Nibbāna is analyzed.' Yet, by its nature, the cycle itself is revealed. For it will be said at the conclusion, 'Only the cycle and the escape from the cycle have been spoken of.' Niyyātane means in the conclusion. Phalena (by the fruit) means: by the attainable fruit, because the path is shown as the cause that accomplishes it. Just as there are three kinds of causes—indicative, productive, and accomplishing—so too, a fruit is threefold: to be indicated, to be produced, and to be accomplished. Therefore, the meaning is that the path, which is the cause that accomplishes Nibbāna, is shown by means of the attainable fruit, Nibbāna. Hence it is said, 'by the fruit as cause,' etc. This is called—thus, this path that has Nibbāna as its fruit is called 'right practice.' 'From complete dispassion, from complete cessation'—this is due to the abandoning of ignorance through eradication, its complete fading away and complete cessation. By these two terms, only cessation without arising is spoken of. For that is Nibbāna. In the second alternative, the intention here is this—to show that path, as the means, by which complete cessation occurs, the complete cessation of ignorance that depends on it. For when this is so—that is, when this is the meaning of the word in the analysis of 'Nibbāna'—the path is analyzed as having power. The path that is the cause of the complete cessation of ignorance is analyzed here as having power due to its association with superior capacity. By the inclusion of wrong practice here, the cycle is also analyzed—thus it is said, 'Only the cycle and the escape from the cycle have been spoken of.'

Paṭipadāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Discourse on the Path is finished.

4. Vipassīsuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Vipassī Sutta

4. Vipphandantīti nimisanavasena. Animisehīti vigatanimisehi ummīlanteheva. Tena vuttaṃ mahāpadāne. Etthāti etasmiṃ “vipassī”ti pade, etasmiṃ vā “animisehī”tiādike yathāgate suttante.

4. Vipphandanti means by way of blinking. Animisehi means without blinking, as if with eyes wide open. Therefore, it is said in the Mahāpadāna. Ettha refers to this word 'Vipassī,' or in this context of the phrase 'animisehi,' etc., as it appears in the discourse.

Mahāpurisassa [M 2.0023] animisalocanato “vipassī”ti samaññāpaṭilābhassa kāraṇaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ akāraṇaṃ aññesampi mahāsattānaṃ carimabhave animisalocanattāti codanaṃ sandhāya “ettha cā”tiādiṃ vatvā tato pana aññameva kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Palāḷayamānassāti tosentassa. Anādare cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Aṭṭassāti atthassa.

The reason for the designation 'Vipassī' due to the unblinking gaze of the Great Being was stated, but since that is not the sole reason—as other Great Beings also possess an unblinking gaze in their final existence—the objection is raised with the phrase 'ettha ca,' etc. Then, to present another reason, the phrase 'apica,' etc., is stated. Palāḷayamānassa means of one who is coaxing. This is a genitive of disrespect. Aṭṭassa means of the meaning.

Puññussayasaṅkhāto bhago assa atisayena atthīti bhagavāti “bhāgyasampannassā”ti vuttaṃ. Sammāti sammadeva yāthāvato, ñāyena kāraṇenāti vuttaṃ hotīti āha “nayena hetunā”ti. Saṃ-saddo “sāma”nti iminā samānatthoti āha “sāmaṃ paccattapurisakārenā”ti, sayambhuñāṇenāti attho. Sammā, sāmaṃ bujjhi etenāti sambodho vuccati maggañāṇaṃ, “bujjhati etenā”ti katvā idha sabbaññutaññāṇassapi saṅgaho. Bodhimā satto bodhisatto, purimapade uttarapadalopo yathā “sākapatthavo”ti. Bujjhanakasattoti ettha mahābodhiyānapaṭipadāya bujjhatīti bodhi ca so sattavisesayogato satto cāti bodhisatto. Patthayamāno pavattatīti “kudāssu nāma mahantaṃ bodhiṃ pāpuṇissāmī”ti sañjātacchando paṭipajjati. Dukkhanti jātiādimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ. Kāmaṃ cutupapātāpi maraṇajātiyo, “jāyati mīyatī”ti pana vatvā “cavati upapajjatī”ti vacanaṃ na ekabhavapariyāpannānaṃ tesaṃ gahaṇaṃ, atha kho nānābhavapariyāpannānaṃ ekajjhaṃ gahaṇanti dassento āha “idaṃ…pe… vutta”nti. Tassa nissaraṇanti tassa jarāmaraṇassa nissaraṇanti vuccati. Yasmā mahāsatto jiṇṇabyādhimate disvā pabbajito, tasmāssa jarāmaraṇameva ādito upaṭṭhāsi.

Bhagavā means: 'A share (bhaga) known as an abundance of merit exists for him to an excellent degree'; thus it is said: 'of one endowed with fortune (bhāgyasampannassa).' Sammā means rightly, in accordance with reality; it means 'by a method, by a reason,' so it is said 'by a method, by a cause.' The word saṃ- has the same meaning as 'by oneself' (sāmaṃ), so it is explained as 'by oneself, by one's own personal effort'; the meaning is 'by self-originated knowledge.' Sambodho (perfect enlightenment) is so called because one awakens rightly (sammā) and by oneself (sāmaṃ) through it; it refers to the knowledge of the path. By taking it as 'one awakens through this,' the knowledge of omniscience is also included here. A being (satto) possessing enlightenment (bodhi) is a bodhisatto; there is an elision of the latter part of the first word, as in sākapatthavo. Here, 'a being who awakens' means: he is bodhi because he awakens by the practice of the path to great enlightenment, and he is a satta due to his connection with that special being; thus a bodhisatto. 'Aspiring, he proceeds' means: with his desire arisen, he practices, thinking, 'When, oh when, will I attain the great enlightenment?' Dukkha means suffering rooted in birth, etc. Granted, passing away and reappearing are also death and birth. However, having said 'is born, dies,' the statement 'passes away, reappears' is not to include those pertaining to a single existence, but rather to show the inclusion of those pertaining to various existences taken together. To show this, it is said, 'this... etc. ...is said.' 'The escape from that' is called the escape from that aging and death. Because the great being went forth after seeing the aged, the sick, and the dead, aging and death presented themselves to him from the very beginning.

Upāyamanasikārenāti [V 2.0021] upāyena vidhinā ñāyena manasikārena pathena manasikārassa pavattanato. Samāyogo ahosīti yāthāvato paṭivijjhanavasena samāgamo ahosi. Yoniso manasikārāti hetumhi nissakkavacananti tassa “yoniso manasikārenā”ti hetumhi karaṇavacanena āha. Jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇanti “kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, kiṃ paccayā jarāmaraṇa”nti jarāmaraṇe kāraṇaṃ pariggaṇhantassa bodhisattassa “yasmiṃ sati yaṃ hoti, asati ca na [M 2.0024] hoti, taṃ tassa kāraṇa”nti evaṃ abyabhicārajātikāraṇapariggaṇhanena “jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa”nti yā jarāmaraṇassa kāraṇapariggāhikā paññā uppajji, tāya uppajjantiyā cassa abhisamayo paṭivedho ahosīti attho.

'By attention to the means' (`Upāyamanasikārena`) means: because attention was applied by a means, a method, a way, a path. 'There was a connection' (`Samāyogo ahosi`) means: there was a coming together by way of penetrating in accordance with reality. 'Wise attention' (`Yoniso manasikāra`) is a definite term for a cause; for he speaks of it with an instrumental term for the cause: 'by wise attention' (`yoniso manasikārena`). 'With birth, there is aging and death' means when the Bodhisatta was investigating the cause of aging and death, thinking, 'When what exists does aging and death occur? What is the condition for aging and death?'—he understood, 'When that exists, this comes to be; with the non-existence of that, this does not come to be. That is its cause.' Through this unerring investigation of the cause, the wisdom that grasps the cause of aging and death arose in him: 'With birth as a condition, there is aging and death; aging and death are conditioned by birth.' With the arising of that wisdom, there was for him comprehension and penetration—this is the meaning.

Itīti vuttappakāraparāmasanaṃ. Hīti nipātamattaṃ. Idanti yathāvuttassa vaṭṭassa paccakkhato gahaṇaṃ. Tenāha “evamida”nti. Idha avijjāya samudayassa āgatattā “ekādasasu ṭhānesū”ti vuttaṃ. Samudayaṃ sampiṇḍetvāti saṅkhārādīnaṃ samudayaṃ ekajjhaṃ gahetvā. Anekavārañhi samudayadassanavasena ñāṇassa pavattattā “samudayo samudayo”ti āmeḍitavacanaṃ. Atha vā “evaṃ samudayo hotī”ti idaṃ na kevalaṃ nibbattidassanaparaṃ, atha kho paṭiccasamuppādasaddo viya paṭiccasamuppādamukhena idha samudayasaddo nibbattimukhena paccayattaṃ vadati. Viññāṇādayo ca yāvanto idha paccayadhammā niddiṭṭhā, te sāmaññarūpena byāpanicchāvasena gaṇhanto “samudayo samudayo”ti avoca. Tenāha “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārānaṃ samudayo hotī”ti. Dassanaṭṭhena cakkhūti samudayassa paccakkhato dassanabhāvo cakkhu. Ñātaṭṭhenāti ñātabhāvena. Pajānanaṭṭhenāti “avijjāsaṅkhārāditaṃtaṃpaccayadhammapavattiyā etassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo”ti pakārato vā jānanaṭṭhena. Paṭivedhanaṭṭhenāti “ayaṃ avijjādi paccayadhammo imassa saṅkhārādikassa paccayabhāvato samudayo”ti paṭivijjhanaṭṭhena. Obhāsanaṭṭhenāti samudayabhāvapaṭicchādakassa mohandhakārassa kilesandhakārassa vidhamanavasena avabhāsanavasena. Taṃ panetaṃ “cakkhu”ntiādinā vuttaṃ ñāṇaṃ. Nirodhavāreti paṭilomavāre. So hi “kissa nirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho”ti nirodhakittanavasena āgato.

The word `iti` is a reference to the manner already stated. The word `hi` is merely a particle. The word `idaṃ` is the direct grasping of the cycle as described. Hence he says, 'Thus this...' Here, because the arising of ignorance has been mentioned, it is said, 'in eleven instances.' 'Having summarized the arising' means having taken the arising of formations and so on together. Because knowledge proceeds by way of seeing the arising many times, the repetitive expression 'arising, arising' is used. Or, the statement 'thus is the arising' is not merely concerned with seeing the production, but rather, like the term 'dependent origination,' the term 'arising' here speaks of conditionality by way of production. And taking all the conditional phenomena pointed out here, beginning with consciousness, in a general way with the wish to encompass them, he said, 'arising, arising.' Hence he says, 'With ignorance as condition, there is the arising of formations.' The eye (`cakkhu`) has the meaning of seeing; it is the state of directly seeing the arising. Knowledge (`ñāṇa`) has the meaning of knowing; it is the state of having known. Wisdom (`paññā`) has the meaning of discerning, that is, of knowing in detail: 'Through the occurrence of these respective conditional phenomena beginning with ignorance and formations, there is the arising of this mass of suffering.' True knowledge (`vijjā`) has the meaning of penetrating, that is, of penetrating that 'this conditional phenomenon beginning with ignorance is the arising of this phenomenon beginning with formations because it is its condition.' Light (`āloko`) has the meaning of illumination, that is, by way of dispelling the darkness of delusion and the darkness of defilements that conceal the state of arising. But this is the knowledge spoken of as 'eye,' etc. The section on cessation is the reverse order. For that comes by way of reciting the cessation: 'With the cessation of what is there the cessation of aging and death?'

Vipassīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Vipassī Sutta is concluded.

5-10. Sikhīsuttādivaṇṇanā

5-10. Commentary on the Sikhī Sutta and Others

5-10. Na [V 2.0022] evaṃ yojetvāti “sikhissapī”tiādinā samuccayavasena evaṃ na yojetvā. Kasmātiādinā tattha kāraṇaṃ vadati. Ekāsane adesitattāti [M 2.0025] vuttamevatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ kātuṃ “nānāṭhānesu hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yadipi tāni visuṃ visuṃ vuttabhāvena desitāni, atthavaṇṇanā pana ekasadisā tadatthassa abhinnattā. “Buddhā jātā”ti na añño ācikkhatīti yojanā. Na hi mahābodhisattānaṃ pacchimabhave paropadesena payojanaṃ atthi. Gatamaggenevāti paṭipattigamanena gatamaggeneva pacchimamahābodhisattā gacchanti, ayamettha dhammatā. Gacchantīti catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu patiṭṭhitacittā satta bojjhaṅge yāthāvato bhāvetvā sammāsambodhiyā abhisambujjhanavasena pavattantīti attho. Yathā pana tesaṃ paṭhamavipassanābhiniveso hoti, taṃ dassetuṃ “sabbabodhisattā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Buddhabhāvānaṃ vipassanā, buddhatthāya vā vipassanā buddhavipassanā.

5-10. `Na evaṃ yojetvā` means not to be connected in this way; that is, not to be combined in this way by way of accumulation with the words “Sikhī also,” etc. With the words “Why?” etc., he states the reason. To make clear the meaning already stated—that it was not taught in a single session—the words “For in various places…” etc., are stated. Although these were taught separately, each in its own way, the explanation of the meaning is similar because its meaning is not different. The construction is: “No one else declares, ‘Buddhas are born.’” For great bodhisattas in their final existence have no need for instruction from another. “By the path already traveled” means that the great bodhisattas in their final existence proceed by the very path of practice that has been traveled; this is the fixed nature of things here. “They proceed” means that with their minds established in the four establishments of mindfulness, having developed the seven factors of enlightenment as they really are, they proceed by way of awakening to perfect self-enlightenment. To show how their initial application of insight occurs, it is said, “For all bodhisattas…” etc. Insight into the states of Buddhahood, or insight for the sake of Buddhahood, is insight for Buddhahood.

Sikhīsuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sikhī Sutta and Others is concluded.

Buddhavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Buddha Chapter is concluded.

2. Āhāravaggo

2. The Chapter on Nutriment

1. Āhārasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Nutriment Sutta

11. Āharantīti ānenti uppādenti, upatthambhentīti attho. Nibbattāti pasutā. Bhūtā nāma yasmā tato paṭṭhāya loke jātavohāro paṭisandhiggahaṇato pana paṭṭhāya yāva mātukucchito nikkhanto, tāva sambhavesino, esa tāva gabbhaseyyakesu bhūtasambhavesivibhāgo, itaresu pana paṭhamacittādivasena vutto. Sambhava-saddo cettha gabbhaseyyakānaṃ vasena pasūtipariyāyo, itaresaṃ vasena uppattipariyāyo. Paṭhamacittapaṭhamairiyāpathakkhaṇesu hi te sambhavaṃ uppattiṃ esanti upagacchanti nāma, na tāva bhūtā upapattiyā na suppatiṭṭhitattā, bhūtā eva sabbaso bhavesanāya samucchinnattā. Na puna bhavissantīti avadhāraṇena nivattitamatthaṃ dasseti. Yo ca “kālaghaso bhūto”tiādīsu bhūta-saddassa khīṇāsavavācitā daṭṭhabbā. Vā-saddo cettha sampiṇḍanattho “agginā vā udakena vā”tiādīsu viya.

11. ‘They bring’ means they bring forth, they produce, they support; this is the meaning. ‘Generated’ means born. ‘Beings’ are so called from the point at which the worldly convention of ‘born’ applies to them. But from the moment of rebirth-linking until emerging from the mother’s womb, they are ‘those seeking a new existence.’ This, for now, is the distinction between ‘beings’ and ‘those seeking a new existence’ in the case of the womb-born. For others, however, it is explained in terms of the first mind-moment, etc. Here, the word ‘existence’ (sambhava), in the case of the womb-born, is a synonym for birth; in the case of others, it is a synonym for origination. For at the moments of the first mind-moment and the first posture, they are said to be seeking or approaching a new existence, or origination; they are not yet ‘beings,’ as they are not well established in their new existence; but those for whom seeking for existence has been completely cut off are truly ‘beings.’ With the emphasis ‘they will not exist again,’ it shows the meaning of cessation. And the word ‘being’ (bhūta) in phrases such as ‘a being devoured by time’ should be seen as designating one whose taints are destroyed. The particle `vā` here has a collective sense, as in such examples as ‘by fire or by water.’

Yathāsakaṃ [V 2.0023][M 2.0026] paccayabhāvena attabhāvassa paṭhapanamevettha āhārehi kātabbaanuggaho hotīti adhippāyenāha “vacanabhedo…pe… eko yevā”ti. Sattassa uppannadhammānanti sattassa santāne uppannadhammānaṃ. Yathā “vassasataṃ tiṭṭhatī”ti vutte anuppabandhavasena pavattatīti vuttaṃ hoti, evaṃ ṭhitiyāti anuppabandhavasena pavattiyāti attho, sā pana avicchedoti āha “avicchedāyā”ti. Anuppabandhadhammuppattiyā sattasantāno anuggahito nāma hotīti āha “anuppannānaṃ uppādāyā”ti. Etānīti ṭhitianuggahapadāni. Ubhayattha daṭṭhabbāni na yathāsambandhato.

With the intention that the support to be given by nutriment here is just this—the establishment of the individual existence in accordance with its own conditions—he said: 'a distinction in speech...pe... one alone.' ‘Of the arisen states of a being’ means of the states arisen in the continuity of a being. Just as when it is said, ‘it lasts for a hundred years,’ this means that it continues in an unbroken series, so too ‘by stability’ means by continuity in an unbroken series. And that is non-severance, so he says ‘for non-severance.’ Because the continuity of a being is supported by the arising of uninterrupted states, he says ‘for the arising of the unarisen.’ ‘These’ are the terms ‘stability’ and ‘support.’ They are to be seen in both cases, not just in accordance with their grammatical connection.

Vatthugatā ojā vatthu viya tena saddhiṃ ajjhoharitabbataṃ gacchatīti vuttaṃ “ajjhoharitabbako āhāro”ti, nibbattitaojaṃ pana sandhāya “kabaḷīkāro āhāro ojaṭṭhamakarūpāni āharatī”ti vakkhati. Oḷārikatā appojatāya na vatthuno thūlatāya kathinatāya vā, tasmā yasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ parittā ojā hoti, taṃ oḷārikaṃ. Sappādayo dukkhuppādakatāya oḷārikā veditabbā. Visāṇādīnaṃ tivassachaḍḍitānaṃ pūtibhūtattā mudukatāti vadanti. Taracchakheḷatemitatāya pana tathābhūtānaṃ tesaṃ mudukatā. Dhammasabhāvo hesa. Sasānaṃ āhāro sukhumo taruṇatiṇasassakhādanato. Sakuṇānaṃ āhāro sukhumo tiṇabījādikhādanato. Paccantavāsīnaṃ āhāro sukhumo māsamuggakurādibhojanattā. Tesanti paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ. Sukhumotvevāti na kiñci upādāya, atha kho sukhumoicceva niṭṭhaṃ patto tato paramasukhumassa abhāvato.

The nutritive essence that has gone into a substance is said to ‘attain the state of being consumable along with it,’ hence it is called ‘consumable nutriment.’ But with reference to the nutritive essence that has been produced, it will be said: ‘Nutriment in the form of morsels brings forth material phenomena with nutritive essence as the eighth.’ Coarseness is due to scantiness of nutritive essence, not to the grossness or hardness of the substance. Therefore, whatever substance has little nutritive essence is coarse. Ghee and the like are to be understood as coarse because they produce discomfort. Regarding things like horns discarded for three years, they say they are soft because they have become putrid. But their softness is due to being moistened by the saliva of hyenas. This is the nature of things. The food of hares is subtle because they eat tender grass and corn. The food of birds is subtle because they eat grass seeds and the like. The food of border-dwellers is subtle because they eat meals of beans, green gram, and other grains. ‘Of them’ refers to the devas of the Paranimmitavasavattī realm. ‘Truly subtle’ means not in dependence on anything, but it has reached the culmination ‘subtle,’ because beyond that there is nothing more subtle.

Vatthuvasena panettha āhārassa oḷārikasukhumatā vuttā, sā cassa appojamahojatāhi veditabbāti dassetuṃ “ettha cā”tiādimāha. Parissayanti khudāvasena uppannaṃ vihiṃsaṃ sarīradarathaṃ. Vinodetīti vatthu tassa vinodanamattaṃ karoti. Na pana sakkoti pāletunti sarīraṃ yāpetuṃ nappahoti nirojattā. Na sakkoti parissayaṃ vinodetuṃ āmāsayassa apūraṇato.

Here, the coarseness and subtlety of nutriment have been explained in terms of the substance; and to show that this should be understood by way of its scantiness or abundance of nutritive essence, he said, “And here,” etc. ‘Danger’ means the affliction, the bodily distress, that has arisen because of hunger. ‘Dispels’ means the substance merely brings about its dispelling. ‘But it cannot protect’ means it is not able to maintain the body because it has little nutritive essence. It cannot dispel the danger because the stomach is not filled.

Chabbidhopīti iminā kassaci phassassa anavasesitabbatamāha. Desanakkamenevettha phassādīnaṃ dutiyāditā, na aññena kāraṇenāti āha “desanānayo eva cesā”tiādi. Manaso sañcetanā na [M 2.0027] sattassāti dassanatthaṃ manogahaṇaṃ yathā “cittassa ṭhiti, cetovimutti cā”ti āha “manosañcetanāti cetanāvā”ti. Cittanti yaṃ kiñci cittameva. Ekarāsiṃ katvāti ekajjhaṃ gahetvā vibhāgaṃ akatvā, sāmaññena gahitāti attho. Tattha labbhamānaṃ upādiṇṇakādivibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “kabaḷīkāro āhāro”tiādi vuttaṃ. Āhāratthaṃ na sādhentīti tādisassa [V 2.0024] āhārassa anāharaṇato. Tadāpīti bhijjitvā vigatakālepi. Upādiṇṇakāhāroti vuccantīti keci. Idaṃ pana ācariyānaṃ na ruccati tadā upādiṇṇakarūpasseva abhāvato. Paṭisandhicitteneva sahajātāti lakkhaṇavacanametaṃ, sabbāyapi kammajarūpapariyāpannāya ojāya atthibhāvassa avicchedappavattisambhavadassanattho. Sattamāti uppannadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva sattamadivasāpi. Rūpasantatiṃ pāleti paveṇighaṭanavasena. Ayamevāti kammajaojā. Kammajaojaṃ pana paṭicca uppannaojā akammajattā anupādiṇṇaāhārotveva veditabbo. Anupādiṇṇakā phassādayo veditabbāti ānetvā sambandho. Lokuttarā phassādayo kathanti āha “lokuttarā pana ruḷhīvasena kathitā”ti. Yasmā tesaṃ kusalānaṃ upetapariyāyo natthi, tasmā vipākānaṃ upādiṇṇapariyāyo natthevāti anupādiṇṇapariyāyopi ruḷhīvasena vuttoti veditabbo.

By ‘the sixfold contact,’ he indicates that no contact whatsoever is to be left out. Here, the second and subsequent places of contact, etc., are due to the order of the exposition and not to any other reason; thus he says, ‘This is just the method of exposition,’ etc. The word ‘of the mind’ is included to show that it is the volition of the mind, not of a being, just as in ‘stability of mind’ and ‘liberation of mind.’ He says, ‘Mental volition means simply volition.’ ‘Consciousness’ means any consciousness whatsoever. ‘Having made it one mass’ means having taken it all together without making a division; that is, it is taken in a general sense. To show the division found therein, such as ‘appropriated,’ etc., it is said, ‘Nutriment in the form of morsels,’ etc. ‘They do not accomplish the purpose of nutriment’ means because such nutriment is not brought forth. ‘Even then’ means even at the time when it has broken up and gone. Some say it is called ‘appropriated nutriment.’ But this is not approved by the teachers because at that time there is no appropriated matter. ‘Born together with the rebirth-linking consciousness’ is a statement of a characteristic, meant to show the possibility of the uninterrupted continuity of the existence of all nutritive essence included in kamma-generated matter. ‘Seventh’ means from the day of arising up to the seventh day. ‘It maintains the continuity of matter’ by way of connecting the lineage. ‘This very one’ means the kamma-generated nutritive essence. But the nutritive essence that arises in dependence on kamma-generated nutritive essence, being non-kamma-generated, should be understood as ‘unappropriated nutriment.’ The connection should be brought in thus: ‘The unappropriated contacts, etc., should be understood.’ Regarding the supramundane contacts, etc., it is said: ‘But the supramundane are spoken of by convention.’ Since for those wholesome states there is no category of ‘associated,’ therefore for their resultants there is no category of ‘appropriated’ either. Thus it should be understood that the category of ‘unappropriated’ is also spoken of by convention.

Pubbe “āhārāti paccayā”ti vuttattā yadi paccayaṭṭho āhāraṭṭhotiādinā codeti, atha kasmā ime eva cattāro vuttāti atha kasmā cattārova vuttā. Ime eva ca vuttāti yojanā. Visesappaccayattāti etena yathā aññe paccayadhammā attano paccayuppannassa paccayāva honti, ime pana tathā ca hoti aññathā cāti samānepi paccayatte atirekapaccayā honti, tasmā “āhārāti vuttā”ti imamatthaṃ dasseti. Idāni taṃ atirekapaccayataṃ dassetuṃ “visesapaccayo hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Visesappaccayo rūpakāyassa kabaḷīkāro āhāro upathambhakabhāvato. Tenāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “rūpārūpānaṃ upathambhakattena upakārakā cattāro āhārā āhārapaccayo”ti (visuddhi. 2.608; paṭṭhā. aṭṭha. paccayuddesavaṇṇanā). Upathambhakattañhi satīpi janakatte arūpīnaṃ āhārānaṃ āhārajarūpasamuṭṭhānakarūpāhārassa [M 2.0028] ca hoti, asati pana upathambhakatte āhārānaṃ janakattaṃ natthīti upathambhakattaṃ padhānaṃ. Janayamānopi hi āhāro avicchedavasena upathambhayamāno eva janetīti upathambhakabhāvo eva āhārabhāvo. Vedanāya phasso visesapaccayo. “Phassapaccayā vedanā”ti hi vuttaṃ. “Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”nti vacanato viññāṇassa manosañcetanā. “Cetanā tividhaṃ bhavaṃ janetī”ti hi vuttaṃ. “Viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa”nti pana vacanato nāmarūpassa viññāṇaṃ visesapaccayo. Na hi okkantaviññāṇābhāve nāmarūpassa atthi sambhavo. Yathāha “viññāṇañca hi, ānanda, mātukucchismiṃ na okkamissatha, api nu kho nāmarūpaṃ mātukucchismiṃ samuccissathā”tiādi (dī. ni. 2.115). Vuttamevatthaṃ suttena sādhetuṃ “yathāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Since it was stated earlier, 'Nutriments are conditions,' one might object, 'If the meaning of condition is the meaning of nutriment, then why are only these four mentioned?' The construction is: 'And why are only these four mentioned? These alone are mentioned.' It is because they are special conditions. By this it is shown that while other conditional states are merely conditions for their own conditionally arisen phenomena, these are so in that way and also otherwise. Thus, although they are similar in being conditions, they are pre-eminent conditions, and this shows why they are called 'nutriments.' Now, to show that special conditionality, it is said, 'For it is a special condition,' and so on. Physical nutriment is a special condition for the material body because of its supporting nature. Hence it is said in the commentary: 'The four nutriments are the nutriment condition because they are helpful by way of supporting material and immaterial phenomena' (Vism 2.608; Paṭṭh-a). For the act of supporting, even when there is also generation, belongs to the immaterial nutriments and to the material nutriment which is the origin of nutriment-born matter. But when there is no supporting, there is no generation by the nutriments, so supporting is the principal factor. For even while generating, a nutriment generates only by supporting in an uninterrupted manner; thus, the state of supporting is the state of being a nutriment. Contact is a special condition for feeling, for it is said: 'With contact as condition, feeling comes to be.' On the authority of the text, 'With formations as condition, consciousness comes to be,' mental volition is a special condition for consciousness. For it is said: 'Volition generates the three kinds of existence.' And on the authority of the text, 'With consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be,' consciousness is a special condition for name-and-form. For if consciousness did not descend, there would be no possibility for the arising of name-and-form. As it is said: 'And if, Ānanda, consciousness were not to descend into the mother’s womb, would name-and-form then coalesce in the mother’s womb?' (DN 15). To confirm the meaning just stated with a sutta, it is said, 'As it is said,' and so on.

Evaṃ yadipi paccayattho āhārattho, visesapaccayattā pana imeva āhārāti vuttāti taṃ nesaṃ [V 2.0025] visesapaccayataṃ avibhāgato dassetvā idāni vibhāgato dassetuṃ “ko panetthā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Mukhe ṭhapitamatto eva asaṅkhādito, tattakenāpi abbhantarassa āhārassa paccayo hoti eva. Tenāha “aṭṭha rūpāni samuṭṭhāpetī”ti. Sukhavedanāya hito sukhavedanīyo. Sabbathāpīti cakkhusamphassādivasena. Yattakā phassassa pakārabhedā, tesaṃ vasena sabbappakāropi phassāhāro yathārahaṃ tisso vedanā āharati, anāhārako natthi.

Thus, although the meaning of condition is the meaning of nutriment, it is because they are special conditions that these alone are called 'nutriments.' Having thus shown their special conditionality without distinction, now, to show it with distinctions, the passage beginning 'But what here?' is introduced. Merely placed in the mouth, not yet chewed, even by that much it becomes a condition for the internal nutriment. Therefore it is said: 'It originates eight kinds of material phenomena.' That which is beneficial for pleasant feeling is productive of pleasant feeling. In every way: by way of eye-contact and so on. However many kinds of contact there are, by way of these, the nutriment of contact in all its varieties brings forth the three feelings as is appropriate. There is no contact that is not a nutriment.

Sabbathāpīti idhāpi phassāhāre vuttanayānusārena attho veditabbo. Tisantativasenāti kāyadasakaṃ bhāvadasakaṃ vatthudasakanti tividhasantativasena. Sahajātādipaccayanayenāti sahajātādipaccayavidhinā. Paṭisandhiviññāṇañhi attanā sahajātanāmassa sahajātaaññamaññavipākindriyasampayuttaatthiavigatapaccayehi paccayo hontoyeva āhārapaccayatāya taṃ āhāreti vuttaṃ, sahajātarūpesu pana vatthuno sampayuttapaccayaṃ ṭhapetvā vippayuttapaccayena, sesarūpānaṃ aññamaññapaccayañca ṭhapetvā itaresaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena yojanā kātabbā. Tānīti napuṃsakaniddeso anapuṃsakānampi napuṃsakehi saha vacanato. Sāsavakusalākusalacetanāva vuttā visesapaccayabhāvadassanaṃ hetanti, tenāha “avisesena panā”tiādi. Paṭisandhiviññāṇameva vuttanti etthāpi [M 2.0029] eseva nayo. Yathā tassa tassa phalassa visesato paccayatāya etesaṃ āhārattho, evaṃ avisesatopīti dassetuṃ “avisesenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha taṃsampayuttataṃsamuṭṭhānadhammānanti tehi phassādīhi sampayuttadhammānañceva taṃsamuṭṭhānarūpadhammānañca. Tattha sampayuttaggahaṇaṃ yathārahato daṭṭhabbaṃ, samuṭṭhānaggahaṇaṃ pana avisesato.

In every way: Here too the meaning should be understood according to the method stated in connection with the nutriment of contact. By the threefold continuity: by way of the threefold continuity of the body-decad, the sex-decad, and the heart-base decad. By the way of conditions such as conascence: by the method of conditions such as conascence. For rebirth-linking consciousness, while being a condition for the name conascent with it by way of conascence, mutuality, result, faculty, association, presence, and non-disappearance conditions, is said to nourish it by way of the nutriment condition. But in the case of conascent materiality, for the base, the connection is by way of the dissociated condition, setting aside the associated condition; for the remaining material phenomena, setting aside the mutuality condition, the connection should be made by way of the other conditions. The neuter designation 'those' (tāni) is used because even non-neuter things are referred to along with neuter things. Only wholesome and unwholesome volitions accompanied by taints are mentioned, the reason being to show their status as special conditions; hence it is said: 'But in a general sense,' etc. Here too, where only rebirth-linking consciousness is mentioned, this same method applies. To show that just as the meaning of nutriment applies to these in a special sense because of their being conditions for their respective results, so it applies in a general sense too, it is said, 'But in a general sense,' etc. Therein, 'for the states associated with them and originated from them' means for the mental states associated with that contact, etc., and for the material phenomena originated from them. Therein, the taking of 'associated' should be understood as is appropriate, but the taking of 'originated' is without distinction.

Upatthambhento āhārakiccaṃ sādhetīti upatthambhento eva rūpaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti, ojaṭṭhamakasamuṭṭhāpaneneva panassa upathambhanakiccasiddhi. Phusantoyevāti phusanakiccaṃ karonto eva. Āyūhamānāvāti cetayamānā eva abhisandahantī eva. Vijānantamevāti upapattiparikappanavasena vijānantameva āhārakiccaṃ sādhetīti yojanā. Sabbattha āhārakiccasādhanañca tesaṃ vedanādiuppattihetutāya attabhāvassa pavattanameva. Kāyaṭṭhapanenāti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu kammajādirūpaṃ kammādināva pavattatīti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “kammajanitopī”tiādi.

'By supporting, it accomplishes the function of nutriment' means that it is by supporting that it originates materiality. And its function of supporting is accomplished precisely by originating the nutritive-essence-octad. 'By touching' means by performing the function of touching. 'By accumulating' means by intending and preparing. 'By knowing': the construction is that it accomplishes the function of nutriment by way of knowing through construing rebirth. And in all cases, the accomplishment of the function of nutriment is simply the continuation of the individual existence, since they are the cause for the arising of feeling and so on. Why is it said, 'by establishing the body'? In reference to the objection, 'Is it not the case that materiality born of kamma, etc., continues through kamma, etc.?' it is said, 'Even though generated by kamma,' etc.

Upādiṇṇarūpasantatiyā upatthambhaneneva utucittajarūpasantatīnampi upatthambhanasiddhi hotīti “dvinnaṃ rūpasantatīna”nti vuttaṃ. Upatthambhanameva sandhāya “anupālako hutvā”ti ca vuttaṃ. Rūpakāyassa ṭhitihetutā hi yāpanā anupālanā. Sukhādivatthubhūtanti sukhādīnaṃ pavattiṭṭhānabhūtaṃ. Ārammaṇampi hi vasati ettha ārammaṇakaraṇavasena tadārammaṇā dhammāti vatthūti [V 2.0026] vuccati. Phusantoyevāti idaṃ phassassa phusanasabhāvattā vuttaṃ. Na hi dhammānaṃ sabhāvena vinā pavatti atthi, vedanāpavattiyā vinā sattānaṃ sandhāvanatā natthīti āha “sukhādi…pe… hotī”ti. Na cettha saññībhavakathāyaṃ asaññībhavo dassetabbo, tassāpi vā kāraṇabhūtavedanāpavattivaseneva ṭhitiyā hetuno abyāpitattā, tathā hi “manosañcetanā…pe… bhavamūlanipphādanato sattānaṃ ṭhitiyā hotī”ti vuttā. Tato eva viññāṇaṃ vijānantamevāti upapattiparikappanavasena vijānantamevāti vuttovāyamattho.

It is by the supporting of the appropriated material continuity that the support of the material continuities born of temperature and mind is also accomplished; hence it is said, 'of the two material continuities.' And it is with reference to this supporting that it is said, 'by becoming a sustainer.' For being the cause of the stability of the material body is maintenance (yāpanā), sustaining (anupālanā). 'Serving as the basis for pleasure, etc.' means being the ground for the occurrence of pleasure and so on. For even an object is called a 'basis' (vatthu) because states having that as their object 'dwell' (vasati) in it by way of making it an object. 'By touching': this is said because touching is the intrinsic nature of contact. For there is no occurrence of states without their intrinsic nature. And without the occurrence of feeling, there is no transmigrating for beings; thus it is said: 'for pleasure, etc. ... it is.' And here, in the discussion of existence with perception, existence without perception should not be shown, for in its case too, the cause for its stability is not encompassed by the reason given, namely, by way of the occurrence of feeling that is its condition. For thus it is said: 'Mental volition... by producing the root of existence, is for the stability of beings.' For that very reason, 'consciousness by knowing' means by knowing through construing rebirth. This meaning has been stated.

Cattāri bhayāni daṭṭhabbāni ādīnavavibhāvanato. Nikantīti nikāmanā, rasataṇhaṃ sandhāya vadati. Sā hi kabaḷīkāre āhāre balavatī, tenevettha avadhāraṇaṃ kataṃ. Bhāyati etasmāti bhayaṃ, nikantiyeva [M 2.0030] bhayaṃ mahānatthahetuto. Upagamanaṃ visayindriyaviññāṇesu visayaviññāṇesu ca saṅgativasena pavatti, taṃ vedanādiuppattihetutāya “bhaya”nti vuttaṃ. Avadhāraṇe payojanaṃ vuttanayameva. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo. Āyūhanaṃ abhisandahanaṃ, saṃvidhānantipi vadanti. Taṃ bhavūpapattihetutāya “bhaya”nti vuttaṃ. Abhinipāto tattha tattha bhave paṭisandhiggahaṇavasena viññāṇassa nibbatti. So bhavūpapattihetukānaṃ sabbesaṃ anatthānaṃ mūlakāraṇatāya “bhaya”nti vuttaṃ. Idāni nikantiādīnaṃ sappaṭibhayataṃ vitthārato dassetuṃ “kiṃ kāraṇā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha nikantiṃ katvāti ālayaṃ janetvā, taṇhaṃ uppādetvāti attho. Sītādīnaṃ purakkhatāti sītādīnaṃ purato ṭhitā, sītādīhi bādhiyamānāti attho.

Four fears are to be seen by way of showing the danger. 'Delight' (nikanti) is longing (nikāmanā); this is said with reference to craving for tastes. For this is strong in the case of physical nutriment; hence the emphasis is made here. One fears it, thus it is a 'fear' (bhaya). Delight itself is a fear because it is a cause of great harm. 'Approach' (upagamanaṃ) is the occurrence by way of contact in relation to sense objects and consciousnesses. Because it is a cause for the arising of feeling, etc., it is called a 'fear.' The purpose of the emphasis is in the way already stated. This same method applies to the remaining two as well. 'Accumulation' (āyūhanaṃ) is preparing (abhisandahanaṃ); they also say it is arranging (saṃvidhānaṃ). Because it is a cause for existence and rebirth, it is called a 'fear.' 'Plunging down' (abhinipāto) is the generation of consciousness by way of taking rebirth-linking in different kinds of existence. Because it is the root cause of all calamities that are caused by existence and rebirth, it is called a 'fear.' Now, to show in detail how delight and so on are fraught with fear, the passage beginning 'For what reason?' is introduced. Therein, 'having formed a delight' means having generated an attachment, having produced craving; this is the meaning. 'Exposed to cold, etc.' means standing in front of cold, etc., that is, being afflicted by cold, etc.

Phassaṃ upagacchantāti cakkhusamphassādibhedaṃ phassaṃ pavattentā. Phassassādinoti kāyasamphassavasena phoṭṭhabbasaṅkhātassa assādanasīlā. Kāyasamphassavasena hi sattānaṃ phoṭṭhabbataṇhā pavattatīti dassetuṃ phassāhārādīnavadassane phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ uddhaṭaṃ “paresaṃ rakkhitagopitesū”tiādinā. Phassassādinoti vā phassāhārassādinoti attho. Sati hi phassāhāre sattānaṃ phassārammaṇe assādo, nāsati, tenāha “phassassādamūlaka”ntiādi.

'Approaching contact' means engaging in contact of various kinds, such as eye-contact. 'Savoring contact' means being disposed to savoring what is called the tangible by way of bodily contact. To show that for beings craving for tangibles occurs by way of bodily contact, in the exposition of the danger of the nutriment of contact, the tangible object is cited with the words 'in what is guarded and protected by others,' etc. Or 'savoring contact' means savoring the nutriment of contact. For when the nutriment of contact exists, beings find savor in the object of contact; when it does not exist, they do not. Hence it is said, 'rooted in the savoring of contact,' etc.

Jātinimittassa bhayassa abhinipātasabhāvena gahitattā “tammūlaka”nti vuttaṃ. Kammāyūhananimittanti attho. Bhayaṃ sabbanti pañcavīsati, tividhamahābhayaṃ, aññañca sabbabhayaṃ āgatameva hoti bhayādhiṭṭhānassa attabhāvassa nipphādanato.

Because the fear that is the sign of birth has been taken as having the nature of plunging down, it is said to be 'rooted in that.' The meaning is: the sign of the accumulation of kamma. All fear—the twenty-five fears, the three great fears, and all other fear—is included because the individual existence, which is the basis for fear, is produced.

Abhinipatatīti abhinibbattati. Paṭhamābhinibbatti hi sattānaṃ tattha tattha aṅgārakāsusadise [V 2.0027] bhave abhinipātasadisī. Tammūlakattāti nāmarūpanibbattimūlakattā. Sabbabhayānaṃ abhinipātoyeva bhayaṃ bhāyati etasmāti katvā.

It plunges means it is reborn. The first rebirth of beings in existences resembling a pit of embers is like plunging. Because it is rooted in that means because it is rooted in the arising of name-and-form. The very plunging into all fears is a fear, because one fears it.

Appeti viyāti phalassa attalābhahetubhāvato kāraṇaṃ, taṃ niyyādeti viya. Tanti phalaṃ. Tatoti kāraṇato. Etesanti āhārānaṃ[M 2.0031]. Yathāvuttenāti “phalaṃ nidetī”tiādinā vuttappakārena atthena. Sabbapadesūti “vedanānirodhenā”tiādīsu sabbesu padesu.

As if it delivers: the cause, because it is the cause for the fruit's attainment of its own state, is as if it delivers it. 'It' (taṃ) means the fruit. 'From that' (tato) means from the cause. 'Of these' (etesaṃ) means of these nutriments. 'In the way stated' means with the meaning in the manner stated, such as 'it indicates the fruit,' etc. 'In all instances' means in all instances, such as 'with the cessation of feeling,' etc.

Paṭisandhiṃ ādiṃ katvāti paṭisandhikkhaṇaṃ ādiṃ katvā. Upādiṇṇakaāhāre sandhāya “attabhāvasaṅkhātānaṃ āhārāna”nti vuttaṃ. Te hi nippariyāyato taṇhānidānā. Paripuṇṇāyatanānaṃ sattānaṃ sattasantativasenāti paripuṇṇāyatanānaṃ sabhāvakānaṃ cakkhu sotaṃ ghānaṃ jivhā kāyo bhāvo vatthūti imesaṃ sattannaṃ santatīnaṃ vasena. Sesānaṃ aparipuṇṇāyatanānaṃ andhabadhiraabhāvakānaṃ. Ūnaūnasantativasenāti cakkhunā, sotena, tadubhayena, bhāvena ca ūnaūnasantativasena. Paṭisandhiyaṃ jātā paṭisandhikā. Paṭhamabhavaṅgacittakkhaṇādīti ādi-saddena tadārammaṇacittassa saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo.

`Taking rebirth as the beginning` means taking the moment of rebirth-linking as the beginning. With reference to nutriment derived from clinging, it is said: 'of the nutriments designated as individual existence.' For these, in the absolute sense, have craving as their source. `For beings with complete sense bases, by way of the sevenfold continuity` means: for those who are naturally endowed with complete sense bases, by way of the continuity of these seven: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, sex, and physical basis. For the rest, those with incomplete sense bases—the blind, deaf, and those without the sex faculty. `By way of a deficient continuity` means by way of a continuity deficient in the eye, the ear, both of them, or the sex faculty. What has arisen at rebirth-linking is 'of rebirth-linking.' `From the first life-continuum moment, etc.` means: by the word 'etc.' the inclusion of the registration consciousness should be understood.

Taṇhāyapi nidānaṃ jānātīti yojanā. Taṇhānidānantipi pāṭho. Vaṭṭaṃ dassetvāti sarūpato nayato ca sakalameva vaṭṭaṃ dassetvā. Idāni tamatthaṃ vitthārato vibhāvetuṃ “imasmiñca pana ṭhāne”tiādimāha. Atītābhimukhaṃ desanaṃ katvāti paccuppannabhavato paṭṭhāya atītadhammābhimukhaṃ tabbisayaṃ desanaṃ katvā tathākāraṇena. Atītena vaṭṭaṃ dassetīti atītabhavena kammakilesavipākavaṭṭaṃ dasseti. Attabhāvoti paccuppanno attabhāvo. Yadi evaṃ kasmā “atītena vaṭṭaṃ dassetī”ti vuttanti? Nāyaṃ doso “atītenevā”ti anavadhāraṇato, evañca katvā atītābhimukhaggahaṇaṃ janakakammaṃ gahitaṃ, taṇhāsīsena nānantariyabhāvato. Na hi kammunā vinā taṇhā bhavanetti yujjati.

The connection is: 'He understands the cause of craving too.' There is also the reading 'the cause of craving.' `Having shown the round` means: having shown the entire round both in its own nature and by its method. Now, to explain that meaning in detail, he says, 'And in this case,' etc. `Having given a teaching directed towards the past` means: having given a teaching that, starting from the present existence, is directed towards past phenomena, having them as its object, for that reason. `He shows the round by means of the past` means: he shows the round of kamma, defilements, and results by means of past existence. `Individual existence` means the present individual existence. If so, why is it said, 'he shows the round by means of the past'? This is not a fault, because there is no restriction to 'only by the past.' And thus, by taking up what is directed towards the past, the generative kamma is included, because it is not immediately subsequent to craving as its head. For without kamma, it is not fitting that craving should be the guide to existence.

Taṃ kammanti taṇhāsīsena vuttakammaṃ. Dassetunti taṃ atītaṃ attabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ. Tassattabhāvassa janakaṃ kammanti tassa yathāvuttassa attabhāvassa janakaṃ. Tato parampi attabhāvaṃ āyūhitaṃ kammaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Avijjā ca nāma taṇhā viya kammattāti kammasseva gahaṇaṃ. Dvīsu ṭhānesūti āhāraggahaṇena vedanādiggahaṇenāti dvīsu ṭhānesu. Attabhāvoti paccuppannakāliko atītakāliko ca attabhāvo. Puna dvīsūti taṇhāggahaṇe avijjāsaṅkhāraggahaṇeti dvīsu ṭhānesu. Tassa janakanti paccuppannassa ceva atītassa ca attabhāvassa [V 2.0028] janakaṃ kammaṃ vuttanti yojanā[M 2.0032]. Kammaggahaṇena cettha yattha taṃ kammaṃ āyūhitaṃ, sā atītā jāti atthato dassitā hoti. Tena saṃsāravaṭṭassa anamataggataṃ dīpeti. Saṅkhepenāti saṅkhepena hetupañcakaphalapañcakaggahaṇampi hi saṅkhepo eva hetuphalabhāvena saṅgahetabbadhammānaṃ anekavidhattā.

`That kamma` means the kamma spoken of as headed by craving. `To show` means to show that past individual existence. `The kamma that generates that individual existence` means the generator of that aforesaid individual existence. It is also said in order to show the kamma accumulated for a future individual existence. And ignorance, like craving, because of its nature as kamma, is included by the taking up of kamma itself. `In two instances` means in two instances: by the taking up of nutriment and by the taking up of feeling, etc. `Individual existence` means individual existence that is present and past. `Again in two` means in two instances: in the taking up of craving and in the taking up of ignorance and formations. `Its generator` means the kamma that generates both the present and the past individual existence is spoken of; this is the connection. And here, by the taking up of kamma, that past birth where that kamma was accumulated is shown in meaning. Thereby he illuminates the beginninglessness of the round of saṃsāra. `In brief` means: for even the taking up of the five causes and five results in brief is indeed a summary, because the phenomena to be included under the cause-and-effect relation are of many kinds.

Yadi atītena vaṭṭaṃ dassitaṃ, evaṃ sati sappadesā paṭiccasamuppādadhammadesanā hotīti dassento “tatrāya”ntiādimāha. Tena hi yadipi sarūpato anāgatena vaṭṭaṃ idha na dassitaṃ, nayato pana tassapi dassitattā nippadesā eva paṭiccasamuppādadesanāti dasseti. Idāni tamatthaṃ upamāya vibhāvetuṃ “yathā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Udakapiṭṭhe nipannanti udakaṃ pariplavavasena nipannaṃ. Parabhāganti parauttamaṅgabhāgaṃ. Oratoti tato aparabhāgato olokento. Aparipuṇṇoti vikalāvayavo. Evaṃsampadantiādi upamāya saṃsandanaṃ.

Showing that if the round was shown by means of the past, the teaching on the Dhamma of dependent origination would be partial, he says, 'In that case, this…,' etc. He shows that although the round by means of the future was not shown here in its own nature, since it was shown by method, the teaching on dependent origination is indeed complete. Now, to clarify that meaning with a simile, it is said, 'Just as…,' etc. `Lying on the surface of the water` means lying there by way of floating on the water. `The other part` means the other, upper part. `From below` means looking from the lower part. `Incomplete` means with defective limbs. `Thus connected, etc.` means the connection with the simile.

Yathā hi gīvā sarīrasandhārakakaṇḍarānaṃ mūlaṭṭhānabhūtā, evaṃ attabhāvasandhārakānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ mūlabhūtā taṇhāti vuttaṃ “gīvāya diṭṭhakālo”ti. Yathā vedanādianekāvayavasamudāyabhūto attabhāvo, evaṃ phāsukapiṭṭhikaṇḍakādianekāvayavasamudāyabhūtā piṭṭhīti “piṭṭhiyā…pe… tassa diṭṭhakālo”ti vuttaṃ. Taṇhāsaṅkhātanti taṇhāya kathitaṃ. Idha desanāya paccayā avijjāsaṅkhārā veditabbāti “naṅguṭṭhamūlassa diṭṭhakālo viyā”ti vuttaṃ. Tathā hi pariyosāne “naṅguṭṭhamūlaṃ passeyyā”ti upamādassanaṃ kataṃ. Nayato paripuṇṇabhāvaggahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ anāgatassāpi paccayavaṭṭassa hetuvasena phalavasena vā paripuṇṇabhāvassa mukhamattadassanīyattā ādito phalahetusandhi, majjhe hetuphalasandhi, antepi phalahetusandhīti evaṃ tisandhikattā catusaṅkhepameva vaṭṭaṃ dassitanti.

Just as the neck is the root-place of the tendons that hold the body together, so craving is the root of the formations that sustain individual existence; thus it is said: 'the time of seeing the neck.' Just as individual existence is a collection of many parts such as feeling, so the back is a collection of many parts such as the ribs, the spine, etc.; thus it is said: 'the time of seeing the back…of that.' `Designated as craving` means spoken of as craving. `Like the time of seeing the root of the tail` is said because here in this teaching, ignorance and formations are to be understood as the conditions. For at the conclusion the showing of the simile is made: 'one would see the root of the tail.' The taking up of its completeness should be understood by way of the method. Because in the Pāli text, concerning the future round of conditions too, only a mere outline of its completeness is shown, whether by way of cause or by way of result, there is a result-cause connection at the beginning, a cause-result connection in the middle, and a result-cause connection at the end too. Thus, having three connections, the round is shown with four sections.

Āhārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Āhārasutta is finished.

2. Moḷiyaphaggunasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Moḷiyaphagguna Sutta

12. Imasmiṃyeva ṭhāneti “cattārome bhikkhu…pe… āhārā”ti evaṃ cattāro āhāre sarūpato dassetvā “ime kho bhikkhave…pe… anuggahāyā”ti nigamanavasena dassite imasmiṃyeva ṭhāne. Desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi [M 2.0033] catuāhāravibhāgadīpakaṃ desanaṃ uddesavaseneva niṭṭhāpesi, upari āvajjetvā tuṇhī nisīdi. Diṭṭhigatikoti attadiṭṭhivasena diṭṭhigatiko. Varagandhavāsitanti sabhāvasiddhena candanagandhena ceva tadaññanānāgandhena ca paribhāvitattā varagandhavāsitaṃ[V 2.0029]. Ratanacaṅkoṭavarenāti ratanamayena uttamacaṅkoṭakena. Desanānusandhiṃ ghaṭentoti yathādesitāya desanāya anusandhiṃ ghaṭento, yathā uparidesanā vaddheyya, evaṃ ussāhaṃ karonto. Viññāṇāhāraṃ āhāretīti tassa āhāraṇakiriyāya vuttapucchāya taṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppāṭento “yo etaṃ…pe… bhuñjati vā”ti āha.

12. `In this very place` means: in this very place where the four nutriments were shown—first in their own nature with the words, “These four, bhikkhus … are nutriments,” and then by way of a conclusion with the words, “These, bhikkhus … are for support.” `He concluded the teaching` means: He concluded the teaching that illuminates the analysis of the four nutriments by way of a summary statement alone; having adverted to what was to follow, he sat down in silence. `One holding a view` means: one holding a view by way of a view of self. `Scented with the finest fragrance` means: perfumed with the naturally arisen fragrance of sandalwood and various other fragrances. `With a superior jeweled casket` means: with an excellent casket made of jewels. `Connecting the sequence of the teaching` means: connecting the sequence of the teaching as it was delivered, making an effort so that the teaching to follow would be elaborated. `‘He partakes of the nutriment of consciousness’`: In response to the question asked about the act of partaking, uprooting that wrong view, he said: “Whoever … eats or partakes.”

Viññāṇāhāre nāma icchite tassa upabhuñjakenapi bhavitabbaṃ, so “ko nu kho”ti ayaṃ pucchāya adhippāyo. Utusamayeti gabbhavuṭṭhānasamaye. So hi utusamayassa mattakasamayattā tathā vutto. “Udakena aṇḍāni mā nassantū”ti mahāsamuddato nikkhamitvā. Gijjhapotakā viya āhārasañcetanāya tāni kacchapaṇḍāni manosañcetanāhārena yāpentīti ayaṃ tassa therassa laddhi. Kiñcāpi ayaṃ laddhīti phassamanosañcetanāhāresu kiñcāpi therassa yuttā ayuttā vā ayaṃ laddhi. Imaṃ pañhanti “ko nu kho, bhante, viññāṇāhāraṃ āhāretī”ti imaṃ pañhaṃ etāya yathāvuttāya laddhiyā na pana pucchati, atha kho sattupaladdhiyā pucchatīti adhippāyo. Soti diṭṭhigatiko. Na niggahetabbo ummattakasadisattā adhippāyaṃ ajānitvā pucchāya katattā. Tenāha “āhāretīti nāhaṃ vadāmī”tiādi.

When the nutriment of consciousness is desired, there must be one who partakes of it; this is the intention of the question, 'Who, now?' `At the proper time` means: at the time of emerging from the womb. It is called thus because that season is a limited time. Having come out of the great ocean with the thought, ‘May the eggs not be destroyed by the water.’ Just as young vultures are sustained by the intention for food, so those turtle eggs are sustained by the nutriment of mental volition; this is that elder’s theory. `Although this is the theory` means: although this theory of the elder concerning the nutriments of contact and mental volition is appropriate or inappropriate. `This question` means: the intention is that he does not ask this question—‘Who, venerable sir, partakes of the nutriment of consciousness?’—based on this aforesaid theory, but he asks it based on the assumption of a being. `He` means: the one holding a view. He should not be rebuked because he is like a madman, having asked the question without knowing the intention. Therefore He said: ‘I do not say, “partakes,”’ and so on.

Tasmiṃ mayā evaṃ vutteti tasmiṃ vacane mayā “āhāretī”ti evaṃ vutte sati. Ayaṃ pañhoti “ko nu kho, bhante, viññāṇāhāraṃ āhāretī”ti ayaṃ pañho yutto bhaveyya. Evaṃ pucchite pañheti sattupaladdhiṃ anādāya “katamassa dhammassa paccayo”ti evaṃ dhammapavattavaseneva pañhe pucchite. Teneva viññāṇenāti teneva paṭisandhiviññāṇena saha uppannaṃ nāmañca rūpañca atītabhave diṭṭhigatikassa vasena āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattīti idhādhippetaṃ. Nāmarūpe jāte satīti nāmarūpe nibbatte tappaccayabhūtaṃ bhinditvā saḷāyatanaṃ hoti.

‘When I have said this’ means: when I have said in that statement, ‘partakes.’ ‘This question’ means the question, ‘Who, venerable sir, partakes of the nutriment of consciousness?’ would be proper. ‘When the question is asked thus’ means: when the question is asked without assuming a being, solely in terms of the process of phenomena, thus: ‘For what phenomenon is what a condition?’ ‘By that very consciousness’ means: it is intended here that by that very rebirth-linking consciousness, along with the mentality-and-materiality that has arisen with it, there is the generation of a new existence in the future on account of one holding a particular view in a past existence. ‘When mentality-and-materiality has arisen’ means: when mentality-and-materiality has been generated, the sixfold sense base comes to be, conditioned by it.

Tatrāyaṃ paccayavibhāgo – nāmanti vedanādikhandhattayaṃ idhādhippetaṃ, rūpaṃ pana sattasantatipariyāpannaṃ, niyamato cattāri bhūtāni cha vatthūni jīvitindriyaṃ [M 2.0034] āhāro ca. Tattha vipākanāmaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe hadayavatthuno sahāyo hutvā chaṭṭhassa manāyatanassa sahajātaaññamaññanissayasampayuttavipākaatthiavigatapaccayehi sattadhā paccayo hoti. Kiñci panettha hetupaccayena kiñci āhārapaccayenāti evaṃ ukkaṃsāvakaṃso veditabbo. Itaresaṃ pana pañcāyatanānaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ sahāyo hutvā sahajātanissayavipākavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena chadhā paccayo hoti. Kiñci panettha hetupaccayena kiñci āhārapaccayenāti sabbaṃ purimasadisaṃ. Pavatte vipākanāmaṃ vipākassa chaṭṭhāyatanassa vuttanayena sattadhā [V 2.0030] paccayo hoti, avipākaṃ pana avipākassa chaṭṭhassa tato vipākapaccayaṃ apanetvā paccayo hoti. Cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ pana paccuppannaṃ cakkhupasādādivatthukampi itarampi vipākanāmaṃ pacchājātavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayehi catudhā paccayo hoti, tathā avipākampi veditabbaṃ. Rūpato pana vatthurūpaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ chaṭṭhassa sahajātaaññamaññanissayavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayehi chadhā paccayo hoti. Cattāri pana bhūtāni cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ sahajātanissayaatthiavigatapaccayehi catudhā paccayo hoti. Rūpajīvitaṃ atthiavigatindriyavasena tidhā paccayo hotīti ayañhettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana visuddhimaggato (visuddhi. 2.594) gahetabbo.

Herein, this is the analysis of conditions. Mentality: this is here intended as the three aggregates beginning with feeling. Materiality, however, is what is included in the continuity of a being, specifically, the four great elements, the six physical bases, the life faculty, and nutriment. Therein, at the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant mentality, being an assistant to the heart-base, is a condition in seven ways for the sixth, the mind base, by way of conascence, mutuality, support, association, result, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. It should be understood that here something is by root condition and something by nutriment condition; thus there is inclusion and omission. For the other five sense bases, however, being an assistant to the four great elements, it is a condition in six ways by way of conascence, support, result, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. Here too, something is by root condition and something by nutriment condition—all is similar to the preceding. In the course of existence, resultant mentality is a condition in seven ways for the resultant sixth sense base in the way stated. Non-resultant mentality, however, is a condition for the non-resultant sixth base, after removing from that the result condition. For the eye base and so on, resultant mentality is a condition in four ways—by postnascence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance—for present materiality (both that with the eye sensitivity etc. as its physical basis and other kinds); the same should be understood for non-resultant mentality. From the side of materiality, the physical basis-materiality at rebirth-linking is a condition in six ways for the sixth sense base by way of conascence, mutuality, support, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The four great elements, however, are a condition in four ways for the five sense bases by way of conascence, support, presence, and non-disappearance. The material life faculty is a condition in three ways by way of presence, non-disappearance, and faculty. This is the summary here; the detailed account, however, should be understood from the Visuddhimagga (Vism. 2.594).

Pañhassa okāsaṃ dentoti “ko nu kho, bhante, phusatī”ti imassa diṭṭhigatikapañhassa okāsaṃ dento. Tato vivecetukāmoti adhippāyo. Sabbapadesūti diṭṭhigatikena bhagavatā ca vuttapadesu. Sattoti attā. So pana ucchedavādinopi yāva na ucchijjati, tāva atthevāti laddhi, pageva sassatavādino. Bhūtoti vijjamāno. Nipphattoti nipphanno. Na tassa dāni nipphādetabbaṃ kiñci atthīti laddhi. Idappaccayā idanti imasmā viññāṇāhārapaccayā idaṃ nāmarūpaṃ. Puna idappaccayā idanti imasmā nāmarūpapaccayā idaṃ saḷāyatananti evaṃ bahūsu ṭhānesu bhagavatā kathitattā yathā paccayato nibbattaṃ saṅkhāramattamidanti saññattiṃ upagato. Tenāpīti saññattupagatenāpi. Ekābaddhaṃ katvāti yathā pucchāya avasaro na hoti, tathā ekābaddhaṃ katvā. Desanāruḷhanti yato saḷāyatanapadato paṭṭhāya “saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso”tiādinā desanā paṭiccasamuppādavīthiṃ āruḷhameva. Tamevāti saḷāyatanapadameva [M 2.0035] gahetvā. Vivajjentoti vivaṭṭento. Evamāhāti “channaṃtvevā”tiādiākārena evaṃ desite, “vineyyajano paṭivijjhatī”ti evamāha. Viññāṇāhāro āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattiyāti evaṃ purimabhavato āyatibhavassa paccayavasena mūlakāraṇavasena ca desitattā “viññāṇanāmarūpānaṃ antare eko sandhī”ti vuttaṃ. Tadaminā viññāṇaggahaṇena abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇassāpi gahaṇaṃ katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

‘Giving an opening for the question’ means giving an opening for this question of one holding a particular view: ‘Who, venerable sir, makes contact?’ The intention is a desire to separate him from that. ‘In all passages’ means in the passages spoken by the one holding a particular view and by the Blessed One. ‘A being’ means a self.
