Kammākammanti vinicchayaṃ. Nijjaṭanti niggumbaṃ, suddhanti attho. Pathavīkasiṇādīsu kammaṃ ārabhatītiādi pāḷiyaṃ samathapubbaṅgamā vipassanā dassitāti katvā vuttaṃ[M 2.0068]. Evañhi pāmojjādidassanaṃ sambhavatīti. Devassāti meghassa. Kasmā panettha “khīṇāsavassa…pe… ṭhitakālo veditabbo”ti vuttaṃ, nanu pubbe devaṭṭhāniyo abhisaṅkhāro vutto, na abhisaṅkhāro khīṇāsavoti? Nāyaṃ doso, kāraṇūpacārena phalassa vuttattā. Abhisaṅkhāramūlako hi khandhasantāno khandhasantāne ca ucchinnasaṃyoge khīṇāsavasamaññāti.

Therein, because formations arise when pre-established ignorance is present and do not arise when it is absent, they are said to be like rain occurring on a high mountain, as stated: 'Ignorance... the rain should be understood.' The passage beginning 'The unlearned one, indeed,' is a confirmation of the meaning already stated. By the phrase 'having made a desire for craving,' it shows the harm in the arising of all formations. For craving is called 'affection.' The formation that produces the final existence for one in their final existence, not having attained Nibbāna, is as if it stands touching Nibbāna, the final part; hence the simile 'like a time standing touching the great ocean' is given. By this, even having completed the round of consciousness and so on, the process of consciousness of one in their final existence is shown. For that can be said to be completed, since beyond that there is no round of consciousness and so on. For a person who is born, the hearing of the Dhamma should be desired for the sake of experiencing the suffering of the round conditioned by birth. Though this is not found in this sutta, it is found in other suttas; thus, showing that it should be brought from there and stated, it is said: 'But the word of the Buddha...' and so forth. This teaching is given with reference to the disciples and bodhisattas. For others, there is no purpose in taking up other suttas, hence it is said: 'For indeed...' and so forth. This is a detailed explanation of the meaning stated in brief, as it is taken in accordance with the Pāli. 'Arising' means the arising aggregates are taken; thus it is said 'with their changes.' Because it explains the characteristic of impermanence and so on, it is brought in as a characteristic. 'Kamma and non-kamma' means the determination. 'Free from entanglement' means free from thickets; the meaning is 'pure.' It is said because in the Pāli, in 'one begins work on the earth kasiṇa, etc.,' insight preceded by serenity is shown. For only in this way is the manifestation of joy and so on possible. 'Of the deva' means of the cloud. Why then is it said here: 'For one whose taints are destroyed... the time should be understood as standing'? Was not the formation previously spoken of as being in the position of a deva? And a formation is not one whose taints are destroyed. This is no fault, because the effect is spoken of by way of a figurative use of the cause. For the continuum of aggregates is rooted in formations, and when the fetters in the continuum of aggregates are cut off, there is the designation 'one whose taints are destroyed'.

Upanisasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Upanisa Sutta is concluded.

4. Aññatitthiyasuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Aññatitthiya Sutta

24. Soti sāriputtatthero. Yadi na tāva paviṭṭho, kasmā “pāvisī”ti vuttanti āha “pavisissāmī”tiādi. Tena avassambhāvini bhūte viya upacāro hotīti dasseti. Idāni tamatthaṃ upamāya vibhāvento “yathā ki”ntiādimāha. Atippagoyeva nikkhantadivasoti pakatiyā bhikkhācaraṇavelāya ativiya pāto eva vihārato nikkhantadivasabhāgo. Etadahosīti etaṃ “atippago kho”tiādikaṃ cintanaṃ ahosi. Dakkhiṇadvārassāti rājagahanagare dakkhiṇadvārassa veḷuvanassa ca antarā ahosi, tasmā “tenupasaṅkamissa”nti cintanā ahosīti adhippāyo. Kiṃ vādīti catūsu vādesu kataraṃ vādaṃ vadasi. Kimakkhāyīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Kiṃ vadatīti pana cattāro vāde sāmaññato gahetvā napuṃsakaliṅgena vadati yathā kiṃ te jātaliṅgaṃ. Sabbanāmañhetaṃ, yadidaṃ napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ. Vadati etenāti vādo, dassanaṃ. Taṃ sandhāyāha “kiṃ ettha…pe… dassananti pucchantī”ti. “Dhammapaṭisambhidā”tiādīsu viya dhamma-saddo hetuatthoti āha “yaṃ vuttaṃ kāraṇaṃ, tassa anukāraṇa”nti. Vādassa vacanassa anuppatti vādappavatti.

24. 'He' refers to the Elder Sāriputta. If he had not yet entered, why was it said, 'he entered'? He replies, 'I will enter,' and so forth. This shows a figurative usage, treating an inevitable future event as if it were past. Now, elaborating on that meaning with a simile, he says, 'Just as...' The phrase 'atippagoyeva nikkhantadivaso' means the part of the day when one leaves the monastery exceptionally early, much earlier than the usual time for the alms-round. 'Etadahosi' means that this thought, 'It is very early,' and so forth, arose. 'Of the southern gate' means it was between the southern gate of Rājagaha and the Bamboo Grove; therefore, the meaning is that the thought arose: 'I will approach him.' 'What is your tenet?' means among the four tenets, which tenet do you state? 'What do you declare?' is a synonym for that. But 'What does he say?'—taking the four tenets generally, he speaks in the neuter gender, as in 'What is your gender?' This is a pronoun, that is, the neuter gender. 'That by which one speaks' is a tenet (`vādo`), a view (`dassanaṃ`). Referring to this, they ask, 'What here... view?' Just as in 'Dhammapaṭisambhidā' and so forth, the word 'dhamma' has the meaning of cause; thus he says, 'What was stated as the reason, its corresponding reason.' The attainment of the tenet, of the utterance, is the process of the tenet.

Idaṃ vacananti “ekamidāha”ntiādivacanaṃ. Sāti “eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā”ti evaṃ pavattakathā. Accharaṃ aṅguliphoṭanaṃ arahatīti acchariyaṃ. Abbhutanti niruttinayena padasiddhi daṭṭhabbā. Sabbavādānanti sabbesaṃ catubbidhavādānaṃ. Paṭhamo hettha sassatavādo, dutiyo ucchedavādo, tatiyo ekaccasassatavādo, catuttho adhiccasamuppannavādo, tesaṃ sabbesaṃ [M 2.0069] paṭikkhepato [V 2.0059] paṭikkhepakāraṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṭiccasamuppādakittanaṃ vā pacurajanañāṇassa alabbhaneyyapatiṭṭhatāya gambhīrañceva, tathā avabhāsanato cetasi upaṭṭhānato gambhīrāvabhāsañca karonto. Tadeva padanti phassapadaṃyeva ādibhūtaṃ gahetvā.

'This statement' refers to the statement beginning, 'I say this one thing.' 'That' refers to the discussion that proceeded thus: 'Some ascetics and brahmins are proponents of the doctrine of kamma.' 'Wonderful' (`acchariyaṃ`) is so called because it deserves a finger-snap. The derivation of the word 'abbhuta' (amazing) should be understood according to the method of etymology. 'All tenets' refers to all four kinds of tenets: The first here is the tenet of eternalism, the second is the tenet of annihilationism, the third is the tenet of partial eternalism, and the fourth is the tenet of adventitious origination. Because of the refutation of all of them, the reason for the refutation has been stated. Or, the exposition of dependent origination is profound, since it is a footing unattainable by the knowledge of the masses, and also, by its manifestation, by its appearance in the mind, it has a profound radiance. 'That very term' means taking the term 'contact' itself as the primary one.

Aññatitthiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Aññatitthiya Sutta is concluded.

5. Bhūmijasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Bhūmija Sutta

25. Purimasutteti anantare purime sutte. Vuttanayeneva veditabbanti padatthe tato visiṭṭhaṃ aniddisitvā itaraṃ atthato vibhāvetuṃ “ayaṃ pana viseso”tiādimāha. Na kevalaṃ phassapaccayā uppajjati, atha kho phassassa sahakārīkāraṇabhūtaaññapaccayā ca uppajjatīti. Kāyenāti copanakāyena, kāyaviññattiyāti attho. Sā hi kāmaṃ paṭṭhāne āgatesu catuvīsatiyā paccayesu kenaci paccayena cetanāya paccayo na hoti. Yasmā pana kāye sati eva kāyakammaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati, tasmā sā tassā sāmaggiyabhāvena icchitabbāti vuttaṃ “kāyenapi kariyamānaṃ karīyatī”ti. Tenāha bhagavā “kāye vā, hānanda, sati kāyasañcetanāhetu uppajjati ajjhattaṃ sukhaṃ dukkha”nti. Vācāyapīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Manasāti pātubhūtena manasā, na manamattenāti. Attanā parehi anussāhitena. Parenāti parena anussāhena. Sampajānenāti ñāṇasampayuttacittavasena pajānantena. Asampajānenāti tathā na sampajānantena. Tassāti sukhadukkhassa. Kāyasañcetanāhetūti kāyakammanimittaṃ, kāyikassa kammassa katattā upacitattāti attho. Esa nayo sesasañcetanāsupi. Uddhaccasahagatacetanā pavattiyaṃ vipākaṃ detiyevāti “vīsati cetanā labbhantī”ti vuttaṃ. Tathā vacīdvāreti ettha “kāmāvacarakusalākusalavasena vīsati cetanā labbhantī”ti idaṃ tathā-saddena upasaṃharati. Rūpārūpacetanāhīti rūpāvacarārūpāvacarakusalacetanāhi. Tappaccayaṃ yathārahanti adhippāyo. Tāpi cetanāti yathāvuttā ekūnavīsati cetanā avijjāpaccayā honti kusalānampi pageva itarādhiṭṭhahitāvijjasseva uppajjanato, aññathā anuppajjanato. Yathāvuttacetanābhedanti [M 2.0070] yathāvuttaṃ kāyacetanādivibhāgaṃ. Parehi anussāhito saraseneva pavattamāno. Parehi kāriyamānoti parehi ussāhito hutvā kayiramāno. Jānantopīti anussavādivasena jānantopi. Kammameva jānantoti tadā attanā kariyamānakammameva jānanto.

25. In the Purima Sutta, which is the immediately preceding sutta. It should be understood in the same way as previously stated. Without indicating anything distinct from that in the meaning of the words, in order to clarify the rest in terms of meaning, he says, 'But this is the distinction,' and so forth. Not only does it arise dependent on contact, but it also arises due to other conditions that are the co-operative cause of contact. By 'body' (kāyena) means by the moving body; the meaning is by bodily intimation. For although, among the twenty-four conditions mentioned in the Paṭṭhāna, it is not a condition for volition by any condition. However, since bodily action is so called only when the body exists, and not when it does not exist, it should be accepted as part of the totality. Thus, it is said, 'Even when done by the body, it is done.' Therefore, the Blessed One said, 'When there is the body, Ānanda, internal pleasure and pain arise due to bodily volition.' The same method applies to 'by speech.' By 'mind' (manasā) means by the manifest mind, not merely by the mind itself. By 'oneself' (attanā) means not urged by others. By 'by others' (parena) means by the urging of another. 'With awareness' means knowing with a consciousness associated with knowledge. 'Without awareness' means not knowing in that way. 'Of that' refers to pleasure and pain. 'Due to bodily volition' (kāyasañcetanāhetu) means the cause of bodily action; the meaning is due to the performance and accumulation of bodily action. This method also applies to the remaining volitions. A volition accompanied by restlessness certainly yields a result in the course of existence; thus, it is said, 'Twenty volitions are obtainable.' Similarly, regarding the verbal door, he concludes with the word 'similarly' that 'twenty volitions are obtainable in terms of sense-sphere wholesome and unwholesome states.' 'By form and formless volitions' means by wholesome volitions of the form sphere and formless sphere. 'Depending on that, accordingly' is the intended meaning. 'Those volitions too'—as stated, the nineteen volitions are dependent on ignorance, even the wholesome ones, let alone the others, since they arise only for one in whom ignorance is established, and otherwise do not arise. 'The classification of volitions as stated' means the division into bodily volition, etc., as previously explained. By 'done by others' means being urged by others and being done. 'Even while knowing' means knowing through hearsay and so on. 'Knowing only the action' means knowing only the action being done by oneself at that time.

Catūsūti “sāmaṃ vā pare vā sampajāno vā asampajāno vā”ti evaṃ vuttesu catūsu ṭhānesu. Yathāvutte ekūnavīsaticetanādhamme asaṅkhārikasasaṅkhārikabhāvena sampajānakatāsampajānakatabhāvena [V 2.0060] catuguṇe katvā vuttaṃ “chasattati dvesatā cetanādhammā”ti. Yesaṃ sahajātakoṭi labbhati, tesampi upanissayakoṭi labbhatevāti “upanissayakoṭiyā anupatitā”tiicceva vuttā. Teti yathāvuttā sabbepi dhammā. So kāyo na hotīti ettha pasādakāyopi gahetabbo. Tenāha “yasmiṃ kāye satī”tiādi. So kāyo na hotīti so kāyo paccayanirodhena na hoti. Vācāti saddavācā. Manoti yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ. Idāni kammavaseneva yojetuṃ “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Eseva nayo “vācāpi dvārabhūtā manopi dvārabhūto”ti. Khīṇāsavassa kathaṃ kāyo na hoti, na tassa kāyakammādhiṭṭhānanti adhippāyo. Avipākattāti avipākadhammattāti attho. Kāyo na hotīti vuttaṃ akammakaraṇabhāvato.

By 'in the four' (catūsu) means in these four instances as stated: 'whether by oneself or by others, whether knowingly or unknowingly.' As mentioned, the nineteen volitional phenomena, classified as unprompted or prompted, and as done knowingly or unknowingly, are multiplied fourfold; hence it is said: 'seventy-six volitional phenomena.' For those for whom the category of co-nascence is obtained, the category of dependence is also obtained—thus, it is stated: 'They are included in the category of dependence.' 'Those' means all the phenomena as stated. By 'that body does not exist'—here, the sensitive body should also be understood. Hence he says, 'In whatever body there is,' and so forth. 'That body does not exist' means that body does not exist due to the cessation of its condition. 'Speech' (vācā) means audible speech. 'Mind' (mano) means any consciousness. Now, to connect this by way of kamma, it is said: 'Moreover,' and so forth. The same method applies to: 'Speech is also a door, and mind is also a door.' How is it that the body of one whose defilements are destroyed does not exist? The meaning is that for him, it is not a basis for bodily kamma. 'Because of being non-resultant' means because it is a non-resultant phenomenon. 'It is said that the body does not exist' because of the absence of the function of producing a result.

Tanti kammaṃ. Khettaṃ na hotīti tassa dukkhassa aviruhanaṭṭhānattā. Viruhanaṭṭhānādayo byatirekavasena vuttā. Tenāha “na hotī”ti. Kāraṇaṭṭhenāti ādhārabhūtakāraṇabhāvena. Sañcetanāmūlakanti sañcetanānimittaṃ. Viruhanādīnaṃ atthānanti “viruhanaṭṭhenā”tiādinā vuttānaṃ atthānaṃ. Iminā viruhanādibhāvena vedanā “sukhadukkhavedanā”ti kathitā, nayidha jeṭṭhalakkhaṇaṃ sukhadukkhaṃ nippayojakassa sukhassa dukkhassa ca adhippetattā. Upekkhāvedanāpettha sukhasaṇhasabhāvavipākabhūtā vedanāva.

That (taṃ) refers to kamma. 'The field does not exist' because it is a place for the non-arising of that suffering. Places of arising and so forth are mentioned by way of contrast. Therefore, it is said, 'it does not exist.' By 'way of cause' means by way of being the causal support. 'Rooted in volition' (sañcetanāmūlakaṃ) means having volition as its cause. 'For the meanings of arising, and so forth' refers to the meanings mentioned in the phrase beginning 'by way of the place of arising.' By this mode of arising and so forth, feeling is called 'pleasant and painful feeling,' but here the pre-eminent characteristic of pleasure and pain is not intended, because pleasure and pain without a specific purpose are meant. Even equanimous feeling here is merely a feeling that is the resultant of a subtly pleasant nature.

Bhūmijasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Bhūmija Sutta is completed.

6. Upavāṇasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Upavāṇa Sutta

26. Vaṭṭadukkhameva [M 2.0071] kathitaṃ itaradukkhassapi vipākassa saṅgaṇhanato.

26. Only the suffering of cyclic existence is taught, as it encompasses even the result of other suffering.

Upavāṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Upavāṇa Sutta is concluded.

7. Paccayasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Paccaya Sutta

27. Paṭipāṭiyāti paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapanena. Catusaccayojanaṃ dassetuṃ pariyosāna…pe… ādi vuttaṃ. Dukkhasaccavasenāti pariññeyyabhāvavasena. Jarāmaraṇāpadesena hi pañcupādānakkhandhā vuttā, te cassa attano phalassa paccayā na honti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “paccayaṃ jānātī”ti. Vineyyajjhāsayavasena hettha desanā pavattā. Sampannoti samannāgato. Āgatoti upagato, adhigatoti attho. Passatīti paccavekkhaṇañāṇena paccakkhato passati, maggapaññāya evaṃ asammohapaṭivedhavasena passati. Maggañāṇeneva, na phalañāṇena. Dhammasotaṃ samāpannoti [V 2.0061] ariyadhammasotaṃ sammadeva āpanno patto. Anaye nairiyanato, aye ca iriyanato, sadevakena ca lokena “saraṇa”nti akaraṇīyato ariyapakkhaṃ bhajanto puthujjanabhūmiṃ atikkanto. Nibbedhikapaññāyāti catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ nibbijjhanakapaññāya. Āhacca tiṭṭhati maggakkhaṇe, phalakkhaṇe pana āhacca ṭhito nāma.

27. ‘In sequence’ (paṭipāṭiyā) means by establishing in sequence. To show the application of the four truths, the conclusion…etc….the beginning was stated. ‘By way of the truth of suffering’ (dukkhasaccavasena) means by way of being something to be fully understood. For by mentioning aging and death, the five aggregates of clinging are stated, and they are not the condition for their own fruit. With reference to this, it was said, ‘He understands the condition.’ The teaching here proceeds by way of the disposition of those to be guided. ‘Endowed’ (sampanno) means possessed. ‘Attained’ (āgato) means approached; the meaning is realized. ‘He sees’ (passati) means he sees directly with the knowledge of reviewing; with the wisdom of the path he sees in this way by penetrating without delusion. Only with the knowledge of the path, not with the knowledge of fruition. ‘He has entered the stream of the Dhamma’ (dhammasotaṃ samāpanno) means he has rightly entered or reached the noble stream of the Dhamma. Because it does not lead to the wrong course and leads to the right course, and because it is not to be made a ‘refuge’ by the world with its devas, resorting to the noble side, he has transcended the plane of the ordinary person. ‘With wisdom that pierces’ (nibbedhikapaññāya) means with wisdom that penetrates the four noble truths. ‘Stands touching’ (āhacca tiṭṭhati) at the moment of the path, but at the moment of fruition, it is said that he stands having touched.

Paccayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Paccaya Sutta is concluded.

8. Bhikkhusuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Bhikkhu Sutta

28. Uttānameva sabbasova sattame āgatanayattā, vineyyajjhāsayavasena hi idaṃ suttaṃ satthārā aññasmiṃ āsane desitaṃ, parisāya vivaṭṭena sātthikāti satthu desanā āgatāti ayaṃ paṭiggāhakādhīnā hotīti dhammagāravena saṅgahaṃ āropentiyeva.

28. It is entirely clear, as it follows the method that has come in the seventh sutta. For this sutta was taught by the Teacher on another seat according to the disposition of those to be trained. The Teacher’s teaching has come as beneficial to the assembly with its meaning unfolded, and this is dependent on the recipient; thus, out of reverence for the Dhamma, they undertake its compilation.

Bhikkhusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Bhikkhu Sutta is concluded.

9. Samaṇabrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Samaṇabrāhmaṇa Sutta

29. Akkharabhāṇakānanti [M 2.0072] akkhararucīnaṃ. Upasaggena padavaḍḍhanampi ruccanti. Tenāha “te hī”tiādi.

29. ‘Of the reciters of syllables’ (akkharabhāṇakānaṃ) means of those who delight in syllables. They delight even in the lengthening of words by prefixes. Therefore, he says, ‘for they’ etc.

Samaṇabrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Samaṇabrāhmaṇa Sutta is concluded.

10. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Second Samaṇabrāhmaṇa Sutta

30. Dvīsu suttesūti navamadasamasuttesu.

30. ‘In two suttas’ (dvīsu suttesu) means in the ninth and tenth suttas.

Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Samaṇabrāhmaṇa Sutta is concluded.

Dasabalavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Dasabalavagga is concluded.

4. Kaḷārakhattiyavaggo

4. The Kaḷārakhattiya Chapter

1. Bhūtasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Bhūta Sutta

31. Ajitamāṇavenāti [V 2.0062] soḷasasu bāvariyabrāhmaṇaparicārakesu “ajito”ti laddhanāmena māṇavena. Saṅkhā vuccati paññā, saṅkhātā pariññātā dhammā yesaṃ te saṅkhātadhammā, paṭividdhasaccā khīṇāsavā. Sekkhā pana vipākassa apariññātattā “saṅkhātadhammā”ti na vuccanti. Sekkhadhammasamannāgamena te sekkhā. Te pana kāmaṃ puggalapaṭilābhavasena anekasahassāva honti, catumaggaheṭṭhimaphalattayassa pana vasena taṃsamaṅgitāsāmaññena na sattajanato uddhanti āha “satta jane”ti niyametvā viseseti. Saṃkilesavajjaṃ, tato vā attānaṃ viya vineyyalokaṃ nipāti rakkhatīti nipako, tassa bhāvo nepakkaṃ, ñāṇanti āha “nepakkaṃ vuccati paññā, tāya samannāgatattā nipako”ti.

31. ‘By the youth Ajita’ (Ajitamāṇavena) means by the youth known by the name ‘Ajita’ among the sixteen attendants of the Brahmin Bāvari. ‘Discernment’ (saṅkhā) is called wisdom. Those for whom phenomena are discerned and fully understood are called ‘those who have discerned the Dhamma,’ those who have penetrated the truths and destroyed the taints. However, trainees, because they have not fully understood the results, are not called ‘those who have discerned the Dhamma.’ They are trainees by virtue of possessing the qualities of a trainee. Indeed, by way of individual attainment, they may number in the thousands. But in terms of the three lower fruits of the four paths, due to their commonality of being endowed with them, they do not go beyond seven persons—thus, it is specified and distinguished as ‘seven persons.’ ‘The fault of defilement’ (saṃkilesavajjaṃ). Or, like oneself, he diligently protects the world to be disciplined—thus, he is prudent (nipako). His state is prudence (nepakkaṃ). Knowledge—it is said, ‘Prudence is called wisdom; because he is endowed with it, he is prudent.’

“Ko nu kho imassa pañhassa attho”ti cintento pañhāya kaṅkhati nāma. “Kathaṃ byākaramāno nu kho satthu ajjhāsayaṃ na virodhemī”ti cintento ajjhāsayaṃ kaṅkhati nāma. Sujānanīyatthaparicchedaṃ katvā cintanā hettha [M 2.0073] “kaṅkhā”ti adhippetā, na vicikicchāti. Pahīnavicikiccho hi mahāthero āyasmato assajimahātherassa santikeyeva, vicinanabhūtaṃ kukkuccasadisaṃ panetaṃ vīmaṃsanamattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pattaṃ ādāya carantoti pabbajitabhāvalakkhaṇaṃ. Dhammasenāpatibhāvena vā mama pattadhammadesanāvāraṃ ādāya carantoti evaṃ vā ettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

Thinking, ‘What indeed is the meaning of this question?’ is called doubting the question. Thinking, ‘How, when answering, might I not contradict the Teacher’s intention?’ is called doubting the intention. Here, ‘doubt’ (kaṅkhā) is intended as the act of thinking after determining what is to be clearly understood, not uncertainty (vicikicchā). For the great elder had already abandoned uncertainty in the presence of the Venerable Assaji the Great Elder. But this should be seen as a mere investigation, similar to scrupulousness (kukkucca), which is of the nature of inquiry. ‘Wandering, taking up the bowl’ (pattaṃ ādāya caranto) signifies the characteristic of the renunciant state. Alternatively, due to being a commander of the Dhamma, the meaning here should be understood as, ‘Wandering, taking up my turn to teach the Dhamma that has been attained.’

Jātanti yathārahaṃ paccayato uppannaṃ, saṅkhatanti attho. Pañhabyākaraṇaṃ upaṭṭhāsīti pañhassa byākaraṇatā paṭibhāsi. “Sammappaññāya passatī”ti pāṭho, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “sammappaññāya passato”ti padaṃ uddharitvā “passantassā”ti attho vutto. Taṃ “bhūtanti…pe… paṭipanno hotī”ti imāya pāḷiyā na sameti, tasmā yathādassitapāṭho eva yutto. Yāva arahattamaggā nibbidādīnaṃ atthāyāti samitāpekkhadhammavasā padaṃ vadanti. Āhārasambhavanti paccayahetukaṃ. Sekkhapaṭipadā kathitā “nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti vacanato. Esa nayo nirodhavārepi. Nibbidāti karaṇe paccattavacanaṃ, virāgā nirodhāti karaṇe nissakkavacananti [V 2.0063] āha “sabbāni kāraṇavacanānī”ti. Anupādāti anupādāya. Bhūtamidantiādimāha sabbasuttaṃ āhaccabhāsitaṃ jinavacanameva karonto.

‘Born’ (jātaṃ) means arisen from conditions as is appropriate; the meaning is ‘conditioned’ (saṅkhataṃ). ‘The explanation of the question appeared’ (pañhabyākaraṇaṃ upaṭṭhāsi) means the answering of the question became clear. The reading is ‘he sees with right wisdom’ (sammappaññāya passati), but in the commentary, the word ‘passato’ is cited, and its meaning is given as ‘of one who sees’ (passantassa). That does not fit with this Pāli passage, ‘bhūtaṃ…pe… paṭipanno hoti,’ therefore the reading as shown is indeed fitting. They say the term is stated by the power of the principle of considering things together, as being for the purpose of disenchantment and so on, up to the path of arahantship. ‘Originating from nutriment’ (āhārasambhavaṃ) means having conditions as its cause. The practice of a trainee is described by the statement, ‘he is practicing for disenchantment, dispassion, cessation.’ This method applies in the section on cessation as well. ‘Nibbidā’ is an instrumental term with a reflexive sense; ‘virāgā’ and ‘nirodhā’ are instrumental terms with a sense of relinquishment, thus it is said, ‘all are instrumental terms.’ ‘Without clinging’ (anupādā) means without clinging (anupādāya). ‘This has come to be’ (bhūtamidaṃ) and so forth—he speaks the entire sutta, making it indeed the word of the Victor, spoken directly.

Bhūtasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Bhūta Sutta is concluded.

2. Kaḷārasuttavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Kaḷāra Sutta

32. Tassa therassa nāmaṃ jātisamudāgataṃ. Nivattoti pubbe vaṭṭasotassa paṭisotaṃ gantuṃ āraddho, taṃ avisahanto anusotameva gacchanto, tato nivatto pariklesavidhame asaṃsaṭṭho viyutto hoti. Ettha cetanāti vā assāso. Hīnāyāvattanaṃ nāma kāmesu sāpekkhatāya, tattha ca nirapekkhatā tatiyamaggādhigamenāti dassento “tayo magge”tiādimāha. Sāvakapāramīñāṇaṃ therassa arahattādhigamena nipphannaṃ, tasmā tassa taṃ uparimakoṭiyā assāso vutto. Ugghāṭitāti vivaṭā, vūpasamitāti attho. Tatthāti arahattappattiyaṃ. Vicikicchābhāvanti nibbematikataṃ.

32. The name of that elder arose from his birth. ‘Turned back’ means that though he had previously begun to go against the stream of the cycle, being unable to bear it, he went along with the stream instead. Then, having turned back from that, he became unmingled and detached from the torment of defilements. Here, ‘intention’ refers to aspiration or breathing. ‘Reverting to the inferior’ means having attachment to sensual pleasures; freedom from such attachment comes through the attainment of the third path. To show this, it is said, ‘the three paths,’ and so on. The knowledge of the disciple’s perfections was fulfilled by the elder’s attainment of arahantship; therefore, that was his aspiration at the highest point. ‘Opened’ means revealed, that is, pacified. ‘There’ refers to the attainment of arahantship. ‘The absence of doubt’ means being without uncertainty.

Na [M 2.0074] evaṃ byākatāti “khīṇā jātī”tiādikā evaṃ uttānakaṃ na byākatā, pariyāyena pana byākatā. Kenacīti kenacipi kāraṇena. Evaṃ uttānakaṃ byākarissati.

‘Not declared thus’ means it was not explicitly declared in this way with ‘destroyed is birth,’ etc., but it was declared indirectly. ‘By some reason’ means by any reason at all. He will declare it explicitly in this way.

Tassa paccayassa khayāti tassa kammabhavasaṅkhātassa paccayassa avijjāya sahakāritāyaṃ saṅgahitassa khayā anuppādā nirodhā. Khīṇasminti khīṇe. Anuppādanirodhena niruddhe jātiyā yathāvutte paccaye. Jātisaṅkhātaṃ phalaṃ khīṇaṃ anuppattidhammataṃ āpāditanti. Viditaṃ ñātaṃ. Ājānāti catusaccaṃ heṭṭhimamaggehi ñātaṃ anatikkamitvāva paṭivijjhatīti aññā aggamaggo. Tadupacārena aggaphalaṃ idha “aññā” nāma. Paccayoti bhavūpapattiyā paccayo paṭiccasamuppādo.

‘With the destruction of that condition’ means with the destruction, non-arising, and cessation of that condition, which is called karmic existence and is included in the cooperation of ignorance. ‘When it is destroyed’ (khīṇasmiṃ) means when the aforesaid condition for birth has ceased through non-arising and cessation. The result called birth has been destroyed, having attained the nature of non-arising. ‘Known’ means understood. ‘He understands’ refers to penetrating the Four Truths without bypassing them, which have been known by the lower paths—thus, the supreme path is called ‘final knowledge.’ By extension, the supreme fruit is here called ‘final knowledge.’ ‘Condition’ refers to dependent origination as the condition for the arising of existence.

Meti mayā. Aññāsi ākāraggahaṇena cittācāraṃ jānāti. Tenāti bhagavatā. Byākaraṇaṃ anumoditaṃ pañhabyākaraṇassa visayakatabhāvato.

‘Me’ means ‘by me.’ ‘He knew’ means he understood the conduct of the mind by grasping the manner. ‘By him’ refers to the Blessed One. The explanation was approved because it pertained to the subject matter of the question's explanation.

Ayamassa visayoti ayaṃ vedanā assa sāriputtattherassa savisayo tattha visayabhāvena pavattattā. Kiñcāpīti kiñcāpi sukhā vedanā ṭhitisukhā dukkhā vedanā vipariṇāmasukhā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā ñāṇasukhā. Vipariṇāmakoṭiyāti aniccabhāvena sabbāva vedanā dukkhā nāma[V 2.0064]. Sukhapaṭikkhepatopi hi sukhapītiyā pharaṇatāya sukhāti tikkhamattena vipariṇāmadukkhāti vipariṇāmato abhāvādhigamena sukhanirodhakkhaṇamattena. Tathā hi vuttaṃ papañcasūdaniyaṃ “sukhāya vedanāya atthibhāvo sukha”nti. Sukhakāmo dukkhaṃ titikkhati. Apariññātavatthukānañhi sukhavedanuparamo dukkhato upaṭṭhāti, tasmāyamattho viyogena dīpetabbo. “Dukkhā vipariṇāmasukhā”ti etthāpi eseva nayo. Tathācāha papañcasūdaniyaṃ “dukkhāya vedanāya natthibhāvo sukha”nti. Dukkhavedanuparamo hi vuttānaṃ sukhato upaṭṭhāti evāti vadanti. Tassa yogassa vūpasamena “aho sukhaṃ jāta”nti majjhattavedanāya jānanabhāvo yāthāvato avabujjhanaṃ sukhaṃ. Adukkhamasukhāpi vedanā vijānantassa sukhaṃ hoti tassa sukhumatāya viññeyyabhāvato. Yathā rūpārūpadhammānaṃ salakkhaṇato sāmaññalakkhaṇato ca sammadeva avabodho paramaṃ sukhaṃ. Tenāha –

‘This is his domain,’ meaning this feeling is the domain of the Venerable Sāriputta, as it arises within his sphere of experience and is present as an object. ‘Even though’ pleasant feeling is pleasant in its stability, painful feeling is pleasant in its change, and neutral feeling is pleasant in its knowledge. ‘By the extremity of change’—due to impermanence, all feeling is called suffering. Even the pleasure of pleasant feeling, due to its sharp intensity of pervasion, is suffering by change, for it is merely the moment of the cessation of pleasure through the attainment of non-existence due to change. As stated in the Papañcasūdanī: ‘The existence of pleasant feeling is pleasure.’ One who desires pleasure endures suffering. For those who have not fully understood the object, the cessation of pleasant feeling appears as suffering; thus, this meaning should be clarified by separation. ‘Painful feeling is pleasant by change’—here too, the same principle applies. As the Papañcasūdanī states: ‘The non-existence of painful feeling is pleasure.’ The cessation of painful feeling, they say, appears as pleasure for those who have understood. Through the calming of that bond, the state of knowing the neutral feeling as ‘Oh, happiness has arisen!’—that is, truly comprehending it—is happiness. Even neutral feeling is happiness when one knows it, due to its subtlety and knowable nature. Just as the correct understanding of form and formless phenomena, both in their specific and general characteristics, is the highest happiness. Therefore, it is said—

“Yato [M 2.0075] yato sammasati, khandhānaṃ udayabbayaṃ;

Labhatī pītipāmojjaṃ, amataṃ taṃ vijānata”nti. (dha. pa. 374);

‘Whenever one comprehends the rise and fall of the aggregates, one obtains joy and delight; that is the deathless for those who know.’

Aññāṇadukkhāti ajānanabhāvo adukkhamasukhāvedanāya dukkhaṃ. Sammā vibhāgajānanasabhāvo ñāṇassa sambhavo. Ñāṇasampayuttā hi ñāṇūpanissayā adukkhamasukhā vedanā pasatthākārā, yato sā iṭṭhā ceva iṭṭhaphalā cāti. Ajānanabhāvoti ettha vuttavipariyāyena attho veditabbo. “Dukkhanti vidito”ti pāḷi, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana viditanti paduddhāro kato, taṃ atthadassanamattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

‘Suffering due to ignorance’ means that the state of not knowing is the suffering inherent in neutral feeling. The nature of knowing by correct distinction is the arising of knowledge. For when the neutral feeling is associated with knowledge and has knowledge as its support, it becomes praiseworthy in nature, since it is both desirable and bears desirable fruit. Here, the meaning of ‘the state of not knowing’ should be understood as the opposite of what has been stated. The Pāli reading is ‘known as suffering,’ but in the commentary, the word ‘known’ is extracted; this should be regarded merely as an illustration of the meaning.

Vedanāparicchedajānaneti “tisso imā vedanā”ti evaṃ paricchedato jānane. Aññāsīti kadā aññāsi? Imasmiṃ desanākāleti vadanti, paṭivedhakāleti pana yuttaṃ. Yathāpaṭividdhā hi vedanā idha therena desitāti. Iminā kāraṇenāti “yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkha”nti vedanānaṃ aniccatāya dukkhabhāvajānanasaṅkhātena kāraṇena. Taṃnimittaṃ hissa vedanāsu taṇhā na uppajjati. Atippapañcoti ativitthāro. Dukkhasmiṃ antogadhaṃ dukkhapariyāpannattā. Dukkhanti sabbaṃ vedayitaṃ dukkhaṃ saṅkhāradukkhabhāvato. Ñātamatteti yāthāvato avabujjhanamatte. Taṇhā na tiṭṭhatīti na santiṭṭhati nappavattati.

The knowledge that discerns feelings is knowing them by way of classification as 'these are three feelings.' When did he know? They say it was at the time of this teaching, but it is more fitting that it was at the time of realization. For the feelings were explained here by the elder as they were penetrated. 'By this reason' means by the reason known as the knowledge of the suffering nature of feelings due to their impermanence, as in 'what is impermanent is suffering.' For him, craving does not arise in feelings on account of that. 'Too elaborate' means excessively detailed. 'Included in suffering' means because it is encompassed by suffering. 'Suffering' means all that is felt is suffering due to its nature as the suffering of formations. 'Merely known' means just the act of comprehending it as it actually is. 'Craving does not persist' means it does not remain or proceed.

Kathaṃ vimokkhāti ajjhattabahiddhābhedesu vimuttā. Hetumhi cetaṃ nissakkavacananti hetuatthena karaṇavacanena atthamāha “katarena vimokkhenā”ti. Karaṇatthepi vā etaṃ nissakkavacananti [V 2.0065] tathā vuttaṃ. Abhinivesoti vipassanārambho. Bahiddhādhammāpi daṭṭhabbāyeva sabbassapi pariññeyyassa parijānitabbato. Ñāṇaṃ pavattetvā. Teti ajjhattasaṅkhāre. Vavatthapetvāti salakkhaṇato paricchinditvā. Bahiddhā otāretīti bahiddhāsaṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ otāreti. Ajjhattaṃ otāretīti ajjhattasaṅkhāre sammasati. Tatra tasmiṃ catukke. Tesaṃ vavatthānakāleti tesaṃ ajjhattasaṅkhārānaṃ vipassanākāle.

'How are there liberations?' They are liberated in the divisions of internal and external. This is a term for renunciation in the sense of cause; thus, he states the meaning with the instrumental case, 'By which liberation?', because it has the meaning of cause. Or, this is also a term for renunciation in the sense of the instrumental; thus it is said. 'Application' is the beginning of insight. External phenomena should also be seen, for all that is to be fully understood must be comprehended. 'Having set knowledge in motion.' 'Those' refers to the internal formations. 'Having determined' means having distinguished by their characteristics. 'It directs externally' means it directs knowledge toward external formations. 'It directs internally' means it contemplates the internal formations. 'There' means in that quartet. 'At the time of their determination' means at the time of insight into those internal formations.

Sabbupādānakkhayāti sabbaso upādānānaṃ khayā. Kāmaṃ diṭṭhisīlabbataattavādupādānāni paṭhamamaggeneva khīyanti, kāmupādānaṃ pana aggamaggenāti tassa [M 2.0076] vasena “sabbupādānakkhayā”ti vadanto thero attano arahattapattiṃ byākaroti. Tenāha “āsavā nānussavantī”ti. Satoti iminā sativepullappattiṃ dasseti. Cakkhuto rūpe savantīti cakkhuviññāṇavīthiyaṃ tadanugatamanoviññāṇavīthiyañca rūpārammaṇā āsavā pavattantīti. Kiñcāpi tattha kusalādīnampi pavatti atthi, kāmāsavādayo eva vaṇato yūsaṃ viya paggharaṇakaasucibhāvena sandanti, tathā sesavāresu. Tenāha “eva”ntiādi, tasmā te eva “āsavā”ti vuccanti. Tattha hi paggharaṇakaasucimhi niruḷho āsavasaddo. “Attānaṃ nāvajānāmī”ti vuttattā “omānapahānaṃ kathita”nti āha. Tena āsavesu samudāyupalakkhaṇaṃ kathitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Na hi seyyamānādippahānena vinā hīnamānaṃyeva pajahati. Pajānanāti “nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti vuttapajānanasampanno hotīti.

'With the complete destruction of all clinging' means the total destruction of all forms of clinging. Indeed, clinging to views, rites and rituals, and self-doctrine are destroyed by the first path, but clinging to sensual pleasures is destroyed by the highest path. Thus, the elder, by saying, 'With the complete destruction of all clinging,' declares his attainment of arahantship. Therefore, he says, 'The taints do not flow.' 'Mindful' indicates the attainment of the fullness of mindfulness. 'Flowing from the eye to forms' means that the taints, with forms as their object, proceed in the cognitive process of eye-consciousness and the subsequent mind-consciousness process. Although wholesome and other states also arise there, the taints of sensual desire and others flow like pus from a sore due to their oozing and impure nature; similarly in the remaining sense doors. Therefore, he says, 'Thus,' etc. Hence, these alone are called 'taints.' For the word 'taint' is established in the sense of an oozing impurity. Because it is said, 'I do not despise myself,' he said that 'the abandoning of low conceit is explained.' By this, it should be seen that the characteristic of the origin of the taints is explained. For without abandoning conceit such as 'I am better,' one does not abandon only low conceit. 'Understanding' means being endowed with the understanding stated as 'there is no more of this state of being.'

Sarūpabhedatopīti “cattāro”ti evaṃ parimāṇaparicchedatopi. Idaṃ bhagavā dassento āhāti sambandho. Idanti ca “ayampi kho”tiādivacanaṃ sandhāyāha.

'Also by the distinction of their own nature' means also by the delimitation of quantity, as in 'four.' The connection is: the Blessed One, showing this, said... And 'this' is said referring to the statement beginning with 'this too...'

Asambhinnāya evāti yathānisinnāya eva, avuṭṭhitāya evāti attho. Puggalathomanatthanti desanākusalānaṃ ānandattherādīnaṃ puggalānaṃ pasaṃsanatthaṃ ukkaṃsanatthaṃ. Dhammathomanatthanti paṭipattidhammassa pasaṃsanatthaṃ. Tepīti ānandattherādayo bhikkhūpi. Dhammapaṭiggāhakā bhikkhū. Attheti sīlādiatthe. Dhammeti pāḷidhamme.

'Without being broken up' means just as they were seated; the meaning is, without having gotten up. 'For the praise of individuals' means for the purpose of praising and extolling individuals skilled in teaching, such as the Elder Ānanda and others. 'For the praise of the Dhamma' means for the purpose of praising the Dhamma of practice. 'They too' means the monks, such as the Elder Ānanda and others. The monks who are receivers of the Dhamma. 'In the meaning' means in the meaning of virtue and so on. 'In the Dhamma' means in the Pāli Dhamma.

Assāti bhagavato. Ānubhāvaṃ karissati “divasañcepi bhagavā”tiādinā. Nanti sāriputtattheraṃ. Ahampi tatheva thomessāmi “sā hi bhikkhū”tiādinā. Evaṃ cintesīti evaṃ vakkhamānena dhammadāyādadesanāya cintitākārena cintesi. Tenāha “yathā”tiādi. Ekajjhāsayāyāti [V 2.0066] samānādhippāyāya. Matiyāti paññāya. Ayaṃ desanā aggāti bhagavā dhammasenāpatiṃ guṇato evaṃ paggaṇhātīti katvā vuttaṃ.

'His' refers to the Blessed One. He will manifest his power with the words beginning 'even if the Blessed One for a day...' 'Him' refers to the Elder Sāriputta. 'I too will praise him in the same way,' with the words beginning 'For that monk...' 'He thought thus' means he thought in the way that the teaching on the heritage of the Dhamma was about to be spoken. Therefore, he said the words beginning 'Just as...' 'Of one accord' means of the same intention. 'With wisdom' means with understanding. This was said because the Blessed One, saying 'This teaching is supreme,' thus extols the General of the Dhamma on account of his virtue.

Pakāsetvāti guṇato pākaṭaṃ paññātaṃ katvā sabbasāvakehi seṭṭhabhāve ṭhapetukāmo. Cittagatiyā cittavasena kāyassa pariṇāmanena “ayaṃ kāyo idaṃ cittaṃ viya hotū”ti kāyasamānagatikattādhiṭṭhānena. Kathaṃ pana kāyo dandhappavattiko lahuparivattena cittena [M 2.0077] samānagatiko hotīti? Na sabbathā samānagatiko. Yatheva hi kāyavasena cittavipariṇāmane cittaṃ sabbathā kāyena samānagatikaṃ hoti. Na hi tadā cittaṃ sabhāvasiddhena attano khaṇena avattitvā dandhavuttikassa rūpadhammassa khaṇena vattituṃ sakkoti, “idaṃ cittaṃ ayaṃ kāyo viya hotū”ti panādhiṭṭhānena dandhagatikassa kāyassa anuvattanato yāva icchitaṭṭhānappatti hoti, tāva kāyagatianulomeneva hutvā santānavasena pavattamānaṃ cittaṃ kāyagatiyā pariṇāmitaṃ nāma hoti, evaṃ “ayaṃ kāyo idaṃ cittaṃ viya hotū”ti adhiṭṭhānena pageva sukhalahusaññāya sampāditattā abhāvitiddhipādānaṃ viya dandhaṃ avattitvā yathā lahukatipayacittavāreheva icchitaṭṭhānappati hoti, evaṃ pavattarūpatā viññāyatīti.

'Having made it evident' means wishing to establish him in a state of supremacy over all disciples by making him manifest and known through his qualities. 'By the mind's movement' means by transforming the body according to the mind's inclination, with the determination that makes the body move in unison, as in 'May this body be like this mind.' But how can the body, which moves slowly, move in unison with the swiftly changing mind? Not entirely in unison. For just as when the mind is transformed according to the body, the mind moves entirely in unison with the body. For at that time, the mind, not proceeding by its own naturally established moment, is able to proceed by the moment of the material phenomenon, which has a slow movement. However, by the determination, 'May this mind be like this body,' by following the slow-moving body, the mind—having become in accordance with the body’s movement and proceeding as a continuum until the desired place is reached—is said to be transformed by the body’s movement. Thus, by the determination, 'May this body be like this mind,' because it is accomplished from the outset by the perception of ease and swiftness, it does not proceed slowly like those with undeveloped bases of psychic power, but the desired place is reached with just a few swift thought-moments; in this way, the nature of the proceeding body is understood.

Adhippāyānurūpameva tassa bhagavato thomanāya katattā. Idaṃ nāma atthajātaṃ bhagavā pucchissatīti pubbe mayā aviditaṃ apassaṃ. Āsayajānanatthanti “evaṃ byākarontena satthu ajjhāsayo gahito hotī”ti evaṃ satthu ajjhāsayajānanatthaṃ. Dutiyaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanto bhagavā paṭhamaṃ pañhaṃ anumodi dutiyaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanteneva paṭhamapañhavissajjanassa sampaṭicchitabhāvato.

Because the praise of that Blessed One was made in accordance with his intention. 'I did not previously know or see that the Blessed One would ask about this particular matter.' 'For the purpose of knowing his disposition' means for the purpose of knowing the Teacher's disposition, as in 'By answering thus, the Teacher’s disposition is grasped.' When asking the second question, the Blessed One approved the first question, because by the very act of asking the second question, his acceptance of the answer to the first question is established.

Etaṃ ahosīti etaṃ parivitakkanaṃ ahosi. Assāti kaḷārakhattiyassa bhikkhuno. Dhamme dahatīti dhammadhātu, sāvakapāramīñāṇaṃ, sāvakavisaye dhamme dahati yāthāvato ajite katvā ṭhapetīti attho. Tenāha “dhammadhātū”tiādi. Sabbaññutaññāṇagatikameva visaye. Gocaradhammeti gocarabhūte ñeyyadhamme.

'This was' means this thought occurred. 'His' refers to the monk Kaḷāra Khattiya. 'He places in the Dhamma' means the Dhamma-element, the knowledge of the disciple's perfections. The meaning is: he places the Dhamma in the sphere of the disciple, having established it as it truly is, unconquered. Therefore, he said 'the Dhamma-element,' etc. In its scope, it pertains only to the knowledge of omniscience. 'In the phenomena that are its resort' means in the knowable phenomena that are its resort.

Kaḷārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kaḷāra Sutta is concluded.

3. Ñāṇavatthusuttavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Ñāṇavatthu Sutta.

33. Ñāṇameva ñāṇavatthu sampattīnaṃ kāraṇabhāvato. Catūsūti catusaccassa bodhanavasena vuttesu catūsu ñāṇesu. Paṭhamanti “jarāmaraṇe ñāṇa”nti evaṃ vuttaṃ ñāṇaṃ, yena dhāraṇaparicayamanasikāravasena [V 2.0067] pavattaṃ sabbaṃ gaṇhi. Sannicayañāṇamayaṃ savanamayaṃ nāmatveva veditabbaṃ. Sabhāvato [M 2.0078] paccayato cassa pariggaṇhanañāṇaṃ sammasanañāṇaṃtveva veditabbaṃ. Jarāmaraṇasīsena cettha jarāmaraṇavantova dhammā gahitā. Paṭivedhañāṇanti asammohato paṭivijjhanañāṇaṃ. Iminā dhammenāti hetumhi karaṇavacanaṃ. Imassa hi dhammassa adhigamahetu ayaṃ ariyo atītānāgate nayenapi catusaccadhamme abhisambujjhati. Maggañāṇameva pana atītānāgate nayanasadisaṃ katvā dassetuṃ “maggañāṇadhammena vā”ti dutiyavikappo vutto. Evañhi “akālika”nti samatthitaṃ hoti.

33. Knowledge itself is the basis of knowledge, since it is the cause for the attainment of accomplishments. “Four” refers to the four knowledges mentioned in relation to the realization of the Four Noble Truths. “First” means the knowledge stated as “knowledge of aging and death,” by which everything that occurs through the practice of retention, familiarity, and attention is comprehended. This should be understood as knowledge consisting of accumulation and listening. From the perspective of its nature and condition, it should be understood as the knowledge of grasping and the knowledge of thorough scrutiny. Here, with aging and death as the head, only phenomena possessing aging and death are grasped. “Knowledge of penetration” is the knowledge of penetrating without delusion. “By this Dhamma” is an instrumental case indicating cause. For it is by the realization of this Dhamma that this noble one fully awakens to the Dhamma of the Four Truths, even with respect to the past and future by this method. However, to show that the knowledge of the path is similar to the method concerning the past and the future, the second alternative “or by the Dhamma which is the knowledge of the path” is stated. Thus, the term “immediate” is appropriately established.

Ñāṇacakkhunā diṭṭhenāti dhammacakkhubhūtena ñāṇacakkhunā asammohapaṭivedhavasena paccakkhato diṭṭhena. Paññāya viditenāti maggapaññāya tatheva viditena. Yasmā tathā diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sabbaso pattaṃ mahāupāyo hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ “pariyogāḷhenā”ti. Diṭṭhenāti vā dassanena, dhammaṃ passitvā ṭhitenāti attho. Viditenāti cattāri saccāni viditvā pākaṭāni katvā ṭhitena. Akālikenāti na kālantaravipākadāyinā. Pattenāti cattāri saccāni patvā ṭhitattā dhammaṃ pattena. Pariyogāḷhenāti catusaccadhamme pariyogāhitvā ṭhitena. Atītānāgate nayaṃ netīti atīte ca anāgate ca nayaṃ neti harati peseti. Idaṃ pana paccavekkhaṇañāṇassa kiccaṃ, satthārā pana maggañāṇaṃ atītānāgate nayanasadisaṃ kataṃ taṃmūlakattā. Atītamaggassa hi paccavekkhaṇaṃ nāma hoti, tasmā maggañāṇaṃ nayanasadisaṃ kataṃ nāma hoti, paccavekkhaṇañāṇena pana nayaṃ neti. Tenāha “ettha cā”tiādi. Yathā pana tena nayaṃ neti. Taṃ ākāraṃ dassetuṃ “ye kho kecī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ettha ca nayanuppādanaṃ nayañāṇasseva pavattiviseso. Tena vuttaṃ “paccavekkhaṇañāṇassa kicca”nti. Kiñcāpi “imināti maggañāṇadhammena vā”ti vuttaṃ, duvidhaṃ pana maggaphalañāṇaṃ sammasanañāṇapaccavekkhaṇāya mūlakāraṇaṃ, na nayanassāti duvidhena ñāṇadhammenāti na na yujjati. Tathā catusaccadhammassa ñātattā maggaphalasaṅkhātassa vā dhammassa saccapaṭivedhasampayogaṃ gatattā “nayanaṃ hotū”ti tena “iminā dhammenā”ti ñāṇassa visayabhāvena ñāṇasampayogena tadañātenāti ca attho na na yujjati. Anuayeti dhammañāṇassa anurūpavasena aye bujjhanañāṇe diṭṭhānaṃ adiṭṭhānayanato adiṭṭhassa diṭṭhatāya ñāpanato ca. Tenāha “dhammañāṇassa anugamane ñāṇa”nti. Khīṇāsavassa sekkhabhūmi nāma aggamaggakkhaṇo[M 2.0079]. Kasmā panetaṃ evaṃ vuttanti ce? “Evaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ pajānātī”tiādinā vattamānavasena desanāya pavattattā.

“Seen with the eye of wisdom” means seen directly with the eye of wisdom, which has become the eye of Dhamma, through penetration without delusion. “Known with wisdom” means known likewise with the wisdom of the path. Because what is thus seen and known is fully attained and is the great means, it is therefore said “by thorough penetration.” Or, “Seen” means by seeing, having seen the Dhamma and being established—this is the meaning. “Known” means having known and made evident the four truths and being established. “Timeless” means not giving a result after a lapse of time. “Attained” means having attained the Dhamma, because of having reached the four truths and being established. “By thorough penetration” means having thoroughly investigated the Dhamma of the Four Truths and being established. “He leads the method concerning the past and the future” means he carries and sends forth the method concerning the past and the future. This, however, is the function of reviewing knowledge; but by the Teacher, path knowledge is made similar to leading concerning the past and future because it is rooted in that. For the reviewing of the past path is what is called reviewing; therefore path knowledge is said to be made similar to leading, but one leads the method with reviewing knowledge. Therefore he said “here also,” and so on. Just as he leads the method, to show that mode, it is said “whatever ones,” and so on. Here, the production of the method is a particular instance of the knowledge of the method. Therefore it is said “the function of reviewing knowledge.” Although it is said “by this Dhamma which is the knowledge of the path,” nevertheless, the twofold knowledge of path and fruit is the root cause for the knowledge of comprehension and reviewing, not for the method—thus it is not unsuitable to say “by the twofold Dhamma of knowledge.” And because the Dhamma of the Four Truths is known, or because the Dhamma called path and fruit has reached connection with the penetration of the truths, “let there be the method”—thus “by this Dhamma,” by being the object of knowledge, by connection with knowledge, and by what is known by that—this meaning is not unsuitable. “Follows” means, in accordance with the knowledge of Dhamma, in the way of awakening knowledge, from leading the unseen from the seen, and from making the unseen known as seen. Therefore he said “the knowledge that follows upon the knowledge of Dhamma.” The moment of the highest path is called the stage of the learner for one whose taints are destroyed. But why is this said thus? Because the teaching proceeds by way of the present tense, as it is said “thus he understands aging and death,” and so on.

Ñāṇavatthusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Bases of Knowledge is finished.

4. Dutiyañāṇavatthusuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Second Discourse on the Bases of Knowledge

34. Sattarīti [V 2.0068] ta-kārassa ra-kārādesaṃ vuttaṃ. Sattatisaddena vā samānattho sattarisaddo. Byañjanarucivasena byañjanaṃ bhaṇantīti byañjanabhāṇakā. Tenāha “bahubyañjanaṃ katvā”tiādi. Tiṭṭhati tattha phalaṃ tadāyattavuttitāyāti ṭhiti, paccuppannalakkhaṇassa dhammassa ṭhiti dhammaṭṭhiti. Atha vā dhammoti kāraṇaṃ, paccayoti attho. Dhammassa yo ṭhitisabhāvo, sova dhammato añño natthīti dhammaṭṭhiti, paccayo. Tattha ñāṇaṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ. Tenāha āyasmā dhammasenāpati – “paccayapariggahe paññā dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇa”nti (paṭi. ma. mātikā 4). Tathā cāha “paccayākāre ñāṇa”ntiādi. Tattha dhammānanti paccayuppannadhammānaṃ. Pavattiṭṭhitikāraṇattāti pavattisaṅkhātāya ṭhitiyā kāraṇattā. “Jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa”ntiādinā addhattaye anvayabyatirekavasena pavattiyā chabbidhassa ñāṇassa. Khayo nāma vināso, sova bhedoti. Virajjanaṃ palujjanaṃ. Nirujjhanaṃ antaradhānaṃ. Ekekasminti jarāmaraṇādīsu ekekasmiṃ. Pubbe “yathābhūtañāṇa”nti taruṇavipassanaṃ āha. Tasmā idhāpi dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ vipassanāti gahetvā “vipassanāpaṭivipassanā kathitā”ti vuttaṃ.

34. In 'sattari', it is stated that the letter 'ta' is substituted by 'ra'. Or the word 'sattari' has the same meaning as 'sattati'. Those who recite consonants out of a liking for consonants are called 'reciters of consonants'. Hence he said, 'having made much of consonants,' and so forth. The fruit remains there, its occurrence being dependent on that, thus it is 'ṭhiti' (stability). The stability of a phenomenon with the characteristic of the present is 'dhammaṭṭhiti' (the stability of phenomena). Alternatively, 'dhamma' means cause, and the meaning is 'condition'. The inherent stability of a phenomenon, that itself is not other than the phenomenon, is 'dhammaṭṭhiti', a condition. The knowledge of this is 'dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇa' (knowledge of the stability of phenomena). Therefore, the Venerable Dhammasenāpati said: 'Wisdom in comprehending conditions is knowledge of the stability of phenomena' (Paṭisambhidāmagga, Mātikā 4). Similarly, he also said: 'knowledge in the mode of conditions,' and so forth. Here, 'of phenomena' means of phenomena arisen from conditions. Because it is the cause of the stability called 'occurrence', of the sixfold knowledge of occurrence by way of sequence and reversal in the three times, as in 'With birth as condition, aging and death,' and so forth. 'Destruction' means ruin; that itself is 'breaking up'. 'Fading away' is decaying. 'Ceasing' is disappearance. 'In each instance' means in each of aging and death, and so forth. Previously, by 'knowledge as it really is' he referred to immature insight. Therefore, here too, taking 'dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇa' as insight, it is said, 'Insight and counter-insight have been discussed.'

Dutiyañāṇavatthusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Discourse on the Bases of Knowledge is concluded.

5. Avijjāpaccayasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Discourse on Ignorance as a Condition

35. Desanaṃ osāpesīti yathāraddhakathaṃ ṭhapesi. Tattha nisinnassa diṭṭhigatikassa laddhiyā bhindanavasena upari kathetukāmo. Buddhānañhi desanāvāraṃ pacchindāpetvā pucchituṃ samattho nāma koci natthi. Tenāha “diṭṭhigatikassa okāsadānattha”nti. Duppañho eso sattūpaladdhiyā pucchitattā[M 2.0080]. Sattūpaladdhivādapadenāti “satto jīvo upalabbhatī”ti evaṃ pavattadiṭṭhidīpakapadavasena. Vadanti etenāti vādo. Diṭṭhi-saddo pana dvayasaṅgahito, brahmacariyavāso pana paramatthato ariyamaggabhāvanāti āha “ariyamaggavāso”ti. Ayaṃ diṭṭhīti anaññe sarīrajīvāti diṭṭhi. “Jīvo”ti ca jīvitameva vadanti. Vaṭṭanti duvidhaṃ vaṭṭaṃ. Nirodhentoti anuppattidhammataṃ āpādento. Samucchindantoti appavattiyaṃ pāpanena upacchindanto. Tadetaṃ maggena nirodhetabbaṃ vaṭṭaṃ nirujjhatīti yojanā. “Ayaṃ satto vināsaṃ abhāvaṃ patvā sabbaso ucchijjatī”ti evaṃ ucchedadiṭṭhiyā gahitākārassa sambhave saccabhāve sati. Na hotīti sātthako na hoti.

35. “He ended the discourse” means he set aside the talk that had been commenced. There, he wished to speak further in order to break the doctrine of the one seated there who held a view. For no one is capable of interrupting the Buddhas’ turn to teach and asking a question. Therefore, he said, 'for the sake of giving an opportunity to one holding a view.' This is a difficult question because it was asked based on the apprehension of a being. By 'a statement based on the doctrine of the apprehension of a being' is meant by way of the phrase that illuminates the view that arises thus: 'a being, a living soul, is apprehended.' They speak by means of this, hence it is called a 'doctrine' (vādo). The word 'view,' however, comprises two aspects. But living the holy life, in the ultimate sense, is the cultivation of the noble path; hence he said 'the dwelling of the noble path.' This view is the view that the body and the living being are not different. And 'jīvo' they call simply 'life.' 'They revolve' means the two kinds of round. 'Ceasing' means bringing about the state of non-arising. 'Cutting off' means eradicating by bringing about non-occurrence. The connection is that this round, which is to be ceased by the path, ceases. If the mode grasped by the annihilation view—'This being, having reached destruction and non-existence, is completely annihilated'—were to exist and be true, then the statement 'it is not' would mean 'it is not purposeful'.

Gacchatīti [V 2.0069] sarīrato nikkhamitvā gacchati. Vivaṭṭentoti appavattiṃ karontoti attho. Vivaṭṭetuṃ na sakkoti niccassa appavattiṃ pāpetuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā. Micchādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhiṃ vijjhati asamāhitapuggalasevanavasena tathā pavattituṃ appadānavasena ca pajahitabbāpajahanavasena sammādiṭṭhiṃ vijjhati. Visūkamivāti kaṇḍako viya. Na kevalaṃ ananuvattakova, atha kho virodhopi “nicca”ntiādinā pavattanadhammatāya viññāpanato. Virūpaṃ bībhacchaṃ phanditaṃ vipphanditaṃ. Paṇṇapupphaphalapallavānaṃ avatthubhūto tālo eva tālāvatthu “asive sivā”ti vohāro viya. Keci pana “tālavatthukatānī”ti paṭhanti, avatthubhūtatāya tālo viya katānīti attho. Tenāha “matthakacchinnatālo viyā”ti. Anuabhāvanti vināsaṃ.

'Gacchati' means departing from the body and going. 'Vivaṭṭento' means causing non-occurrence; that is the meaning. It cannot turn away because it is impossible to bring about the non-occurrence of what is permanent. Wrong view pierces right view by way of associating with unconcentrated individuals, by not giving an opportunity for it to arise in that way, and by not abandoning what ought to be abandoned. 'Visūkamiva' means like a thorn. Not only is it non-conforming, but it is also contradictory because it makes known the nature of occurrence by saying 'permanent,' and so forth. 'Virūpaṃ' is deformed; 'bībhacchaṃ' is repulsive; 'phanditaṃ' is trembling; 'vipphanditaṃ' is quivering. The palm tree, which is without a basis for leaves, flowers, fruits, and shoots, is 'tālāvatthu,' just like the expression 'the inauspicious as auspicious.' Some, however, read 'tālavatthukatāni,' meaning made like a palm tree because it is without a basis. Therefore, it is said, 'like a palm tree with its head cut off.' 'Anuabhāvanti' means destruction.

Avijjāpaccayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Avijjāpaccaya Sutta is concluded.

6. Dutiyaavijjāpaccayasuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Second Avijjāpaccaya Sutta.

36. Iti vāti evaṃ vā. Jarāmaraṇassa ceva jarāmaraṇasāmikassa ca khaṇavasena yo vadeyya. Avisāradadhātuko pucchituṃ acchekatāya maṅkubhāvena jāto. Tenāha “pucchituṃ na sakkotī”ti.

36. 'Iti vā' means 'or thus,' or 'in this way.' If one were to speak by way of the moment of aging and death, and of the owner of aging and death. He became embarrassed due to his lack of skill in asking, being of an unconfident disposition. Therefore, it is said, 'he is not able to ask.'

Dutiyaavijjāpaccayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Avijjāpaccaya Sutta is concluded.

7. Natumhasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Natumha Sutta.

37. Na [M 2.0081] tumhākanti kāyassa anattaniyabhāvadassanameva panetanti yā tassa anattaniyatā, taṃ dassetuṃ “attani hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yadi na attaniyaṃ, parakiyaṃ nāma siyāti, tampi natthīti dassento “nāpi aññesa”nti āha. Nayidaṃ purāṇakammamevāti “idaṃ kāyo”ti vuttasarīraṃ purāṇakammameva na hoti. Na hi kāyo vedanāsabhāvo. Paccayavohārenāti kāraṇopacārena. Abhisaṅkhatantiādi napuṃsakaliṅgavacanaṃ. Purimaliṅgasabhāgatāyāti “purāṇamidaṃ kamma”nti evaṃ vuttapurimanapuṃsakaliṅgasabhāgatāya. Aññamaññābhimukhehi samecca paccayehi kato abhisaṅkhatoti āha “paccayehi katoti daṭṭhabbo”ti. Abhisañcetayitanti tathā abhisaṅkhatattasaṅkhātena abhimukhabhāvena cetayitaṃ pakappitaṃ, pavattitanti attho. Cetanāvatthukoti cetanāhetuko. Vedaniyanti vedanāya hitaṃ vatthārammaṇabhāvena vedanāya paccayabhāvato. Tenāha “vedaniyavatthū”ti.

37. “Not yours” (Na tumhākaṃ) is simply to show the body’s nature of not belonging to oneself. And to show that nature of not belonging to oneself, it is said, “for if it were self…” (attani hi) and so forth. If it does not belong to oneself, it might belong to others—showing that this too is not the case, he said, “nor does it belong to others” (nāpi aññesaṃ). “This is not merely old kamma” (Na yidaṃ purāṇakammameva): The body, spoken of as “this body,” is not merely old kamma. For the body is not of the nature of feeling. “By way of conditions” (paccayavohārena) means through the figurative use of ‘cause’ (kāraṇopacārena). “Fabricated” (abhisaṅkhataṃ) and so on are in the neuter gender. “Because of sharing the nature of the preceding gender” (purimaliṅgasabhāgatāya) means because of sharing the nature of the previously mentioned neuter gender, as in “this is old kamma” (purāṇamidaṃ kammaṃ). On “fabricated” (abhisaṅkhata): it is made by conditions that have come together and converged; thus he said, “it should be seen as made by conditions” (paccayehi kato ti daṭṭhabbo). “Intentionally produced” (abhisañcetayitaṃ) means it is intended, arranged, and set in motion by way of its being fabricated; that is the meaning. “Having volition as its ground” (cetanāvatthuko) means caused by volition (cetanāhetuko). “To be felt” (vedaniyaṃ) means conducive to feeling, as it serves as the basis and object for feeling, being a condition for feeling. Hence he said, “a basis for feeling” (vedaniyavatthu).

Natumhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Natumha Sutta is concluded.

8. Cetanāsuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Cetanā Sutta.

38. Yañcāti [V 2.0070] ettha ca-saddo aṭṭhāne. Tena cetanāya viya pakappānānusayānampi viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā vakkhamānaṃyeva avisiṭṭhaṃ ārammaṇabhāvaṃ joteti. Kāmaṃ tīsupi padesu “pavatteti”icceva attho vutto, vattanattho pana cetanādīnaṃ yathākkamaṃ cetayanapakappanānusayanarūpo visiṭṭhaṭṭho daṭṭhabbo. Tebhūmakakusalākusalacetanā gahitā kammaviññāṇassa paccayaniddhāraṇametanti. Taṇhādiṭṭhikappā gahitā yathārahanti adhippāyo. Aṭṭhasupi hi lobhasahagatacittesu taṇhākappo, tattha catūsveva diṭṭhikappoti. Kāmaṃ anusayā lokiyakusalacetanāsupi anusentiyeva, akusalesu pana pavatti pākaṭāti “dvādasannaṃ cetanāna”nti vuttaṃ. Sahajātakoṭiyāti idaṃ paccuppannāpi kāmarāgādayo anusayāva vuccanti taṃsadisatāyāti vuttaṃ. Na hi kālabhedena lakkhaṇappabhedo atthīti. Anāgatā eva hi kāmarāgādayo nippariyāyato “anusayā”ti vattabbataṃ arahanti. Paccayuppanno [M 2.0082] vaṭṭatīti āha “ārammaṇaṃ paccayo”ti. Kammaviññāṇassa ṭhitatthanti kammaviññāṇasseva pavattiyā. Tasmiṃ paccaye satīti tasmiṃ cetanāpakappanānusayasaññite paccaye sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti. Santāne phaladānasamatthatāyeva hotīti “patiṭṭhā hoti, tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite”ti vuttaṃ. Sanniṭṭhāpakacetanāvasena viruḷheti. Patiṭṭhiteti hi iminā kammassa katabhāvo vutto, “viruḷhe”ti iminā upacitabhāvo. Tenāha “kammaṃ javāpetvā”tiādi. Tattha puretaraṃ uppannāhi kammacetanāhi laddhapaccayattā balappattāya sanniṭṭhāpakacetanāya kammaviññāṇaṃ laddhapatiṭṭhaṃ viruḷhamūlañca hotīti vuttaṃ “nibbattamūle jāte”ti. Tathā hi sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā vipākaṃ dentaṃ anantare jātivasena deti upapajjavedanīyakammanti.

38. In 'yañca,' the particle 'ca' is out of place. By it, the undifferentiated state of being an object for the stability of consciousness, which will be described, is illuminated for planning and latent tendencies as well, just as for volition. Although in all three instances the meaning is stated simply as 'it sets in motion' (pavatteti), the specific meaning of this setting in motion should be seen distinctly for volition and so on, in sequence, as having the forms of intending, planning, and lying latent. The wholesome and unwholesome volitions of the three realms are taken; this is the determination of the condition for kamma-consciousness. The intention is that craving, views, and planning are taken as appropriate. Indeed, in all eight types of consciousness accompanied by greed, there is the planning of craving; but in only four of them is there the planning of views. Although latent tendencies do indeed lie latent even in worldly wholesome volitions, their occurrence is manifest in unwholesome states—hence, it is said, 'of the twelve volitions.' Regarding 'in the co-nascent category' (sahajātakoṭiyā): by this it is said that even present greed and so on are called 'latent tendencies' because of their similarity. For there is no difference in characteristic based on a difference in time. Indeed, only future greed and so on unequivocally deserve to be called 'latent tendencies' (anusayā). 'The conditionally arisen revolves' (paccayuppanno vaṭṭati); thus, he said, 'the object is a condition' (ārammaṇaṃ paccayo). 'For the stability of kamma-consciousness' (kammaviññāṇassa ṭhitatthaṃ) means for the occurrence of kamma-consciousness. 'When that condition exists' (tasmiṃ paccaye sati) means when that condition designated as volition, planning, and latent tendency exists, consciousness has a support. It exists only as the capacity to give fruit in the continuity—thus, it is said, 'it has a support; when it is established' (patiṭṭhā hoti, tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite). 'It grows' (viruḷhe) means through decisive volition. By 'established' (patiṭṭhite), the fact that the kamma has been done is stated; by 'grows' (viruḷhe), the fact that it has been accumulated is stated. Hence he said, 'having impelled the kamma' (kammaṃ javāpetvā) and so forth. There, it is said that kamma-consciousness has gained a support and its root has grown strong through the decisive volition which has become powerful, having obtained its condition from the kamma-volitions that arose earlier. Thus it is said, 'when the root has been produced and has arisen' (nibbattamūle jāte). For decisive volition, when giving its result, gives it by way of arising immediately after; this is kamma to be experienced upon rebirth.

Tebhūmakacetanāyāti tebhūmakakusalākusalacetanāya. Appavattanakkhaṇoti idha pavattanakkhaṇo jāyamānakkhaṇo. Na jāyamānakkhaṇo appavattanakkhaṇo na kevalaṃ bhaṅgakkhaṇo appahīnānusayassa adhippetattā. Appahīnakoṭiyāti asamucchinnabhāvena. Tadidaṃ tebhūmakakusalākusalacetanāsu appavattamānāsu anusayānaṃ sahajātakoṭiādinā pavatti nāma natthi, vipākādīsu appahīnakoṭiyā pavattati karontassa abhāvatoti imamatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Avāritattāti paṭipakkheti avāritabbattā. Paccayova hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.

‘By volition pertaining to the three realms’ (tebhūmakacetanāya) means by wholesome and unwholesome volition pertaining to the three realms. ‘The moment of non-occurrence’ (appavattanakkhaṇo): here, the moment of occurrence is the moment of arising. The moment of non-occurrence is not the moment of arising, nor is it only the moment of dissolution, because what is intended is the state of one whose latent tendencies have not been abandoned. ‘In the category of the unabandoned’ (appahīnakoṭiyā) means in the state of not being eradicated. This is said with reference to the following meaning: when wholesome and unwholesome volitions pertaining to the three realms are not occurring, there is no occurrence of the latent tendencies by way of the co-nascent category and so on; it occurs in results and so on in the category of the unabandoned, because there is no doer. ‘Because of being unrestrained’ (avāritattā) means because of not being restrained by a counteragent. It is simply a condition for the stability of consciousness.

Paṭhamadutiyavārehi vaṭṭaṃ dassetvā tatiyavāre “no ce”tiādinā vivaṭṭaṃ dassitanti “paṭhamapade tebhūmakakusalākusalacetanā nivattā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha nivattāti akaraṇato appavattiyā [V 2.0071] apagatā. Taṇhādiṭṭhiyo nivattāti yojanā. Vuttappakāresūti “tebhūmakavipākesū”tiādinā vuttappakāresu.

Having shown the round of existence (vaṭṭaṃ) with the first and second sections, in the third section the ending of the round (vivaṭṭaṃ) is shown with 'if not' (no ce) and so forth. Thus, it is said, 'In the first phrase, the wholesome and unwholesome volitions relating to the three realms have ceased' (paṭhamapade tebhūmakakusalākusalacetanā nivattā), and so forth. Here, 'have ceased' (nivattā) means they are gone due to non-doing and non-occurrence. The construction is: craving and views have ceased. 'Among the types mentioned' (vuttappakāresu) means among the types mentioned as 'in the resultants of the three realms' (tebhūmakavipākesu) and so forth.

Etthāti imasmiṃ sutte. Ettha cetanāpakappanānaṃ pavattanavasena dhammaparicchedo dassitoti “cetetīti tebhūmakakusalākusalacetanā gahitā”tiādinayo idheva hotīti dassito. Catassoti paṭighadvayamohamūlasamāgatā catasso akusalacetanā. Catūsu akusalacetanāsūti yathāvuttāsu eva catūsu akusalacetanāsu, itarā pana “na pakappetī”ti iminā paṭikkhepena nivattāti. Sutte āgataṃ vāretvāti “no ca pakappetī”ti evaṃ paṭikkhepavasena [M 2.0083] sutte āgataṃ vajjetvā. “Na pakappetī”ti hi iminā aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatacittesu sahajātakoṭiyā pavattaanusayo nivattito tesaṃ cittānaṃ appavattanato, tasmā taṃ ṭhānaṃ ṭhapetvāti attho. Purimasadisova purimanayesu vuttanayena gahetabbo dhammaparicchedattā.

'Herein' (ettha) means in this Sutta. Herein, the delimitation of phenomena is shown by way of the occurrence of volition and planning. Thus, it is shown that the method beginning, ''He intends' (ceteti): here the wholesome and unwholesome volitions of the three realms are taken,' applies only here. 'Four' (catasso) means the four unwholesome volitions associated with the two types of aversion and with the root of delusion. 'In the four unwholesome volitions' (catūsu akusalacetanāsu) means in just the four unwholesome volitions as stated; the others are turned back by this negation, 'he does not plan' (na pakappeti). 'Having excluded what is in the Sutta' (sutte āgataṃ vāretvā) means having set aside what is in the Sutta by way of negation, as in 'and he does not plan' (no ca pakappeti). For by 'he does not plan' (na pakappeti), the latent tendency that occurs in the co-nascent category in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed is turned back, due to the non-occurrence of those consciousnesses; therefore, the meaning is 'having set that case aside.' It is just like the preceding; it should be understood according to the method stated in the preceding sections, because it is a delimitation of phenomena.

Tadappatiṭṭhiteti samāsabhāvato vibhattilopo, sandhivasena da-kārāgamo, tassa appatiṭṭhitaṃ tadappatiṭṭhitaṃ, tasmiṃ tadappatiṭṭhiteti evamettha samāsapadasiddhi daṭṭhabbā. Etthāti etasmiṃ tatiyavāre arahattamaggassa kiccaṃ kathitaṃ sabbaso anusayanibbattibhedanato. Khīṇāsavassa kiccakaraṇantipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati sabbaso vedanādīnaṃ paṭikkhepabhāvato. Nava lokuttaradhammātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati maggapaṭipāṭiyā anusayasamugghāṭanato maggānantarāni phalāni, tadubhayārammaṇañca nibbānanti. Viññāṇassāti kammaviññāṇassa. Punabbhavasīsena anantarabhavasaṅgahitaṃ nāmarūpaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇameva vā gahitanti āha “punabbhavassa ca antare eko sandhī”ti. Bhavajātīnanti ettha “dutiyabhavassa tatiyabhave jātiyā”ti evaṃ paramparavasena gahetabbaṃ. Āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattigahaṇena pana nānantariyato kammabhavo gahito, jātihetuphalasiddhipettha vuttā evāti veditabbaṃ. Ettha ca “no ce, bhikkhave, ceteti no ca pakappeti, atha kho anusetī”ti evaṃ bhagavatā dutiyanaye pubbabhāge bhavanibbattakakusalākusalāyūhanaṃ, pakappanañca vināpi bhavesu diṭṭhādīnavassa yogino anusayapaccayā vipassanācetanāpi paṭisandhijanakā hotīti dassanatthaṃ kusalākusalassa appavatti cepi, tadā vijjamānatebhūmakavipākādidhammesu appahīnakoṭiyā anusayitakilesappaccayā bhavavajjassa kammaviññāṇassa patiṭṭhitatā hotīti dassanatthañca vutto. “Na ceteti pakappeti anusetī”ti ayaṃ nayo na gahito cetanaṃ vinā pakappanassa abhāvato.

“It is unestablished” (tadappatiṭṭhite): Here, the elision of the case ending is due to the compound nature, and the addition of the letter ‘d’ is due to euphonic combination. “That which is unestablished” is tadappatiṭṭhitaṃ, and “in that which is unestablished” is tasmiṃ tadappatiṭṭhite. Thus, the formation of the compound word should be understood here. “Herein” (ettha) means in this third section, the function of the path to arahantship is explained as the complete destruction of the arising of latent tendencies. It is also proper to say that the task of one whose defilements are destroyed is done, due to the complete rejection of feelings and so forth. It is also proper to say that there are nine supramundane states because, following the sequence of the path, the latent tendencies are uprooted, the fruits follow immediately after the path, and both have Nibbāna as their object. “Of consciousness” (viññāṇassa) refers to kamma-consciousness. The name-and-form included in the immediately following existence, or rebirth-linking consciousness itself, is taken under the heading of future existence—hence he said, “There is one link between one existence and the next.” “Of births in existence” (bhavajātīnaṃ): Here, it should be understood sequentially as “the birth in the third existence from the second existence.” However, by the mention of the production of a future new existence, kamma-existence is not taken as immediately following; it should be understood that the establishment of the cause and effect of birth is stated here. Here, the Blessed One stated in the second method, in the earlier part, “If, bhikkhus, one does not intend, and does not plan, but rather has latent tendencies.” This was stated to show that even without the wholesome and unwholesome accumulation that generates existence, and without planning, for a meditator who sees the danger in existences, insight volition can still produce rebirth-linking due to the condition of latent tendencies. And it was stated to show that even if wholesome and unwholesome states are inactive, then, due to the defilements that are latent tendencies in the unrelinquished category among the existing resultant states of the three realms and so forth, the kamma-consciousness, which is faulty in existence, becomes established. The method “one does not intend, one plans, and one has latent tendencies” is not taken here because, without volition, planning is impossible.

Cetanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Cetanā Sutta is concluded.

9. Dutiyacetanāsuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Second Discourse on Intention

39. Viññāṇanāmarūpānaṃ [V 2.0072][M 2.0084] antare eko sandhīti hetuphalasandhi viññāṇaggahaṇena kammaviññāṇassa gahitattā. Nāmarūpaṃ pana vipākanāmarūpamevāti pākaṭameva. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

39. Between consciousness and name-and-form there is one connection, namely, the cause-and-effect connection, because kamma-consciousness is comprised by the term 'consciousness'. Name-and-form, however, is clearly only resultant name-and-form. The rest is easily understood.

Dutiyacetanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Discourse on Intention is concluded.

10. Tatiyacetanāsuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Third Discourse on Intention

40. Rūpādīsu chasu ārammaṇesu. Tena cettha bhavattayaṃ saṅgaṇhāti chaḷārammaṇapariyāpannattā. Tasseva bhavattayassa patthanā paṇidhānādivasena nati nāma. Āgatimhi gatīti paccupaṭṭhānavasena abhimukhaṃ gati pavatti etasmāti āgati, kammādinimittaṃ. Tasmiṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇassa gati pavatti nibbatti hoti. Tenāha “āgate”tiādi. Cutūpapātoti cavanaṃ cuti, maraṇaṃ. Upapajjanaṃ nibbatti, upapāto. Cutito upapāto punaruppādo. Tenāha “evaṃ viññāṇassā”tiādi. Itoti nibbattabhavato. Tatthāti punabbhavasaṅkhāte āyatibhave. Ekova sandhīti eko hetuphalasandhi eva kathito.

40. 'Rūpādīsu chasu ārammaṇesu': In the six objects such as form. 'Tena cettha bhavattayaṃ saṅgaṇhāti chaḷārammaṇapariyāpannattā': By that, it here encompasses the three existences because it is included in the six objects. 'Tasseva bhavattayassa patthanā paṇidhānādivasena nati nāma': The inclination towards that very triple existence, in the sense of aspiration, resolution, and so on, is called ‘nati’. 'Āgatimhi gatīti paccupaṭṭhānavasena abhimukhaṃ gati pavatti etasmāti āgati, kammādinimittaṃ': 'Movement in the coming' (`āgatimhi gati`). `Āgati` is that from which there is a forward movement or occurrence in the sense of its appearance; it is the sign of kamma and so on. 'Tasmiṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇassa gati pavatti nibbatti hoti': In that, the movement, occurrence, or production of rebirth-linking consciousness happens. 'Tenāha ‘‘āgate’’tiādi': Hence it is said, “in the coming,” etc. 'Cutūpapātoti cavanaṃ cuti, maraṇaṃ. Upapajjanaṃ nibbatti, upapāto. Cutito upapāto punaruppādo': 'Passing away and arising' (`cutūpapāta`). Passing away (`cavanaṃ`) is `cuti`, death. Arising (`upapajjanaṃ`) is production (`nibbatti`), `upapāta`. Arising from passing away is re-arising. 'Tenāha ‘‘evaṃ viññāṇassā’’tiādi': Hence it is said, “thus of consciousness,” etc. 'Itoti nibbattabhavato': 'From this' means 'from the existence that has arisen.' 'Tatthāti punabbhavasaṅkhāte āyatibhave': 'There' means 'in the future existence designated as renewed becoming.' 'Ekova sandhīti eko hetuphalasandhi eva kathito': 'A single link' means 'only a single link of cause and effect is spoken of.'

Tatiyacetanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Third Discourse on Intention is concluded.

Kaḷārakhattiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kaḷārakhattiya Section is concluded.

5. Gahapativaggo

5. The Householder Chapter

1. Pañcaverabhayasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on the Five Fears and Animosities

41. Yatoti yasmiṃ kāle. Ayañhi to-saddo dā-saddo viya idha kālavisayo. Tenāha “yadā”ti. Bhayaveracetanāyoti bhāyitabbaṭṭhena bhayaṃ, verapasavanaṭṭhena veranti ca laddhanāmā cetanāyo. Pāṇātipātādayo hi yassa pavattanti, yañca uddissa pavattiyanti, ubhaye sabhayabheravāti te eva bhāyitabbabhayaverajanakāvāti. Sotassa ariyamaggassa ādito paṭṭhāya paṭipattiadhigamo sotāpatti[M 2.0085], tadatthāya tattha patiṭṭhitassa ca aṅgāni sotāpattiyaṅgāni, tadubhayaṃ [V 2.0073] sandhāyāha “duvidhaṃ sotāpattiyā aṅga”nti, sotāpattiatthaṃ aṅganti attho. Yaṃ pubbabhāgeti yaṃ sayaṃ sotāpattimaggaphalapaṭilābhato pubbabhāge tadatthāya saṃvattati. Kiṃ pana tanti āha “sappurisasaṃsevo”tiādi. Sappurisānaṃ buddhādīnaṃ ariyañāṇasaññāṇajātā payirupāsanā, saddhammassavanaṃ catusaccadhammassavanaṃ, yoniso upāyena aniccādito manasi karaṇaṃ yoniso manasikāro, ussukkāpentena dhammassa nibbānassa anudhammapaṭipajjanaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipattīti etāni sotāpattiyā aṅgāni. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana sotāpattiaṅganti padaṃ apekkhitvā “evaṃ āgata”nti vuttaṃ. Ṭhitassa puggalassa aṅgaṃ. Sotāpanno aṅgīyati ñāyati etenāti sotāpannassa aṅgantipi vuccati. Idaṃ pacchā vuttaṃ aṅgaṃ. Dosehi ārakāti ariyoti āha “niddoso”ti. Kathaṃ avijjā saṅkhārānaṃ paccayotiādinā kenacipi anupārambhiyattā nirupārambho. Ñāṇaṃ sandhāya “niddoso”ti vuttaṃ, paṭiccasamuppādaṃ sandhāya “nirupārambho”ti vadanti. Ubhayampi pana sandhāya ubhayaṃ vuttanti apare. Paṭiccasamuppādo ettha adhippeto. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “aparāparaṃ uppannāya vipassanāpaññāyā”ti. Na hi maggañāṇaṃ vipassanāpaññāti. Sammā upāyattā tassa paṭiccasamuppanne yāthāvato ñāyatīti ñāyo, paṭiccasamuppādo. Ñāṇaṃ pana ñāyati so etenāti ñāyo.

41. 'Yatoti yasmiṃ kāle.' 'Yato' means 'at the time when.' 'Ayañhi to-saddo dā-saddo viya idha kālavisayo.' Here, the suffix '-to' (in 'yato') signifies a temporal sense, like the suffix '-dā.' 'Tenāha ‘‘yadā’’ti.' Hence, it is said, 'yadā.' 'Bhayaveracetanāyoti bhāyitabbaṭṭhena bhayaṃ, verapasavanaṭṭhena veranti ca laddhanāmā cetanāyo.' 'Bhayaveracetanāyo' refers to intentions that have obtained the name 'fear' because they are to be feared, and 'hostility' because they generate enmity. 'Pāṇātipātādayo hi yassa pavattanti, yañca uddissa pavattiyanti, ubhaye sabhayabheravāti te eva bhāyitabbabhayaverajanakāvāti.' Indeed, those intentions for acts like killing living beings, for whom they occur and with reference to whom they occur, both are fearful and terrifying; thus, they are producers of fear and hostility that should be feared.
