Idāneva kho mayantiādi heṭṭhā paccayuppannaṃ anāloḷentena dassetvā desanā āhaṭā, na aññamaññapaccayatāvasena, idha pana yenādhippāyena taṃ āloḷetvā nivattetvā kathitaṃ mahātherena, tamevassa adhippāyaṃ teneva pakāsetukāmo mahākoṭṭhikatthero āha “idāneva kho maya”ntiādi. Tenāha “idaṃ thero”tiādi.

67. In the seventh sutta, 'Why does he ask?'—the intention is, why does the Elder Mahākoṭṭhika ask, being himself free from doubt on that point? 'To understand the intention'—this too, for that great disciple, would be no special feat through his knowledge of others' minds. Therefore, not being fully satisfied with that, he says 'moreover' and so on. Here, 'two chief disciples' means the foremost disciples in virtues such as morality. For the Elder Mahākoṭṭhika had not attained the characteristics of a chief disciple, but rather had attained the characteristics of a great disciple. 'Just now, indeed, we,' and so on—the teaching was presented by showing the dependently arisen phenomena below without analyzing them, not by way of mutual conditionality. Here, however, the Elder Mahākoṭṭhika, wishing to reveal that very intention with which the Great Elder had considered, reflected upon, and spoken, said, 'Just now, indeed, we,' and so on. Therefore, it is said, 'this elder,' and so on.

Ettake ṭhāneti “kiṃ nu kho āvuso”tiādinā paṭhamārambhato paṭṭhāya yāva “nirodho hotī”ti padaṃ, ettake ṭhāne. Avijjāsaṅkhāre aggahetvā “nāmarūpapaccayā viññāṇa”nti desanāya pavattattā “paccayuppannapañcavokārabhavavasena desanā kathitā”ti vuttaṃ. “Phale gahite kāraṇaṃ gahitamevā”ti viññāṇe gahite saṅkhārā, tesañca kāraṇabhūtā avijjā gahitā eva hotīti vuttaṃ “heṭṭhā vissajjitesu dvādasasu padesū”ti. Ekekasminti ekekasmiṃ pade. Tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vasenāti “nirodhāya dhammaṃ desesi, nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, nirodhā anupādāvinimutto hotī”ti evamāgatānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vārānaṃ vasena. “Aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhī”tiādīsu [V 2.0105] (mahāva. 468) viya idha vatthusaddo kāraṇapariyāyoti āha “chattiṃsāya kāraṇehī”ti. Paṭhamo anumodanāvidhi. Dhammakathikaguṇoti vipassanāvisayo abhedopacārena vutto. Sesadvayesupi eseva nayo. Dutiyo anumodanā, tatiyaṃ anumodananti abhidheyyānurūpaṃ vattabbaṃ. Desanāsampatti kathitā “nibbidāya…pe… dhammaṃ desetī”ti vuttattā. Sekkhabhūmi kathitā “nibbidāya…pe… paṭipanno hotī”ti vuttattā. Asekkhabhūmi kathitā “nibbidā …pe… anupādāvimutto hotī”ti vuttattā.

'At this point' refers to the section from the initial beginning, 'What now, friend?' and so on, up to the word 'cessation occurs.' Since the teaching proceeds with 'consciousness is conditioned by name-and-form' without taking ignorance and formations, it is said, 'The teaching is explained by way of the dependently arisen five-constituent existence.' 'When the fruit is grasped, the cause is also grasped'—thus, when consciousness is grasped, formations are grasped, and their cause, ignorance, is also grasped. This is stated 'in the twelve points explained earlier.' 'Ekekasmiṃ' means in each point. 'In sets of three' refers to the three phrases that come thus: 'he teaches the Dhamma for cessation, he practices for cessation, he is liberated without clinging through cessation.' As in 'by eighteen grounds' and so on (Mahāva. 468), here the word 'vatthu' is a synonym for 'cause,' hence it is said, 'by thirty-six causes.' The first is the method of appreciation. 'The qualities of a Dhamma teacher' refers to the domain of insight, stated by a figure of speech based on identity. The same principle applies to the remaining two. The second appreciation, the third appreciation—these should be spoken in accordance with what is to be expressed. The perfection of the teaching is stated, because it is said, 'he teaches the Dhamma for disenchantment…' The stage of a trainee is stated, because it is said, 'he practices for disenchantment…' The stage of one beyond training is stated, because it is said, 'through disenchantment… he is liberated without clinging…'

Naḷakalāpīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Naḷakalāpī Sutta is concluded.

8. Kosambisuttavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Kosambi Sutta

68. Aṭṭhame [M 2.0122] parassa saddahitvāti parassa vacanaṃ saddahitvā. Tenāha “yaṃ esa bhaṇati, taṃ bhūtanti gaṇhātī”ti. Parapattiyo hi eso paraneyyabuddhiko. Yaṃ kāraṇanti yaṃ attanā cintitavatthu. Ruccatīti “evametaṃ bhavissati, na aññathā”ti attano matiyā cintentassa ruccati. Ruciyā gaṇhātīti parapattiyo ahutvā sayameva tathā rocento gaṇhāti. Anussavoti “anu anu suta”nti evaṃ cirakālagatāya anussutiyā labbhamānaṃ “kathamidaṃ siyā, kasmā bhūtameta”nti anussavena gaṇhāti. Vitakkayatoti “evametaṃ siyā”ti parikappentassa. Ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ upaṭṭhātīti yathāparikappitavatthu cittassa upaṭṭhāti. Ākāraparivitakkenāti attanā kappitākārenā taṃ gaṇhāti. Ekā diṭṭhi uppajjatīti “yathāparikappitaṃ kiñci atthaṃ evametaṃ, nāññathā”ti abhinivisantassa eko abhiniveso uppajjati. Yāyassāti yāya diṭṭhiyā assa puggalassa. Nijjhāyantassāti paccakkhaṃ viya nirūpetvā cintentassa. Khamatīti tathā gahaṇakkhamo hoti. Tenāha “so…pe… gaṇhātī”ti. Etānīti saddhādīni. Tāni hi saddheyyānaṃ vatthūnaṃ gahaṇahetubhāvato “kāraṇānī”ti vuttāni. Bhavanirodho nibbānanti navavidhopi bhavo nirujjhati ettha etasmiṃ adhigateti bhavanirodho, nibbānaṃ. Svāyaṃ bhavo pañcakkhandhasaṅgaho tabbinimutto natthīti āha “pañcakkhandhanirodho nibbāna”nti. Bhavanirodho nibbānaṃ nāmāti “nibbānaṃ nāma bhavanirodho”ti esa pañho sekkhehipi jānitabbo, na asekkheheva. Imaṃ ṭhānanti imaṃ yāthāvakāraṇaṃ.

68. In the eighth sutta, 'believing another' means believing the words of another. Hence it is said, 'Whatever he says, he takes it as true.' For he is one who relies on others, one whose wisdom is guided by others. 'Whatever reason' means a matter one has considered oneself. 'It is agreeable' means that to one who thinks with one's own mind, 'It will be thus, not otherwise,' it is agreeable. 'He accepts by inclination' means that without being one who relies on others, he himself, approving in that way, accepts it. 'Hearsay' means 'heard again and again'; thus, what is obtained through long-standing tradition, he accepts by that tradition, thinking, 'How could this be? Why is this true?' 'To one who ponders' means to one who conjectures, 'It must be like this.' 'A reason appears' means the matter as conjectured appears to the mind. 'By pondering the aspect' means one accepts it according to the aspect one has conceived. 'A single view arises' means a single adherence arises in one who insists, 'Whatever matter was conceived is thus, not otherwise.' 'Yāyassa' means: by which view for that person. 'To one who reflects' means to one who thinks, having examined it as if directly perceived. 'It is agreeable' means he is capable of accepting it in that way. Hence it is said, 'He... accepts it.' 'These' refers to faith and the rest. For these are called 'reasons' because they are the causes for accepting matters worthy of faith. 'The cessation of existence is Nibbāna' means that the ninefold existence ceases here, in this attainment; thus, the cessation of existence is Nibbāna. This existence is the collection of the five aggregates; there is nothing apart from it. Thus he says, 'The cessation of the five aggregates is Nibbāna.' 'The cessation of existence is called Nibbāna' means 'Nibbāna is called the cessation of existence.' This question should be understood by trainees as well, not only by those beyond training. 'This ground' means this reason according to reality.

Suṭṭhu diṭṭhanti “bhavanirodho nibbāna”nti mayā suṭṭhu yāthāvato diṭṭhaṃ, bhavassa pīḷanasaṅkhatasantāpavipariṇāmaṭṭhānaṃ, bhavanirodhassa ca nissaraṇavivekāsaṅkhatāmataṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya [V 2.0106] diṭṭhattā. Anāgāmiphale ṭhito hi anāgāmimagge ṭhito eva nāma uparimaggassa anadhigatattāti vuttaṃ “anāgāmimagge ṭhitattā”ti. Nibbānaṃ ārabbha pavattampi therassetaṃ ñāṇaṃ “nibbānaṃ paccavekkhatī”ti vuttañāṇaṃ viya na hotīti vuttaṃ “ekūnavīsatiyā…pe… paccavekkhaṇañāṇa”nti. Etena etaṃ nibbānapaccavekkhaṇā viya na hoti sappadesabhāvatoti dasseti. Evañca katvā idha udapānanidassanampi samatthitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Paccavekkhaṇañāṇenāti avasesakilesānaṃ, nibbānasseva [M 2.0123] vā paccavekkhaṇañāṇena. Upari arahattaphalasamayoti upari sijjhanato arahattapaṭilābho tathā atthi. “Yenāhaṃ taṃ pariyesato nibbānaṃ sacchikarissāmī”ti jānāti.

'Well seen' means: 'The cessation of existence is Nibbāna' has been well and truly seen by me, because the state of existence has been seen with perfect wisdom as it really is—as oppressive, conditioned, afflicted, and subject to change—and the cessation of existence has been seen as an escape, seclusion, the unconditioned, and the deathless. For one established in the fruit of non-return is indeed said to be established in the path of non-return because the higher path has not yet been attained—hence it is said, 'by being established in the path of non-return.' Even this knowledge of the elder that arises concerning Nibbāna is not like the knowledge described as 'he reviews Nibbāna'—thus it is said, 'with the nineteen... reviewing knowledges.' By this, it is shown that this is not like a review of Nibbāna due to its partial nature. And having done so, here too, the example of the well should be seen as fitting. 'By the reviewing knowledge' means by the reviewing knowledge of the remaining defilements, or of Nibbāna itself. 'Above, at the time of the fruit of arahantship' means that the attainment of arahantship exists in that way because of its accomplishment above. He knows, 'By this, when I seek it, I will realize Nibbāna.'

Kosambisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Kosambī Sutta Commentary is completed.

9. Upayantisuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Upayanti Sutta

69. Navame udakavaḍḍhanasamayeti sabbadivasesu mahāsamuddassa anto mahantacandakantamaṇipabbatānaṃ juṇhasamphassena pahatattā jalābhisandanavasena udakassa vaḍḍhanasamaye. Upari gacchantoti pakatiyā udakassa tiṭṭhaṭṭhānassa tato upari gacchantoti attho. Upari yāpetīti udakaṃ tattha uparūpari vaḍḍheti. Tathābhūto ca taṃ brūhento pūrentoti vuccatīti āha “vaḍḍheti pūretīti attho”ti. Yasmā paccayadhammā attano phalasamavāyapaccaye honte tassa upari ṭhito viya hoti tassa attano vase vattāpanato, tasmā vuttaṃ “avijjā upari gacchantī”ti. Paccayabhāvena hi sā tathā vuccati. Tenāha “saṅkhārānaṃ paccayo bhavituṃ sakkuṇantī”ti. Apagacchanto yāyanto. Tenāha “osaranto”ti, avaḍḍhanto parihīyamānoti attho.

69. In the ninth sutta, 'at the time of the water increasing' means at the time of the water increasing due to the flow of water, because on all days, the interior of the great ocean is struck by the touch of moonlight from great moonstone mountains. 'Going above' means going above the natural standing place of the water. 'It maintains above' means the water keeps increasing higher and higher there. And being such, augmenting and filling it, it is called so, hence it is said, 'It increases and fills—this is the meaning.' Because when causal phenomena are conditions for the aggregation of their result, it is as if they stand above it, making it proceed under their own control, therefore it is said, 'Ignorance rises above.' For it is called so due to its role as a condition. Hence it is stated, 'Being capable of being a condition for formations.' 'Going away, departing.' Hence it is stated, 'subsiding,' meaning decreasing and diminishing, not increasing.

Upayantisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Upayanti Sutta Commentary is finished.

10. Susimasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Susīma Sutta

70. Dasame garukatoti garubhāvahetūnaṃ uttamaguṇānaṃ matthakappattiyā anaññasādhāraṇena garukārena garukato. Mānitoti sammāpaṭipattiyā mānito. Tāya hi viññūnaṃ manāpatāti āha “manena piyāyito”ti. Catupaccayapūjāya ca pūjitoti idaṃ atthavacanaṃ. Yadatthaṃ saṃgītikārehi “tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sakkato hotī”tiādinā imassa suttassa nidānaṃ nikkhittaṃ, tassa atthassa ulliṅgavasena vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Esa nayo sesapadesupi. Aṃsakūṭatoti [V 2.0107][M 2.0124] uttarāsaṅgena ubho aṃsakūṭe paṭicchādetvā ṭhitā dakkhiṇaaṃsakūṭato, ubhayato vā apanenti. Paricitaganthavasena paṇḍitaparibbājako, yato pacchā visesabhāgī jāto. Vicittanayāya dhammakathāya kathanato “kaviseṭṭho”ti āhaṃsu.

70. In the tenth, 'highly esteemed' means esteemed due to the supreme qualities that are a cause for greatness, by reaching the pinnacle with a reverence not shared by others. 'Honored' means honored through proper conduct. For by that, one is pleasing to the wise, thus it is said, 'cherished by the mind.' 'And worshipped with the four requisites'—this is an explanatory statement. This meaning should be seen as stated by way of allusion to the purpose for which the compilers of the texts inserted the introduction to this sutta, 'At that time, the Blessed One was honored,' and so on. This principle applies to the remaining passages as well. 'From the shoulder-peak' means that having covered both shoulder-peaks with the upper robe, they uncover it from the right shoulder-peak, or from both. The learned wanderer, due to his familiarity with texts, later became a partaker of distinction. Because he delivered a Dhamma talk with varied methods, they called him 'the foremost of poets.'

Tejussadoti mahātejo. Purebhattakiccādīnaṃ niyatabhāvena niyamamanuyutto. Vipassanālakkhaṇamhīti ñāṇaṃ tattha kathitaṃ. Dhammanti tassaṃ tassaṃ parisāyaṃ therassa asammukhā desitaṃ dhammaṃ. Āharitvā katheti tathā varassa dinnattā.

'Abounding in splendor' means of great splendor. He is devoted to the discipline by the fixed nature of forenoon duties and so on. 'In the characteristic of insight': knowledge is spoken of there. 'Dhamma' refers to the Dhamma taught in each assembly in the Elder's absence. Having brought it, he speaks, because a boon was granted to that effect.

Kiñcāpi susimo pūraṇādayo viya satthupaṭiñño na hoti, titthiyehi pana “ayaṃ brāhmaṇapabbajito paññavā vedaṅgakusalo”ti gaṇācariyaṭṭhāne ṭhapito, tathā cassa sambhāvito. Tena vuttaṃ “ahaṃ satthāti paṭijānanto”ti, na sassatadiṭṭhikattā. Tathā hesa bhagavato sammukhā upagantuṃ asakkhi.

Although Susīma was not a professed teacher like Pūraṇa and others, he was placed in the position of a group leader by the sectarians, who esteemed him, saying, 'This brahmin renunciate is wise and skilled in the ancillary Vedic texts.' Thus, he was respected. Therefore, it is said, 'professing myself as a teacher,' not because he held the view of eternalism. For in that way he was able to approach the presence of the Blessed One.

Aññāti arahattassa nāmaṃ aññindriyassa ciṇṇante pavattattā. Taṃ pavattinti yaṃ aññabyākaraṇaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ sutvā. Assa susimassa, paramappamāṇanti uttamakoṭi. Ācariyamuṭṭhīti ācariyassa muṭṭhikatadhammo.

'Aññā' is a name for Arahantship, because it proceeds at the culmination of cultivating the faculty of final knowledge. 'They declare it' means they do so having heard the declaration of final knowledge that was spoken. For this Susīma, 'the highest measure' means the ultimate limit. 'Teacher's fist' refers to the teacher's closed-fist teaching.

Aṅgasantatāyāti nīvaraṇādīnaṃ paccanīkadhammānaṃ vidūrabhāvena jhānaṅgānaṃ vūpasantatāya. Nibbutasabbadarathapariḷāhatāya hi tesaṃ jhānānaṃ paṇītatarabhāvo. Ārammaṇasantatāyāti rūpapatibhāgavigamena saṇhasukhumādibhāvappattassa ārammaṇassa santabhāvena. Yadaggena hi tesaṃ bhāvanātisayasambhāvitasaṇhasukhumappakārāni ārammaṇāni santāni, tadaggena jhānaṅgānaṃ santatā veditabbā. Ārammaṇasantatāya vā tadārammaṇadhammānaṃ santatā lokuttaradhammārammaṇāhi paccavekkhaṇāhi dīpetabbā. Āruppavimokkhāti arūpajjhānasaññāvimokkhā. Paññāmatteneva vimuttā, na ubhatobhāgavimuttā. Dhammānaṃ ṭhitatā taṃsabhāvatā dhammaṭṭhiti, aniccadukkhānattatā, tattha ñāṇaṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇanti āha “vipassanāñāṇa”nti. Evamāhāti “pubbe kho, susima, dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ, pacchā nibbāne ñāṇa”nti evamādi.

'Tranquility of the factors' means due to the remoteness of the hindrances and other opposing states, and the pacification of the jhāna factors. For indeed, the superior quality of those jhānas lies in the quenching of all disturbances and afflictions. 'Tranquility of the object' refers to the tranquil nature of the object, which has attained qualities such as softness and subtlety through the disappearance of the counterpart sign of form. Indeed, to the extent that their meditation objects—developed through the excellence of cultivation—are tranquil in their soft and subtle aspects, to that extent the tranquility of the jhāna factors should be understood. Alternatively, the tranquility of the object can be explained as the tranquility of the phenomena related to that object, through reviewing with supramundane phenomena as objects. 'Formless liberations' refer to the liberations of perception in the formless jhānas. They are liberated solely through wisdom, not liberated in both ways. The stability of phenomena, their inherent nature, is the fixed state of phenomena – impermanence, suffering, and non-self. Knowledge of that is 'knowledge of the fixed state of phenomena,' which is called 'insight knowledge.' Thus it is said: 'First, Susīma, comes knowledge of the fixed state of phenomena, afterward knowledge of Nibbāna,' and so forth.

Vināpi [M 2.0125] samādhinti samathalakkhaṇappattaṃ purimasiddhaṃ vināpi samādhinti vipassanāyānikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Evanti vuttākārena. Na samādhinissando anupubbavihārā viya. Na samādhiānisaṃso [V 2.0108] lokiyābhiññā viya. Na samādhissa nipphatti sabbabhavaggaṃ viya. Vipassanāya nipphatti maggo vā phalaṃ vāti yojanā.

The phrase 'even without concentration' means without a previously accomplished concentration that has attained the characteristic of tranquility; this is said with reference to one who proceeds by way of insight. Thus, in the manner stated, it is not the result of concentration like the successive abidings. It is not a benefit of concentration like the mundane higher knowledges. It is not the accomplishment of concentration like the peak of all existence. The accomplishment of insight is the path or the fruit—this is the connection.

Rūpādīsu cetesu tiṇṇaṃ lakkhaṇānaṃ parivattanavasena desanā teparivaṭṭadesanā. Anuyogaṃ āropentoti nanu vuttaṃ, susima, idāni arahattādhigamena sabbaso paccayākāraṃ paṭivijjhitvā tattha vigatasammohoti anuyogaṃ karonto. Pākaṭakaraṇatthanti yathā tvaṃ, susima, nijjhānako sukkhavipassako ca hutvā āsavānaṃ khayasammasane suppatiṭṭhito, evametepi bhikkhū, tasmā “api pana tumhe āyasmanto”tiādinā na te tayā anuyuñjitabbāti.

The teaching concerning these things, such as form, given by way of the revolution of the three characteristics is the teaching with a triple revolution. Regarding 'imposing an interrogation': this refers to one who interrogates, thinking: 'Surely, Susīma, now that you have attained arahantship, have fully penetrated the structure of conditions in every respect, and are free from delusion in regard to it...' 'For the purpose of making it manifest' means: just as you, Susīma, being a reflective one and a dry-insight practitioner, are well-established in the comprehension of the destruction of the taints, so too are these monks. Therefore, they should not be interrogated by you with the phrase 'But do you, venerable ones,' and so on.

Susimasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Susīma Sutta Commentary is concluded.

Mahāvaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Mahāvagga Commentary is concluded.

8. Samaṇabrāhmaṇavaggo

8. The Chapter on Ascetics and Brahmins

1. Jarāmaraṇasuttādivaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Suttas beginning with the one on Aging and Death

71-72. Ekekaṃ suttaṃ katvā ekādasa suttāni vuttāni avijjāya vasena desanāya anāgatattā, tathānāgamanañcassā catusaccavasena ekekassa padassa uddhaṭattā. Kāmañca “āsavasamudayā avijjāsamudayo”ti attheva aññattha suttapadaṃ, idha pana veneyyajjhāsayavasena tathā na vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Eleven suttas were spoken, treating each as a single sutta, because the teaching had not yet been presented by way of ignorance, and because each term was analyzed in terms of the four truths with respect to that non-presentation. And although elsewhere there is indeed the sutta phrase, 'With the arising of the taints, there is the arising of ignorance,' here it was not spoken in that way, it should be understood, due to the disposition of those to be trained.

Jarāmaraṇasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Jarāmaraṇa Sutta and others is concluded.

Samaṇabrāhmaṇavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Chapter on Ascetics and Brahmins is concluded.

9. Antarapeyyālavaggo

9. The Chapter of Intermediate Expansion

1. Satthusuttādivaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Satthu Sutta and so forth.

73. Ayaṃ [V 2.0109][M 2.0126] satthā nāmāti ayaṃ ariyamaggassa atthāya sāsati vimuttidhammaṃ anusāsatīti satthā nāma. Adhisīlādivasena tividhāpi sikkhā. Yogoti bhāvanānuyogo. Chandoti niyyānetā kattukamyatākusalacchando. Sabbaṃ bhāvanāya parissayaṃ sahati, sabbaṃ vāssa upakārāvahaṃ sahati vāhetīti sabbasahaṃ. Appaṭivānīti na paṭinivattatīti appaṭivānī. Antarāya sahanaṃ mohanāsanavīriyaṃ ātappati kileseti ātappaṃ. Vidhinā īretabbattā pavattetabbattā vīriyaṃ. Satataṃ pavattiyamānabhāvanānuyogakammaṃ sātaccanti āha “satatakiriya”nti. Tādisamevāti yādisī sati vuttā, tādisameva ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇādivasena catusaccapariggāhakaṃ ñāṇanti attho.

73. ‘This is the Teacher’ means: because he teaches for the sake of the Noble Path and instructs in the Dhamma of liberation, he is called the Teacher. The threefold training is by way of higher virtue and so on. ‘Yoga’ is the application to development. ‘Chanda’ is the wholesome desire to act that leads out to liberation. He endures every danger of development, or he endures and bears all that is helpful to him—thus he is ‘all-enduring.’ ‘Undaunted’ means he does not turn back—thus he is ‘undaunted.’ ‘Zeal’ is the energy that endures obstacles and destroys delusion; it burns up the defilements. ‘Energy’ is so called because it should be stirred up and set going according to the method. ‘Persistence’ is the continuous action of applying oneself to development—thus it is called ‘constant activity.’ ‘Such knowledge’ means knowledge of the same kind as the mindfulness described, that is, the knowledge that comprehends the Four Noble Truths in terms of aging, death, and so on—this is the meaning.

Antarapeyyālavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Antarapeyyāla Vagga is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

The Sāratthappakāsinī, the Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Nidānasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The explanation of the subtle meaning in the commentary on the Nidānasaṃyutta is concluded.

2. Abhisamayasaṃyuttaṃ

2. The Connected Discourses on Penetration.

1. Nakhasikhāsuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Nakhasikhā Sutta.

74. Sukhumāti [V 2.0110][M 2.0127] taruṇā parittā kesaggamattabhāvato. Yathā kesā dīghaso dvaṅgulamattāya sabbasmiṃ kāle etappamāṇāva, na tacchindanaṃ, evaṃ nakhaggāpi kesaggamattāva, na tesaṃ chindanaṃ avaḍḍhanato. Paratoti “sahassimaṃ satasahassima”nti vuttaṭṭhāne. Abhisametvāti paṭivijjhitvā, tasmā abhisametāvino paṭividdhasaccassāti attho. Kāmaṃ purimapadaṃ dukkhakkhandhassa atītabhāvaṃ upādāyapi vattuṃ yuttaṃ. Puretaraṃyeva pana vuttabhāvaṃ upādāya vuttanti dassetuṃ “purimaṃ dukkhakkhandha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Purimaṃ nāma pacchimaṃ apekkhitvā. Purimapacchimatā hi taṃ taṃ upādāya vuccatīti idhādhippetaṃ purimaṃ nīharitvā dassetuṃ “katamaṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Atītampi parikkhīṇa”nti idhādhippetaṃ parikkhīṇameva vibhāvetuṃ “katamaṃ pana parikkhīṇa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Sotāpannassa dukkhakkhayo idha coditoti taṃ dassetuṃ “paṭhamamaggassa abhāvitattā uppajjeyyā”ti vatvā idāni taṃ sarūpato dassetuṃ puna “katama”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Sattasu attabhāvesu yaṃ apāye uppajjeyya aṭṭhamaṃ paṭisandhiṃ ādiṃ katvā yattha katthaci apāyesu cāti yaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjeyya, taṃ sabbaṃ parikkhīṇanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Assāti sotāpannassa, yaṃ parimāṇaṃ, tato uddhañca upapātaṃ atthīti adhippāyo. Mahā attho guṇo mahattho, so etassa atthīti mahatthiyo ka-kārassa ya-kāraṃ katvā. Tenāha “mahato atthassa nipphādako”ti.

74. `Sukhumā` means subtle, young, and limited, due to being the size of a hair-tip. Just as hairs are always about two finger-breadths long, of that measure, without being cut, so too the tips of the nails are the size of a hair-tip, without being cut, because they do not grow longer. `Parato`: in the place where 'a thousand, a hundred thousand' is mentioned. 'Having fully understood' means having penetrated; therefore, 'of one who has fully understood' means of one who has penetrated the truth. Indeed, it is appropriate that the former phrase refers to the past state of the mass of suffering. However, to show that it is said in reference to what was stated just before, 'the former mass of suffering,' etc., is said. 'Former' is said in relation to 'latter.' For 'former' and 'latter' are spoken of in relation to this or that. To extract and show what is intended here by 'former,' it is said, 'But what is...?' etc. Regarding 'The past is also exhausted'—to clarify what is intended here by 'exhausted,' it is said, 'But what is exhausted?' etc. Here the destruction of suffering for a stream-enterer is questioned. To explain this, having said 'it might arise because the first path has not been developed,' now, to explain it in its own terms, it is again said, 'But what...?' etc. Whatever suffering might arise in the lower realms during seven states of existence, and whatever suffering might arise anywhere in the lower realms starting from the eighth relinking—all that is to be seen as exhausted. `Assa` means 'of the stream-enterer.' The meaning is that whatever that measure is, beyond that there is still rebirth. A great benefit (`mahā attho`) is a great quality, hence `mahattho`. Because he possesses this, he is `mahatthiyo` (by changing 'ka' to 'ya'). Therefore, he says 'producer of great benefit'.

Nakhasikhāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Nakhasikhā Sutta is concluded.

2. Pokkharaṇīsuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Pokkharaṇī Sutta.

75. Ubbedhenāti avavedhena adhodisatāya. Tenāha “gambhīratāyā”ti.

75. Ubbedhena: by penetrating downwards, by being directed downwards. Therefore, he says 'by its depth'.

Pokkharaṇīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Pokkharaṇī Sutta is concluded.

3. Saṃbhejjaudakasuttādivaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Saṃbhejjaudaka Sutta and so forth.

76-77. Sambhijjaṭṭhāneti [V 2.0111][M 2.0128] sambhijjasamodhānagataṭṭhāne. Samenti sametā honti. Tenāha “samāgacchantī”ti. Pāḷiyaṃ vibhattilopena niddesoti tamatthaṃ dassento “tīṇi vā”ti āha. Sambhijjati missībhāvaṃ gacchati etthāti sambhejjaṃ, missitaṭṭhānaṃ. Tattha udakaṃ sambhejjaudakaṃ. Tenāha “sambhinnaṭṭhāne udaka”nti.

76-77. Sambhijjaṭṭhāne means in the place where coming together and mingling occur. "Samenti" means they come together. Therefore, it is said, "they converge." In the Pāḷi, it is stated by way of elision of the case ending; showing that meaning, he said, "three or..." etc. "Sambhijjati" means it goes to a state of mixing; therefore, the place of mixing is called "sambhejja," the mixed place. There, the water is "sambhejjaudaka," mixed water. Therefore, it is said, "water in a mixed place."

Saṃbhejjaudakasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Saṃbhejjaudaka Sutta and so forth is concluded.

4. Pathavīsuttādivaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Pathavī Sutta and so forth.

78-84. Cakkavāḷabbhantarāyāti cakkavāḷapabbatassa antogadhāya.

78-84. “Within the world-sphere” means inside the Cakkavāḷa Mountain.

Chaṭṭhādīsu vuttanayenevāti idha chaṭṭhasuttādīsu paṭhamasuttādīsu vuttanayenevāti attho veditabbo visesābhāvato.

Here, “by the method stated in the sixth and so forth” should be understood to mean “by the method stated in the first sutta and so forth,” since there is no difference.

Pariyosāneti imassa abhisamayasaṃyuttassa osānaṭṭhāne. Aññatitthiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇaparibbājakānanti aññatitthiyānaṃ. Guṇādhigamoti jhānābhiññāsahito guṇādhigamo. Satabhāgampi…pe… na upagacchati saccapaṭivedhassa mahānubhāvattā. Tenāha bhagavā paccakkhasabbadhammo “evaṃ mahādhigamo, bhikkhave, diṭṭhisampanno puggalo evaṃ mahābhiñño”ti.

'Pariyosāne' means at the concluding point of this Abhisamaya Saṃyutta. 'Of other sectarian ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers' refers to other sectarians. 'Attainment of virtues' means the attainment of virtues accompanied by jhānas and higher knowledges. 'Not even a hundredth part...' does not approach, owing to the great power of the penetration of the truth. Therefore, the Blessed One, who has directly realized all phenomena, said: 'Monks, a person accomplished in view has such a great attainment, such a great higher knowledge.'

Pathavīsuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Pathavī Sutta and so forth is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

The Sāratthappakāsinī, Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Abhisamayasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The explanation of the subtle meaning in the commentary on the Abhisamayasaṃyutta is completed.

3. Dhātusaṃyuttaṃ

3. The Connected Discourses on the Elements

1. Nānattavaggo

1. The Chapter on Diversity

1. Dhātunānattasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sutta on the Diversity of Elements.

85. Paṭhamanti [V 2.0112][M 2.0129] imasmiṃ nidānavagge saṃyuttānaṃ paṭhamaṃ saṃgītattā. Nissattaṭṭhasuññataṭṭhasaṅkhātenāti dhammamattatāya nissattatāsaṅkhātena niccasubhasukhaattasuññatatthasaṅkhātena. Sabhāvaṭṭhenāti yathābhūtasabhāvaṭṭhena. Tato eva sabhāvassa dhāraṇaṭṭhena dhātūti laddhanāmānaṃ. Nānāsabhāvo aññamaññavisadisatā dhātunānattaṃ. Cakkhusaṅkhāto pasādo cakkhupasādo. So eva cakkhanaṭṭhena cakkhu, nissattasuññataṭṭhena dhātu cāti cakkhudhātu. Cakkhupasādavatthuṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ katvā pavattaṃ cakkhupasādavatthukaṃ. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Dve sampaṭicchanamanodhātuyo, ekā kiriyā manodhātūti tisso manodhātuyo manodhātu “mananamattā dhātū”ti katvā. Vedanādayo…pe… nibbānañca dhammadhātu visesasaññāparihārena sāmaññasaññāya pavattanato. Tathā hete dhammā āyatanadesanāya “dhammāyatana”nteva desitā. Na hi nesaṃ rūpāyatanādīnaṃ viya viññāṇehi aññaviññāṇena gahetabbatākāro atthi. Sabbampīti chasattatividhaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ. Kāmāvacarā kāmadhātupariyāpannattā. Avasāne dveti dhammadhātumanoviññāṇadhātuyo. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana visuddhimagge taṃsaṃvaṇṇanāsu daṭṭhabbo.

85. 'First' is said because it is the first of the Saṃyuttas compiled in this Nidāna Vagga. 'Designated as having the meaning of non-being and emptiness' means designated as non-being by being mere phenomena, and designated as having the meaning of being empty of permanence, beauty, pleasure, and self. 'By their intrinsic nature' means by their true intrinsic nature. From that very fact, they are called 'elements' because of their characteristic of bearing their own nature. 'Diversity of elements' is diversity of nature, dissimilarity from one another. The sensitivity designated as 'eye' is eye-sensitivity. That very sensitivity is the 'eye' in the sense of seeing, and an 'element' in the sense of being without a being and empty; thus it is the 'eye-element.' That which arises having made the eye-sensitivity base its foundation is 'based on the eye-sensitivity base.' The same principle applies to the remaining terms. Two receiving mind-elements and one functional mind-element make three mind-elements; they are the 'mind-element' because they are 'elements that are mere minding.' Feelings and so on... and Nibbāna are the dhamma-element because they proceed by way of a general cognition, by abandoning specific cognitions. Thus, these phenomena are taught in the discourse on the sense bases only as the 'dhamma-base.' For unlike the form-base and others, they do not have the characteristic of being apprehended by one consciousness as distinct from another. 'All' refers to the seventy-six kinds of mind-consciousness. 'Pertaining to the sense-sphere' is said because they are included in the sense-sphere element. 'At the end, two' refers to the dhamma-element and the mind-consciousness-element. This is the summary here; the detailed explanation, however, should be seen in the Visuddhimagga and its sub-commentaries.

Dhātunānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sutta on the Diversity of Elements is concluded.

2. Phassanānattasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Sutta on the Diversity of Contact.

86. Jātipasutiārammaṇādibhedena nānābhāvo phasso. Jātipaccayabhedena hi paccayuppannassa bhedo hotiyeva. Dhammaparicchedavasena dhātudesanāyaṃ tisso mananamattā dhātuyova manodhātuyo. Kiriyāmayassa cittuppattivibhāgena paccayuppannassa vasena dhātudesanāyaṃ [M 2.0130] mananaṭṭhena dhātutāya [V 2.0113] sāmaññato manodvārāvajjanaṃ “manodhātū”ti adhippetanti vuttaṃ “manosamphasso manodvāre paṭhamajavanasampayutto”tiādi. Tasmāti yasmā kāmaṃ sampaṭicchanamanodhātuanantaraṃ uppajjamāno santīraṇaviññāṇadhātuyā sampayutto phassopi manosamphasso eva nāma, dubbalattā pana so sabbabhavesu asambhavato ca gahito anavasesato gahaṇaṃ na hotīti manodvāre javanasamphasso hoti, tasmā. Ayamettha atthoti ayaṃ idha adhippāyānugato attho.

86. Contact is diverse due to the distinctions of birth, origin, object, and so forth. For the diversity of the conditionally arisen is indeed due to the diversity of the originating condition. In the teaching on the elements, by way of the classification of phenomena, the three elements that are mere mentation are the mind-elements. In the teaching on the elements, in terms of the conditionally arisen by way of the division of the arising of functional consciousness, mind-door adverting is intended as 'mind-element' due to its commonality as an element by way of its meaning of 'minding.' Thus it is said, 'Mental contact is that associated with the first impulsion in the mind-door,' and so on. 'Therefore' means: although the contact arising immediately after the receiving mind-element and associated with the investigating consciousness-element is indeed named mental contact, yet because of its weakness and its non-occurrence in all states of existence, its inclusion is not exhaustive; therefore, it is the contact of impulsion in the mind-door that is meant. This is the meaning here; this is the meaning consistent with the intention in this context.

Phassanānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of Contact is concluded.

3. Nophassanānattasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Discourse on the Non-Diversity of Contact

87. Manosamphassaṃ paṭiccāti manodvāre paṭhamajavanasampayutto phasso manosamphasso, taṃ manosamphassaṃ paṭicca. Manodhātūti āvajjanakiriyamanodhātu. Manoviññāṇadhātu manodhātūti veneyyajjhāsayavasena vuttaṃ. Tenāha “manodvāre…pe… evamattho daṭṭhabbo”ti. Tathā hi vakkhati “sabbāni cetānī”tiādi.

87. 'Dependent on mental contact' means: the contact associated with the first impulsion at the mind-door is mental contact; dependent on that mental contact. 'Mind-element' means the functional mind-element of adverting. The mind-consciousness-element is called 'mind-element' according to the disposition of those to be trained. Hence, he said, 'At the mind-door... and so on... the meaning should be understood in this way.' For thus it will be stated, 'All these are classifications of the suttas,' and so on.

Nophassanānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Discourse on the Non-Diversity of Contact is concluded.

4. Vedanānānattasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of Feeling

88. Sabbāpi tasmiṃ dvāre vedanā vatteyyuṃ cakkhusamphassavedanā upanissayapaccayabhāvitā. Nibbattiphāsukatthanti nibbattiyā upanissayabhāvena pavattiyā dassanasukhatthaṃ. Sampaṭicchanavedanameva gahetuṃ vaṭṭati, tāya gahitāya itarāsaṃ gahaṇaṃ ñāyāgatamevāti. Vuttaṃ porāṇaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Āvajjanasamphassanti āvajjanamanosamphassaṃ. Anantarūpanissayabhūtaṃ paṭicca paṭhamajavanavasena uppajjatīti yojanā. Ayamadhippāyo upanissayassa adhippetattā.

88. All feelings at that door would occur—the feeling born of eye-contact, developed by way of a strong dependence condition. 'For the sake of ease of arising' means for the sake of ease in seeing the occurrence by way of a strong dependence for its arising. It is proper to take only the feeling of receiving; when that is taken, the inclusion of the others is logically implied. This is stated in the ancient commentary. 'Adverting-contact' means the mental contact of adverting. The construction is: it arises by way of the first impulsion, dependent on what has become an immediate and decisive support condition. This is the intention, because a decisive support condition is intended.

Vedanānānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of Feeling is concluded.

5. Dutiyavedanānānattasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Second Discourse on the Diversity of Feeling

89. Tatiyacatutthesu [M 2.0131] vuttanayāvāti “no cakkhusamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati cakkhudhātū”ti evaṃ vuttanayo, catutthe “cakkhudhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati cakkhusamphasso”tiādinā vuttanayo ca. Ekato katvāti ekajjhaṃ katvā desitā. Kasmā pana tesu suttesu evaṃ desanā pavattāti āha “sabbāni cetānī”tiādi. Paṭisedho pana tesaṃ vedanānānattādīnaṃ [V 2.0114] phassanānattādikassa paccayabhāvato tathāuppattiyā asambhavato. Ito paresūti “no pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānatta”ntiādīsu.

89. 'The method stated in the third and fourth' means: the method stated thus, 'The eye-element does not arise dependent on eye-contact,' and the method stated in the fourth, beginning, 'Monks, eye-contact arises dependent on the eye-element.' 'Having made into one' means they are taught having been combined. But why is the teaching set forth in this way in those discourses? He says, 'All these are classifications of the suttas,' and so on. The denial, however, is due to the impossibility of such an arising, since the diversity of contact and so on is the condition for the diversity of feeling and so on. 'In those that follow this' refers to suttas such as, 'The diversity of anguish does not arise dependent on the diversity of searching,' and so on.

Dutiyavedanānānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Second Discourse on the Diversity of Feeling is concluded.

6. Bāhiradhātunānattasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of External Elements

90. Pañca dhātuyo kāmāvacarā rūpasabhāvattā.

90. The five elements pertain to the sense sphere because they are of the nature of form.

Bāhiradhātunānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of External Elements is concluded.

7. Saññānānattasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of Perception

91. Āpāthe patitanti cakkhussa āpāthagataṃ sāṭakaveṭhanādisaññitaṃ bhūtasaṅghātaṃ sammā nissitaṃ. Cakkhudvāre sampaṭicchanādisampayuttasaññānaṃ saṅkappagatikattā, cakkhuviññāṇasampayuttasaññāgahaṇeneva vā gahetabbato “rūpasaññāti cakkhuviññāṇasampayuttā saññā”ti vuttaṃ tattha saññāya eva labbhanato. Eteneva hi taṃsampayutto saṅkappoti idampi saṃvaṇṇitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tenāha “saññāsaṅkappachandā ekajavanavārepi nānājavanavārepi labbhantī”ti. Javanasampayuttassa vitakkassa chandagatikattā vuttaṃ “tīhi cittehi sampayutto saṅkappo”ti. Chandikataṭṭhenāti chandakaraṇaṭṭhena, icchitaṭṭhenāti attho. Anuḍahanaṭṭhenāti pariḍahanaṭṭhena. Sannissayaḍāharasā hi rāgaggiādayo “rūpe”ti pana tassa ārammaṇadassanametaṃ. Pariḷāhoti pariḷāhasīsena apekkhaṃ vadati. Tenāha “pariḷāhe uppanne”tiādi. “Pariḷāho”ti daḷhajjhosānā [M 2.0132] balavākārappattā vuttāti āha “pariḷāhapariyesanā pana nānājavanavāreyeva labbhantī”ti. Tāsaṃ laddhūpanissayabhāvatoti dasseti. Iminā nayenāti “uppajjati saññānānatta”nti ettha vuttanayena attho veditabbo. “Rūpasaññādinānāsabhāvaṃ saññaṃ paṭicca kāmasaṅkappādinānāsabhāvo saṅkappo uppajjatī”tiādinā nayena veditabbo.

91. 'Fallen within the range' means: having entered the range of the eye, a mass of primary elements, rightly depended upon, designated as a cloth, a wrapping, and so on. Because perceptions associated with reception and so on at the eye-door have thought as their destination, or because it is to be grasped only by grasping the perception associated with eye-consciousness, it is said, 'Perception of form is the perception associated with eye-consciousness,' for it is obtained there by perception alone. By this, it should be understood that the thought associated with it is also explained. Hence he said, 'Perception, thought, and desire are found in a single impulsion process as well as in multiple impulsion processes.' Because the initial thought associated with the impulsion has desire as its destination, it is said, 'Thought is associated with three cittas.' 'By the meaning of being made into a desire' means by the meaning of making a desire; the meaning is 'by the meaning of being wished for.' 'By the meaning of burning' means by the meaning of scorching. For the fires of lust and so on have the nature of burning with a basis. 'In form,' however, is a demonstration of its object. 'Anguish' is spoken of with anguish as its main point. Hence he said, 'When anguish has arisen,' and so on. He says that 'anguish' is spoken of as strong adherence that has reached a powerful state, and therefore, 'But the searching that is anguish is found only in multiple impulsion processes.' This shows their state of having obtained a strong dependence condition. 'By this method' means the meaning should be understood by the method stated here: 'The diversity of perception arises.' It should be understood by the method beginning: 'Dependent on perception, which has diverse characteristics such as perception of form, thought arises with diverse characteristics such as sensual thought.'

Saññānānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of Perception is concluded.

8. Nopariyesanānānattasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of Searching (Negative Formulation)

92. Paṭisedhamattameva nānaṃ, sesaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayamevāti adhippāyo.

92. The diversity is merely the negation; the rest is just according to the method stated previously. Such is the intention.

Nopariyesanānānattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of Searching (Negative Formulation) is concluded.

9. Bāhiraphassanānattasuttādivaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Discourse on the Diversity of External Contact, and so on

93. Vuttappakāre [V 2.0115] ārammaṇeti “āpāthe patita”ntiādinā heṭṭhā vuttappakāre rūpārammaṇe. Saññāti rūpasaññāva. Arūpadhammopi samāno yasmiṃ ārammaṇe pavattati, taṃ phusanto viya hotīti vuttaṃ “ārammaṇaṃ phusamāno”ti. Taṇhāya vatthubhūtaṃyeva rūpārammaṇaṃ labbhatīti katvā “rūpalābho”ti adhippetanti āha “saha taṇhāya ārammaṇaṃ rūpalābho”ti. Sabbasaṅgāhikanayoti ekasmiṃyeva ārammaṇe sabbesaṃ saññādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ uppattiyā sabbasaṅgaṇhanavasena dassitanayo. Tenāha “ekasmiṃyevā”tiādi. Sabbasaṅgāhikanayoti vā dhuvaparibhogavasena nibaddhārammaṇanti vā āgantukārammaṇanti vā vibhāgaṃ akatvā sabbasaṅgāhikanayo. Aparo nayo. Missakoti āgantukārammaṇe nibaddhārammaṇe ca visayato nibaddhārammaṇena missako. Nibaddhārammaṇe sattānaṃ kileso mando hoti. Tathā hi saññāsaṅkappaphassavedanāva dassitā. Yaṃ kiñci viyāti yaṃ kiñci aññamaññaṃ viya. Khobhetvāti kutūhaluppādanavasena cittaṃ khobhetvā.

93. 'In an object of the kind stated' means: in a form-object of the kind stated previously, beginning with 'fallen into the range.' 'Perception' means just perception of form. Even though it is an immaterial phenomenon, when it occurs in an object, it is as if it were touching it; hence it is said, 'touching the object.' Because it is the form-object, which is the very basis for craving, that is obtained, 'acquisition of form' is intended; thus he says, 'together with craving, the object is the acquisition of form.' 'The all-encompassing method' means the method shown by way of completely gathering all phenomena, such as perception and so on, due to their arising in one single object. Hence he says, 'in just one,' and so on. Or, 'the all-encompassing method' is the method that is all-encompassing without making a distinction between a 'fixed object' by way of constant use, or an 'adventitious object.' Another method. 'Mixed' means: with respect to the domain, in the case of an adventitious object and a fixed object, it is mixed with the fixed object. In the case of a fixed object, the defilement of beings is weaker. Thus, indeed, perception, thought, contact, and feeling alone are shown. 'Like whatever' means like whatever other thing. 'Having agitated' means having agitated the mind by way of arousing curiosity.

Upāsikāti [M 2.0133] tassa amaccaputtassa bhariyaṃ sandhāyāha. Tasminti āgantukārammaṇe. Lābho nāma “labbhatī”ti katvā.

'Laywoman' (Upāsikā): he said this referring to the wife of that minister's son. 'In that' refers to an adventitious object. 'Acquisition' (lābho) is so named because 'it is acquired'.

Uruvalliyavāsīti uruvalliyaleṇavāsī, uruvalliyavihāravāsīti vadanti. Pāḷiyāti “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjatī”tiādinayapavattāya imissā suttapāḷiyā. Parivaṭṭetvāti majjhe gahitaphassavedanāpariyosāne ṭhapanavasena pāḷiṃ parivaṭṭetvā. Vuttappakāretiādi parivattetabbākāradassanaṃ. Tattha vuttappakāreti āpāthagatarūpārammaṇe. Avibhūtavāranti avibhūtārammaṇavāraṃ. Ayameva vā pāṭho. Gaṇhanti kathenti. Ekajavanavārepi labbhanti cirataranivesābhāvā. Nānājavanavāreyeva daḷhataranivesatāya.

The dweller at Uruvelā—they say, the dweller in the Uruvelā cave, or the dweller in the Uruvelā monastery. In the Pāli text—of this discourse's Pāli text which proceeds in the manner of 'Monks, dependent on the diversity of elements, arises...'. Having turned it around—by turning around the Pāli, placing it at the end after taking contact and feeling in the middle. 'As stated,' etc., is a demonstration of the manner in which it should be turned around. Therein, 'as stated' means in a form-object that has come into range. 'The section on the unclear' means the section on the unclear object. Or, this is the reading itself. They grasp and state it. Even in a single impulsion-sequence, they are obtainable due to the absence of a more lasting establishment. It is only in a sequence of diverse impulsions that there is a firmer establishment.

94. Dasamaṃ uttānameva navame vuttanayattā. Paṭisedhamattameva hettha nānattanti.

94. The tenth is simply clear, following the method stated in the ninth. Here, the only diversity is the negation.

Bāhiraphassanānattasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Discourse on the Diversity of External Contacts, and so on, is completed.

Nānattavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the chapter on diversity is completed.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Sattadhātusuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on the Seven Elements

95. Ābhātīti [V 2.0116] ābhā, ālokabhāvena nipphajjati, upaṭṭhātīti vā attho. So eva nijjīvaṭṭhena dhātūti ābhādhātu. Ālokassāti ālokakasiṇassa. Suṭṭhu, sobhanaṃ vā bhātīti subhaṃ. Kasiṇasahacaraṇato jhānaṃ subhaṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Suparisuddhavaṇṇaṃ kasiṇaṃ. Ākāsānañcādayopi subhārammaṇaṃ evāti keci. Desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesīti desanaṃ uddesamatte eva ṭhapesi. Pāḷiyaṃ “andhakāraṃ paṭicca paññāyatī”ti etthāpi ārammaṇameva gahitaṃ, tathā “ayaṃ dhātu asubhaṃ paṭicca paññāyatī”ti etthāpi. Yathā hi idha suvaṇṇaṃ kasiṇaṃ subhanti adhippetaṃ, evaṃ dubbaṇṇaṃ asubhanti.

95. 'It shines' means light; it is produced as illumination, or the meaning is 'it appears.' That itself, in the sense of being lifeless, is an element; hence, the light-element. 'Of light' means of the light kasiṇa. 'It shines well or beautifully,' thus it is 'beautiful' (subha). Because of its association with the kasiṇa, the jhāna is 'beautiful.' The rest is just as was stated. The kasiṇa is of supremely pure color. Some say that the attainment of the base of infinite space, and so on, also have a beautiful object. 'He concluded the teaching' means he established the teaching merely as a topic heading. In the Pāli text, in the phrase 'it is discerned in dependence on darkness,' here too only the object is taken. Similarly, in 'this element is discerned in dependence on the unattractive,' here too. For just as here the golden kasiṇa is intended as 'beautiful,' so the discolored one is 'unattractive'.

Andhakāraṃ paṭiccāti andhakāraṃ paṭicchādakapaccayaṃ paṭicca. Paññāyatīti pākaṭo hoti. Tenāha “andhakāro hī”tiādi. Ālokopi, andhakārena [M 2.0134] paricchinno hotīti yojanā. Andhakāro tāva ālokena paricchinno hotu “yattha āloko natthi, tattha andhakāro”ti āloko kathaṃ andhakārena paricchinno hotīti āha “andhakārena hi so pākaṭo hotī”ti. Paricchedalekhāya viya cittarūpaṃ andhakārena hi parito paricchinno hutvā paññāyati, yathā taṃ chāyāya ātapo. Eseva nayoti asubhasubhānaṃ aññamaññaparicchinnataṃ atidisitvā tattha adhippetameva dassento “asubhe sati subhaṃ paññāyatī”ti āha. Evamāhāti “asubhaṃ paṭicca subhaṃ paññāyatī”ti avoca. “Rūpī rūpāni passatī”tiādīsu viya uttarapadalopenāyaṃ niddesoti āha “rūpaṃ paṭiccāti rūpāvacarasamāpattiṃ paṭiccā”ti. Tāya hi sati adhigatāya. Rūpasamatikkamā vā hotīti sabhāvārammaṇānaṃ rūpajjhānānaṃ samatikkamā ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpatti nāma hotīti attho. Eseva nayoti iminā “ākāsānañcāyatanasamatikkamā viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpatti nāma hotī”tiādinā dvepi pakāre atidisati. Paṭisaṅkhāti paṭisaṅkhāñāṇena. Appavattinti yathāparicchinnakālaṃ appavattanaṃ. Etena khaṇanirodhādiṃ paṭikkhipati.

'Depending on darkness' means depending on darkness as a concealing condition. 'Is discerned' means it becomes manifest. Therefore, he said, 'For darkness indeed,' and so on. Light, too, is delimited by darkness—this is the connection. Let it be that darkness is delimited by light, as in 'Where there is no light, there is darkness'; but how is light delimited by darkness? He said, 'For through darkness it becomes manifest.' For, being delimited on all sides by darkness, it is discerned like a painting with an outline, just as sunlight is by shadow. 'This is the method': having extended this to the mutual delimitation of the unattractive and the beautiful, showing the intended meaning therein, he said, 'When the unattractive exists, the beautiful is discerned.' Thus he said: he spoke of 'depending on the unattractive, the beautiful is discerned.' He said that this is a designation by way of eliding the latter term, as in such phrases as 'One with form sees forms'; thus, 'depending on form' means 'depending on the form-sphere attainment.' For when that has been attained... 'Or there is the transcending of form' means that the transcending of the form-jhānas, which have their own nature as object, is what is called the attainment of the base of infinite space. 'This is the method': by this he extends it to both cases, as in 'By transcending the base of infinite space, what is called the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness arises,' and so on. 'He reflects' means with the knowledge of reflection. 'Non-occurrence' means non-occurrence for a defined period of time. By this he rejects momentary cessation and so on.

Kathaṃ samāpatti pattabbāti imāsu sattasu dhātūsu kā pakārā saññāsamāpatti nānā hutvā samāpajjitabbā. Tenāha “kīdisā samāpattiyo”tiādi. Saññāya atthibhāvenāti paṭukiccāya [V 2.0117] saññāya atthibhāvena. Sukhumasaṅkhārānaṃ tattha samāpattiyaṃ avasissatāya. Nirodhovāti saṅkhārānaṃ nirodho eva.

'How is the attainment to be attained?' In these seven elements, what kind of perception-attainment is to be attained in diverse ways? Therefore, he said, 'What are the kinds of attainments?' and so on. 'By the existence of perception' means by the existence of keen perception. Because of the remainder of subtle formations in that attainment. 'Or cessation' means the cessation of formations itself.

Sattadhātusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Seven Elements is concluded.

2. Sanidānasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Sanidāna Sutta

96. Bhāvanapuṃsakametaṃ “visamaṃ candimasūriyā parivattantī”tiādīsu (a. ni. 4.70) viya. Sanidānanti attano phalaṃ nidadātīti nidānaṃ, kāraṇanti āha “sanidāno [M 2.0135] sappaccayo”ti. Kāmapaṭisaṃyuttoti kāmarāgasaṅkhātena kāmena paṭisaṃyutto vā kāmapaṭibaddho vā. Takketīti takko. Abhūtakāraṃ samāropetvā kappetīti saṅkappo. Ārammaṇe cittaṃ appetīti appanā. Visesena appetīti byappanā. Ārammaṇe cittaṃ abhiniropentaṃ viya pavattatīti cetaso abhiniropanā. Micchā viparīto pāpako saṅkappoti micchāsaṅkappo. Aññesu ca kāmapaṭisaṃyuttesu vijjamānesu vitakko eva kāmadhātusaddena niruḷho daṭṭhabbo vitakkassa kāmapasaṅgappattisātisayattā. Esa nayo byāpādadhātuādīsupi. Sabbepi akusalā dhammā kāmadhātu hīnajjhāsayehi kāmetabbadhātubhāvato.

96. This is a neuter [noun] indicating an abstract state, as in 'unevenly the moon and sun revolve' (Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.70). 'With a cause' (sanidāna): because it lays down its own fruit, it is a cause (nidāna); it is a reason. Thus he said, 'with a cause, with a condition.' 'Connected with sensual desire' means connected with or bound to sensuality, which is characterized as sensual lust. 'One reasons,' thus it is reasoning (takka). 'One forms a thought, having superimposed an unreal quality,' thus it is conception (saṅkappa). 'One applies the mind to an object,' thus it is application (appanā). 'One applies it in a special way,' thus it is special application (byappanā). 'It proceeds as if implanting the mind in an object,' thus it is the implanting of the mind (cetaso abhiniropanā). 'A conception that is wrong, perverse, and evil,' thus it is 'wrong conception.' And although other things connected with sensual desire exist, it should be understood that thought (vitakka) itself is established by the word 'sensual-element' because thought is exceedingly prone to sensual attachment. This is the method for the element of ill will, and so on, as well. All unwholesome states are the sensual-element because they are elements to be desired by those with inferior dispositions.

Kilesakāmassa ārammaṇabhāvattā sabbākusalasaṃgāhikāya kāmadhātuyā itarā dve saṅgahetvā kathanaṃ sabbasaṅgāhikā. Tissannaṃ dhātūnaṃ aññamaññaṃ asaṅkarato kathā asambhinnā. Imaṃ kāmāvacarasaññitaṃ kāmavitakkasaññitañca kāmadhātuṃ. Paṭiccāti paccayabhūtaṃ labhitvā. Tīhi kāraṇehīti tīhi sārabhūtehi kāraṇehi.

Because the sensual-element is the object of defilement-desire and is inclusive of all unwholesome states, the statement that includes the other two is all-inclusive. Because the three elements do not mix with one another, the discussion is unconfused. Regarding this sensual-element, designated as the sensual sphere and designated as sensual thought... 'Depending on' means having obtained it as a condition. 'By three reasons' means by three essential reasons.

Byāpādavitakko byāpādo uttarapadalopena, so eva nijjīvaṭṭhena sabhāvadhāraṇaṭṭhena dhātūti byāpādadhātu. Byāpajjati cittaṃ etenāti byāpādo, doso. Byāpādopi dhātūti yojanā. Sahajātapaccayādivasenāti sahajātaaññamaññanissayasampayuttaatthiavigatapaccayavasena. Visesena hi parassa attano ca dukkhāpanaṃ vihiṃsā, sā eva dhātu, atthato rosanā parūpaghāto, tathā pavatto vā dosasahagatacittuppādo.

'Ill-willed thought' is ill will, by elision of the latter word. That itself is an element in the sense of being lifeless and in the sense of determining its own nature; hence, the 'element of ill will.' 'The mind is corrupted by this,' thus it is 'ill will' (byāpāda); it is hatred (dosa). The connection is: 'Ill will, too, is an element.' 'By way of co-arisen conditions, etc.' means by way of the conditions of co-arising, mutuality, dependence, association, presence, and non-disappearance. For violence (vihiṃsā) is the specific infliction of suffering on others and oneself; that itself is the element. In meaning, it is anger, harm to others, or a mind-moment accompanied by hatred that has arisen in such a way.

Tiṇagahane araññeti tiṇehi gahanabhūte araññe. Anayabyasananti apāyabyasanaṃ, pariharaṇūpāyarahitaṃ vipattinti vā attho. Avaḍḍhiṃ vināsanti avaḍḍhiñceva vināsañcāti vadanti sabbaso vaḍḍhirahitaṃ. Sukkhatiṇadāyo viya ārammaṇaṃ kilesaggisaṃvaddhanaṭṭhena. Tiṇukkā viya [V 2.0118] akusalasaññā anudahanaṭṭhena. Tiṇakaṭṭha…pe… sattā anayabyasanāpattito. “Ime sattā”ti hi ayoniso paṭipajjamānā adhippetā. Tenāha “yathā sukkhatiṇadāye”tiādi.

'In a wilderness that is a thicket of grass' means in a wilderness that has become a thicket with grass. 'Misfortune and disaster' means disaster in the plane of misery, or the meaning is 'a calamity devoid of a means of avoidance.' 'Decline and ruin': they say it means both decline and ruin, being completely without growth. The object is like a pyre of dry grass, in the sense that it increases the fire of the defilements. Unwholesome perceptions are like grass torches, in the sense that they burn along with it. Grass, sticks... beings, from falling into misfortune and disaster. For by 'these beings' is meant those who practice unwisely. Therefore he said, 'just as in a pyre of dry grass,' etc.

Samatābhāvato [M 2.0136] samatāvirodhato visamatāhetuto ca visamā rāgādayoti āha “rāgavisamādīni anugata”nti. Icchitabbā avassaṃbhāvinibhāvena.

Because of the absence of evenness, because of opposition to evenness, and because they are a cause of unevenness, lust and so on are 'uneven.' Thus he said, 'followed by the unevenness of lust, etc.' They are to be wished for because of their resemblance to what is inevitable.

Saṃkilesato nikkhamanaṭṭhena nekkhammo, so eva nijjīvaṭṭhena dhātūti nekkhammadhātu. Svāyaṃ nekkhammasaddo pabbajjādīsu kusalavitakke ca niruḷhoti āha “nekkhammavitakkopi nekkhammadhātū”ti. Itarāpi dve dhātuyoti abyāpādaavihiṃsādhātuyo vadati. Visuṃ dīpetabbā sarūpena āgatattā. Vitakkādayoti nekkhammasaṅkappacchandapariḷāhapariyesanā. Yathānurūpaṃ attano attano paccayānurūpaṃ. Kathaṃ panettha kusaladhammesu pariḷāho vuttoti? Saṅkhārapariḷāhamattaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ, soḷasasu ākāresu dukkhasacce santāpaṭṭho viya vutto, yassa vigamena arahato sītibhāvappatti vuccati.

By the meaning of emerging from defilements, it is renunciation; that very renunciation is an element, by the meaning of being without a living principle. This term 'renunciation' is established in such things as going forth and in wholesome thought, thus it is said: 'The thought of renunciation is also the element of renunciation.' The other two elements, he says, are the elements of non-ill-will and non-cruelty. They should be explained separately because they are presented in their own form. 'Thoughts and so on' refers to the thought of renunciation, desire, ardor, and search. Each arises appropriately, in accordance with its own respective conditions. But how is ardor mentioned here in relation to wholesome states? It is said with reference to the mere torment of formations, just as in the sixteen aspects of the truth of suffering, the sense of torment is mentioned. With the cessation of that ardor, the attainment of coolness by the Arahant is spoken of.

Sayaṃ na byāpajjati, tena vā taṃsamaṅgīpuggalo na kiñci byāpādetīti abyāpādo, vihiṃsāya vuttavipariyāyehi sā veditabbā. Hitesibhāvena mijjati siniyhatīti mitto, mittassa esāti metti, abyāpādo. Mettāyanāti mettākāraṇaṃ, mettāya vā ayanā pavattanā. Mettāyitattanti mettāyitassa mettāya pavattassa bhāvo. Mettācetovimuttīti mettāyanavasena pavatto cittasamādhi. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

He himself is not malevolent, nor does a person endowed with it harm anything—this is non-ill-will; non-cruelty should be understood in the opposite way to what was said for cruelty. One who is affectionate and loving from a desire for the welfare of others is a friend; the state of a friend is friendliness, which is non-ill-will. Mettāyana means the cause of loving-kindness, or the proceeding by way of loving-kindness. Mettāyitatta means the state of one who has loving-kindness, of one who proceeds with loving-kindness. The liberation of mind through loving-kindness is the concentration of mind that proceeds by way of mettāyana. The rest is as has been explained.

Sanidānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sanidāna Sutta is concluded.

3. Giñjakāvasathasuttavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Giñjakāvasatha Sutta

97. Ito paṭṭhāyāti “dhātuṃ, bhikkhave”ti imasmā tatiyasuttato paṭṭhāya. Yāva kammavaggo, tāva netvā upagantvā seti etthāti āsayo, hīnādibhāvena adhīno āsayo ajjhāsayo, taṃ ajjhāsayaṃ, adhimuttanti attho. Saññā uppajjatītiādīsu hīnādibhedaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ paṭicca hīnādibhedā saññā, tannissayadiṭṭhivikappanā, vitakko ca uppajjati sahajātakoṭiyā upanissayakoṭiyā ca. Satthāresūti tesaṃ satthupaṭiññatāya vuttaṃ, na satthulakkhaṇasabbhāvato. Asammāsambuddhesūti ādhāre visaye ca bhummaṃ ekato katvā [M 2.0137] vuttanti paṭhamaṃ tāva dassento “mayaṃ sammāsambuddhā”tiādiṃ vatvā itaraṃ dassento “tesu sammāsambuddhā [V 2.0119] ete”tiādimāha. Tesaṃ “mayaṃ sammāsambuddhā”ti uppannadiṭṭhi idha mūlabhāvena pucchitā, itarā anusaṅkitāti pucchatiyevāti sāsaṅkaṃ vadati.

97. 'From here onwards' means starting from this third sutta, 'Monks, the element...'. The basis (āsaya) is where the mind, having been led up to the Kammavagga, comes to rest. The basis (āsayo) that is dependent (adhīno) in inferior and other ways is the disposition (ajjhāsayo); that disposition means inclination (adhimutti). In cases like 'perception arises,' dependent on a disposition of an inferior kind and so on, perceptions of an inferior kind and so on arise; dependent on that, views, conceptual constructions, and thought arise, both as co-nascent factors and as decisive support conditions. 'Regarding teachers' is said because of their claim to be teachers, not from the actual existence of the characteristics of a teacher. 'Concerning those who are not rightly self-awakened,' the locative case is used here to refer to both the basis and the object. First, showing one side, he said, 'We are rightly self-awakened,' etc., and then showing the other, he said, 'Among them, these are rightly self-awakened,' etc. Their arisen view, 'We are rightly self-awakened,' is questioned here as the root; the other is suspected, so he asks with uncertainty, thus it is spoken with doubt.

“Mahatī”ti ettha mahāsaddo “mahājano”tiādīsu viya bahuatthavācakoti daṭṭhabbo. Avijjāpi hīnahīnatarahīnatamādibhedena bahupakārā. Tassāti diṭṭhiyā. Kasmā panettha “yadidaṃ avijjā dhātū”ti avijjaṃ uddharitvā “hīnaṃ dhātuṃ paṭiccā”ti ajjhāsayadhātu niddiṭṭhāti? Na kho panetaṃ evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ, “aññaṃ uddharitvā aññaṃ niddiṭṭhā”ti, yato avijjāsīsena ajjhāsayadhātu eva gahitā. Avijjāgahito hi purisapuggalo diṭṭhajjhāsayo hīnādibhedaṃ avijjādhātuṃ nissāya tato saññādiṭṭhiādike saṅkappeti. Paṇidhi patthanā, sā pana tathā tathā cittassa ṭhapanavasena hotīti āha “cittaṭṭhapana”nti. Tenāha “sā panesā”tiādi. Eteti hīnapaccayā saññādiṭṭhivitakkacetanā patthanā paṇidhisaṅkhātā hīnā dhammā. Hīno nāma hīnadhammasamāyogato. Sabbapadānīti “paññapetī”tiādīni padāni yojetabbāni hīnasaddena majjhimuttamaṭṭhānantarassa asambhavato. Upapajjanaṃ “upapattī”ti āha “dve upapattiyo paṭilābho ca nibbatti cā”ti. Tattha hīnakulādīti ādi-saddena hīnarūpabhogaparisādīnaṃ saṅgaho. Hīnattikavasenāti hīnattike vuttattikapadavasenāti adhippāyo. Cittuppādakkhaṇeti idaṃ hīnattikapariyāpannānaṃ cittuppādānaṃ vasena tattha tattha laddhattā vuttaṃ. Pañcasu nīcakulesūti caṇḍālavenanesādarathakārapukkusakulesu. Dvādasaakusalacittuppādānaṃ pana yo koci paṭilābho hīnoti yojanā. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo. Imasmiṃ ṭhāneti “yāyaṃ, bhante, diṭṭhī”tiādinā āgate imasmiṃ ṭhāne. “Dhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjatī”tiādinā āgatattā nibbattiyeva adhippetā, na paṭilābho.

Here, in 'great,' the word 'great' (mahā) should be understood as denoting 'many,' as in 'a great many people' (mahājano). Ignorance is also of many kinds, distinguished as low, lower, and lowest. 'Of that' means of that view. Why here, having brought up 'the element of ignorance,' is 'dependent on an inferior element' specified as the element of disposition? This should not be seen as one thing being brought up and another specified, for the element of disposition is included under the heading of ignorance. A person seized by ignorance, having a disposition for views, relies on the element of ignorance—which is of inferior and other kinds—and based on that, he forms perceptions, views, and so on. Aspiration (paṇidhi) is a wish (patthanā); since it occurs by way of placing the mind in such and such a way, it is called 'placing of the mind' (cittaṭṭhapana). Therefore he says 'But this...' and so on. These are the inferior phenomena, namely, these inferior conditions: perception, view, thought, volition, wishing, and aspiration. 'Inferior' means due to association with inferior phenomena. All the terms, such as 'designates,' should be connected with the word 'inferior,' because there is no possibility of an intermediate or superior state immediately following. 'Arising' (upapajjanaṃ) is called 'occurrence' (upapatti); thus he says 'two occurrences: acquisition and production.' Therein, 'in an inferior family, etc.'—by the word 'etc.' are included inferior forms, enjoyments, retinues, and so on. 'By way of the inferior triad' means by way of the terms of the triad stated in the inferior triad. 'At the moment of the arising of consciousness' is said because these states are found here and there by way of the arisings of consciousness that fall into the inferior triad. 'In the five low families' means in the families of outcastes, bamboo-workers, hunters, chariot-makers, and scavengers. The construction is that any acquisition of the twelve unwholesome arisings of consciousness is inferior. This is the method for the other two as well. 'In this place' means in this place introduced by 'Venerable sir, this view...'. Because it is stated 'Monks, dependent on an element it arises...,' production (nibbatti) is intended, not acquisition (paṭilābho).

Giñjakāvasathasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Giñjakāvasatha Sutta is concluded.

4. Hīnādhimuttikasuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Hīnādhimuttika Sutta

98. Ekato [M 2.0138] hontīti samānacchandatāya ajjhāsayato ekato honti. Nirantarā hontīti tāya eva samānacchandatāya cittena nibbisesā honti. Idha adhimutti nāma ajjhāsayadhātūti āha “hīnādhimuttikāti hīnajjhāsayā”ti.

98. 'They come together' means they come together due to having the same desire and disposition. 'They are continuous' means they are without distinction in mind due to that same shared desire. Here, inclination (adhimutti) is the element of disposition (ajjhāsayadhātu), for it is said: 'Those of inferior inclination means those of inferior disposition.'

Hīnādhimuttikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Hīnādhimuttika Sutta is concluded.

5. Caṅkamasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Caṅkama Sutta

99. Mahāpaññesūti [V 2.0120] vipulapaññesu. Nanti sāriputtattheraṃ. Khandhantaranti khandhavibhāgaṃ, khandhānaṃ vā antaraṃ viseso atthīti khandhantaro. Esa nayo sesesupi. Parikammanti iddhividhādhigamassa pubbabhāgaparikammañceva uttaraparikammañca. Ānisaṃsanti iddhānisaṃsañceva ānisaṃsañca. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ vikubbananti adhiṭṭhānavidhānañceva vikubbanavidhānañca. Vuttanayenevāti “pathaviṃ pattharanto viyā”tiādinā.

99. 'Among those of great wisdom' means among those of extensive wisdom. 'Him' refers to the Elder Sāriputta. 'Distinction between aggregates' means the analysis of the aggregates, or because there is a difference, a distinction, among the aggregates, it is the distinction between aggregates. This method applies to the rest as well. 'Preparation' refers to both the preliminary and subsequent preparation for the attainment of psychic powers. 'Benefit' refers to both the benefit of psychic powers and benefit in general. 'Determination and transformation' refers to both the method of determination and the method of transformation. 'In the manner stated' refers to 'Just as one spreads out the earth,' etc.

Dhutaṅgaparihāranti dhutaṅgānaṃ pariharaṇavidhiṃ. Pariharaṇaggahaṇeneva samādānaṃ siddhaṃ hotīti taṃ na gahitaṃ. Ānisaṃsanti taṃtaṃdhutaṅgapariharaṇe daṭṭhabbaṃ ānisaṃsameva. Samodhānanti “ettakā piṇḍapātapaṭisaṃyuttā, ettakā senāsanapaṭisaṃyuttā”ti paccayavasena aññamaññañca antogadhattā. Adhiṭṭhānanti adhiṭṭhānavidhiṃ. Bhedanti ukkaṭṭhādibhedañceva bhinnākārañca.

'Upholding the ascetic practices' refers to the method of upholding the ascetic practices. Since the undertaking is accomplished by the very taking up of 'upholding,' it is not mentioned separately. 'Benefit' refers to the benefit that should be seen in upholding each respective ascetic practice. 'Inclusion' means the mutual inclusion and being contained within each other by way of requisites, such as 'this many are connected to almsfood, this many to lodging.' 'Determination' refers to the method of determination. 'Distinctions' refers to the distinctions of superior, etc., as well as the different forms.

Parikammanti “dibbacakkhu evaṃ uppādetabbaṃ, evaṃ visodhetabba”ntiādinā parikammavidhānaṃ. Ānisaṃsanti paresaṃ ajjhāsayānurūpāyatanādiānisaṃsapabhedaṃ. Upakkilesanti sādhāraṇaṃ asādhāraṇaṃ duvidhaṃ upakkilesaṃ. Vipassanābhāvanupakkilesā hi dibbacakkhussa upakkilesāti veditabbā.

'Preparation' refers to the method of preparation, such as 'the divine eye should be developed thus, purified thus,' etc. 'Benefit' refers to the various kinds of benefits, such as those related to the bases suitable to the dispositions of others. 'Corruptions' refers to the twofold corruptions: common and uncommon. The corruptions of the development of insight should be understood as the corruptions of the divine eye.

Saṅkhepavitthāragambhīruttānavicitrakathādīsūti saṅkhepo vitthāro gambhīratā uttānatā vicitrabhāvo neyyatthatā nītatthatāti evamādīsu dhammassa kathetabbappakāresu taṃ taṃ kathetabbākāraṃ.

Regarding 'in brief, detailed, profound, shallow, varied discourse, etc.': this refers to brevity, detail, depth, shallowness, variety, meaning that requires interpretation, and definitive meaning. In these and other types of ways of speaking about the Dhamma, it refers to each respective mode of speaking.

Iti-saddo [M 2.0139] ādiattho, pakārattho vā. Tena –

The word 'iti' has the meaning of 'etc.' or the meaning of 'kind.'

“Ādimhi sīlaṃ deseyya, (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.190; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.291)

Majjhe cittaṃ viniddise;

Ante paññā kathetabbā,

Eso dhammakathāvidho”ti. –

At the beginning, virtue should be taught; in the middle, the mind should be explained; at the end, wisdom should be spoken of—this is the method of a Dhamma talk.

Evaṃ kathetabbākāraṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

Thus it includes the manner of speaking.

“Sithilaṃ [V 2.0121] dhanitañca dīgharassaṃ, garukaṃ lahukañca niggahītaṃ;

Sambandhaṃ vavatthitaṃ vimuttaṃ, dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyā pabhedo”ti. (dī. ni. 1.190; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.291; pari. 485) –

“Loose, tight, long, short, heavy, light, checked; connected, separated, released: thus tenfold is the distinction in the understanding of letters.”

Evaṃ vuttaṃ dasavidhaṃ byañjanabuddhiṃ. Aṭṭhuppattinti tassa tassa suttassa jātakassa ca aṭṭhuppattiṃ. Anusandhinti pacchānusandhiādianusandhiṃ. Pubbāparanti sambandhaṃ. Idaṃ padaṃ evaṃ vattabbaṃ, idaṃ pubbāparaṃ evaṃ gahetabbanti.

Thus is stated the tenfold understanding of letters. ‘Aṭṭhuppatti’ refers to the occasion of utterance for each sutta and Jātaka. ‘Anusandhi’ refers to subsequent and preceding connections. ‘Pubbāpara’ refers to the sequence. ‘This word should be spoken thus; this sequence should be understood thus.’

Kulasaṅgaṇhanaparihāranti lābhuppādanatthaṃ kulānaṃ saṅgaṇhanavidhino pariharaṇaṃ tanniyamitaṃ ekantikaṃ kulasaṅgahaṇavidhiṃ.

‘Kulasaṅgaṇhanaparihāra’ means the avoidance of the method of associating with families for the purpose of generating gain; it is the regulated and exclusive method of associating with families.

Caṅkamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Caṅkama Sutta is concluded.

6. Sagāthāsuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Sagāthā Sutta

100. “Dhātuso saṃsandantī”ti idaṃ ajjhāsayato sarikkhatādassanaṃ, na kāyena missībhāvadassananti āha “samuddantare”tiādi. Nirantaroti nibbiseso. Saṃsaggāti pañcavidhasaṃsaggahetu. Saṃsaggagahaṇena cettha saṃsaggavatthukā taṇhā gahitā. Tenāha “dassana…pe… snehenā”ti.

100. “They converge by way of elements”: this shows similarity in disposition, not a manifestation of bodily mingling; thus it is said, “between the oceans,” etc. “Without interval” means without distinction. “Through association” means the cause of the five kinds of association. And here, by the term “association,” craving that has association as its basis is meant. Hence it is said: “by seeing …pe… through affection.”

Vanati bhajati sajjati tenāti vanaṃ, vanathoti ca kileso vuccatīti āha “vanatho jātoti kilesavanaṃ jāta”nti. Itare saṃsaggamūlakāti tameva paṭikkhipanto āha “adassanenā”ti. Sādhujīvīti sādhu suṭṭhu jīvī, taṃjīvanasīlo. Tenāha “parisuddhajīvitaṃ jīvamāno”ti.

Because one desires (vanati), resorts to, and clings on account of it, it is called craving (vana); and “thicket” (vanatha) is also said to be a defilement. Thus he says: ‘“A thicket has grown” means the jungle of defilements has grown.’ ‘The others are rooted in association’: rejecting just that, he says, ‘by not seeing.’ ‘One who lives well’ means one who lives well, excellently, one whose nature is to live thus. Hence he says: ‘living a perfectly pure life.’

Sagāthāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sagāthā Sutta is finished.

7. Assaddhasaṃsandanasuttavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Assaddhasaṃsandana Sutta

101. Nirojāti [M 2.0140] saddhāsnehābhāvena nisnehā. Tato eva arasabhāvena nirasā. Ekasadisāti samasamā nibbisesā. Tenāha “nirantarā”ti. Alajjitāya ekasīmakatā bhinnamariyādā. Saddhā tesaṃ atthīti saddhā. Tantipālakāti saddhammatantiyā pālakā. Vaṃsānurakkhakāti [V 2.0122] ariyavaṃsassa anurakkhakā. Āraddhavīriyāti paggahitavīriyā. Yasmā tādisānaṃ vīriyaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ nāma hoti kiccasiddhiyā, tasmā vuttaṃ “paripuṇṇaparakkamā”ti. Sabbakiccapariggāhikāyāti catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvanākiccapariggāhikāya.

101. “Devoid of sap” means without affection due to the absence of faith and affection. For that very reason, they are tasteless. “Of the same kind” means equal, without distinction. Therefore it is said: “without interval.” For the shameless one, boundaries are made one, standards are broken. “Faithful” means they possess faith. “Protectors of the tradition” means protectors of the tradition of the good Dhamma. “Preservers of the lineage” means preservers of the noble lineage. “Of aroused energy” means of exerted energy. Because the energy of such ones is called complete on account of the accomplishment of the task, it is therefore said, “of complete exertion.” “Encompassing all tasks” means encompassing the task of developing the four establishments of mindfulness.

Assaddhasaṃsandanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Assaddhasaṃsandana Sutta is finished.

8-12. Assaddhamūlakasuttādivaṇṇanā

8-12. The Commentary on the Assaddhamūlaka Sutta and others

102-106. Aṭṭhamādīnīti aṭṭhamaṃ navamaṃ dasamaṃ ekādasamaṃ dvādasamanti imāni pañca suttānīti eke. Apare pana nava suttānīti icchanti. Svāyamattho aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttoyeva. Pāḷiyañca kesuci potthakesu likhīyati.

102-106. “The eighth and so on”: this means the eighth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth—these five suttas, according to some. Others, however, hold that there are nine suttas. This meaning is stated in the commentary itself. And in some books it is written in the Pāli text.

Assaddhamūlakasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Assaddhamūlaka Sutta and others is finished.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Second Chapter is finished.

3. Kammapathavaggo

3. The Chapter on the Courses of Action

1-2. Asamāhitasuttādivaṇṇanā

1-2. The Commentary on the Asamāhita Sutta and others

107-108. Ito paresūti ito dutiyavaggato paresu suttesu. Paṭhamanti paṭhamavagge paṭhamaṃ. Kasmā panettha evaṃ desanā pavattāti āha “evaṃ vuccamāne”tiādi.

107-108. “In those that follow this” means in the suttas that follow this second chapter. “The first” means the first in the first chapter. Why did the teaching proceed in this way here? He says: “when it is said thus,” etc.

Asamāhitasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Asamāhita Sutta and others is finished.

3-5. Pañcasikkhāpadasuttādivaṇṇanā

3-5. The Commentary on the Pañcasikkhāpada Sutta and others

109-111. Surāmerayasaṅkhātanti [M 2.0141] piṭṭhasurādisurāsaṅkhātaṃ pupphāsavādimerayasaṅkhātañca. Majjanaṭṭhena majjaṃ. Surāmerayamajjappamādoti vuccati “majjati tenā”ti katvā. Tasmiṃ tiṭṭhantīti tasmiṃ pamāde pamajjanavasena tiṭṭhantīti attho. Sesaṃ tatiyacatutthesu suviññeyyamevāti.

109-111. “Reckoned as liquor and spirits” means that reckoned as liquor, such as grain liquor, and that reckoned as spirits, such as flower-sap liquor. It is an “intoxicant” (majja) because it has the nature of intoxicating. “Heedlessness from liquor, spirits, and intoxicants” is so called because “one is intoxicated by it.” “They stand in that” means they stand in that heedlessness by way of being intoxicated. The rest in the third and fourth suttas is easy to understand.

Pañcame [V 2.0123] tāni padāni saṃvaṇṇetuṃ “pañcame”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha pāṇo nāma vohārato satto, paramatthato jīvitindriyaṃ, taṃ pāṇaṃ atipātenti aticca antareyeva, atikkamma vā satthādīhi abhibhavitvā pātenti saṇikaṃ patituṃ adatvā sīghaṃ pātentīti attho. Kāyena vācāya vā adinnaṃ parasantakaṃ. Ādiyantīti gaṇhanti. Micchāti na sammā, gārayhavasena. Musāti atathaṃ vatthu. Vadantīti visaṃvādanavasena vadanti. Piyasuññakaraṇato pisuṇā, pisati vā pare satte, hiṃsatīti attho. Mammacchedikāti etena parassa mammacchedavasena ekantapharusasañcetanā pharusavācā nāmāti dasseti. Abhijjhāsaddo lubbhane niruḷhoti āha “parabhaṇḍe lubbhanasīlāti attho”ti. Byāpannanti dosavasena vipannaṃ. Pakativijahanena pūtibhūtaṃ. Sādhūhi garahitabbataṃ pattā “natthi dinna”ntiādinayappavattā natthikāhetukaakiriyadiṭṭhi kammapathapariyāpannā nāma. Micchattapariyāpannā sabbāpi lokuttaramaggapaṭipakkhā viparītadiṭṭhi.

To explain those terms in the fifth sutta, the passage beginning “In the fifth” was started. Herein, “living being” (pāṇa) is conventionally a being; in the ultimate sense, it is the life faculty. “They destroy that living being”: this means, having overcome it with weapons and so on, they fell it, not allowing it to fall slowly but felling it quickly. “What is not given” is the property of another. “They take” means they grasp it with body or speech. “Wrongly” means not rightly, in a blameworthy way. “Falsely” means an untrue matter. “They speak” means they speak by way of deception. “Slanderous” (pisuṇā) is from making one destitute of friends, or it “crushes” (pisati) other beings, that is, it harms them. “Cutting to the quick”: by this it is shown that harsh speech is the intention that is entirely harsh by way of cutting another’s vital spot. The word “covetousness” is established in the sense of greed; thus he says: “it means having the nature of being greedy for another’s property.” “Malevolent” means corrupted by way of hatred, having become putrid by abandoning its natural state. “Having attained a state of being blameworthy by the good”: this refers to the nihilistic, uncaused, inefficacious view that proceeds in the manner of “there is nothing given,” etc., which is included in the course of action. Included in “wrongness” is all perverted view that is the opponent of the supramundane path.

Tesanti kammapathānaṃ. Vohāratoti indriyabaddhaṃ upādāya paññattimattato. Tiracchānagatādīsūti ādi-saddena petānaṃ saṅgaho. Payogavatthumahantatādīhi mahāsāvajjatā tehi paccayehi uppajjamānāya cetanāya balavabhāvato. Yathāvuttapaccayavipariyāyepi taṃtaṃpaccayehi cetanāya balavabhāvavasena appasāvajjamahāsāvajjatā vā veditabbā. Iddhimayoti kammavipākiddhimayo dāṭhākoṭanādīnaṃ viya.
