He made them grasp it so that it proceeded as if one had entered a path. “He stimulated them” (samuttejesi) means that when insight was undertaken and the arising and passing away of formations became apparent, he led them to the middle path of development by the timely application of exertion and equanimity through the factors of awakening, and thus properly stimulated their insight mind by making the faculties clear, so that insight knowledge flowed brightly. Or, he established them with Nibbāna as the goal. “He gladdened them” (sampahaṃsesīti) means that as insight thus progressed, he gladdened their minds through the evenly progressing development and the development to be attained further on, and thoroughly pleased them with the taste of what was attained. Thus, the meaning here should be understood.

Manute pariññādivasena saccāni bujjhatīti muni. Teti taṃ. Upayogatthe hi idaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Uttarīti upari, tava yathābhūtasabhāvato paratoti attho. Pakkhapatito agatigamanaṃ atirekaokāso. Upaparikkhīti anuvicca nivārako na bahumato. Buddhapaṭibhāgo thero. “Bālā bhikkhunī dubbhāsitaṃ āhā”ti avatvā “khamatha, bhante”ti vadantena pakkhapātena viya vuttaṃ hotīti āha “ekā bhikkhunī na vāritā”tiādi.

One who understands the truths by way of full comprehension and so on is a ‘muni.’ ‘Te’ means ‘taṃ.’ For this is a genitive in the sense of connection. ‘Uttari’ means above, that is, beyond your true nature. ‘Pakkhapatito’ (being partial) means going to a wrong course, an excessive opportunity. ‘Upaparikkhī’ (one who investigates) means one who investigates and prevents, not one who is highly regarded. The elder is a counterpart of the Buddha. Not saying, “The foolish nun spoke badly,” but saying, “Forgive me, venerable sir,” is as if it were said with partiality. Therefore, he said, “One nun was not restrained,” and so on.

Cutā saliṅgato naṭṭhā, desantarapakkamena adassanaṃ na gatā. Kaṇṭakasākhā viyāti kuraṇṭakaapāmaggakaṇṭakalasikāhi sākhā viya.

Fallen, they are destroyed, lost from their own form; they have not gone out of sight by departing to another country. ‘Like thorny branches’ means like branches with kuraṇṭaka, apāmārga, and kaṇṭakalasikā thorns.

Upassayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Upassaya Sutta is finished.

11. Cīvarasuttavaṇṇanā

11. The Commentary on the Cīvara Sutta

154. Rājagahassa [M 2.0164] dakkhiṇabhāge giri dakkhiṇāgiri ṇa-kāre a-kārassa dīghaṃ katvā, tassa dakkhiṇabhāge janapadopi “dakkhiṇāgirī”ti vuccati, “girito dakkhiṇabhāgo”ti [V 2.0144] katvā. Ekadivasenāti ekena divasena uppabbājesuṃ tesaṃ saddhāpabbajitābhāvato.

154. A mountain in the southern part of Rājagaha is Dakkhiṇāgiri. By making the ‘a’ vowel in the letter ‘ṇa’ long, the region in its southern part is also called ‘Dakkhiṇāgirī,’ because it is ‘the southern part of the mountain.’ ‘In a single day’ means they gave them the going forth in one day, because they had not gone forth out of faith.

Yattha cattāro vā uttari vā bhikkhū akappiyanimantanaṃ sādiyitvā pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ ekato paṭiggaṇhitvā bhuñjanti, etaṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ nāma, taṃ tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti “tikabhojanaṃ paññatta”nti vacanena gaṇabhojanaṃ paṭikkhittanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tayo atthavase paṭicca anuññātattāpi “tikabhojana”nti vadanti.

When four or more bhikkhus, having accepted an improper invitation, receive and eat together any one of the five kinds of food, this is called a ‘group meal’ (gaṇabhojana). Since it is permissible for three bhikkhus to eat, by the statement ‘a meal for three (tikabhojana) is prescribed,’ it is said that a group meal is prohibited. It is also called a ‘meal for three’ because it is permitted on account of three circumstances.

“Dummaṅkūnaṃ niggaho eva pesalānaṃ phāsuvihāro”ti idaṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ. Tenevāha “dummaṅkūnaṃ niggahenevā”tiādi. “Yathā devadatto…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindeyyu”nti iminā kāraṇena tikabhojanaṃ paññattaṃ.

‘The subduing of the unruly is indeed the comfortable dwelling of the agreeable’—this is one factor. Therefore it was said, ‘by subduing the unruly,’ and so forth. ‘Just as Devadatta… might split the Saṅgha’—for this reason the meal for three was prescribed.

Atha kiñcarahīti atha kasmā tvaṃ asampannagaṇaṃ bandhitvā carasīti adhippāyo. Asampannāya parisāya cārikācaraṇaṃ kulānuddayāya na hoti, kulānaṃ ghātitattāti adhippāyena thero “sassaghātaṃ maññe carasī”tiādimavoca.

‘But what then?’ means, ‘Why then do you go about, having formed an incomplete group?’ Wandering with an incomplete retinue is not for the compassion of families, because it is a destruction of families—with this meaning, the elder said, ‘You seem to be practicing crop-slaughter,’ and so forth.

Sodhento tassā ativiya parisuddhabhāvadassanena. Uddisituṃ na jānāmi tathā cittasseva anuppannapubbattā. Kiñcanaṃ kilesavatthu. Saṅgahetabbakhettavatthu palibodho, ālayo apekkhā. Okāsābhāvatoti bahukiccakaraṇīyatāya kusalakiriyāya okāsābhāvato. Sannipātaṭṭhānatoti saṅketaṃ katvā viya kilesarajānaṃ tattha sannijjhapavattanato.

‘Purifying’ means by seeing its extreme purity. ‘I do not know how to point out’ means because such a state of mind had never arisen before. ‘Anything’ (kiñcanaṃ) is a basis for defilement. ‘A field or property to be acquired’ is an impediment (palibodha); ‘attachment’ (ālaya) is expectation (apekkhā). ‘Due to lack of opportunity’ means because, being occupied with many duties and tasks, there is no opportunity for wholesome action. ‘A gathering place’ means because the kings of defilements assemble and proceed there as if by prior arrangement.

Sikkhattayabrahmacariyanti adhisīlasikkhādisikkhattayasaṅgahaṃ brahmaṃ seṭṭhaṃ cariyaṃ. Khaṇḍādibhāvāpādanena akhaṇḍaṃ katvā. Lakkhaṇavacanañhetaṃ. Kiñci sikkhekadesaṃ asesetvā ekanteneva paripūretabbatāya ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ. Cittuppādamattampi saṃkilesamalaṃ anuppādetvā accantameva visuddhaṃ katvā pariharitabbatāya ekantaparisuddhaṃ. Tato eva saṅkhaṃ viya likhitanti saṅkhalikhitaṃ. Tenāha “likhitasaṅkhasadisa”nti. Dāṭhikāpi taggahaṇeneva gahetvā [M 2.0165] “massu”tveva vuttaṃ, na ettha kevalaṃ massuyevāti attho. Kasāyena rattāni kāsāyāni.

‘The threefold training and the holy life’ (sikkhattayabrahmacariya) means the holy, excellent practice, comprising the threefold training beginning with the higher moral training. By preventing it from becoming broken and so forth, it is made unbroken. This is a characteristic expression. Because one must completely fulfill it in every way, without leaving out any part of the training, it is ‘entirely complete’ (ekantaparipuṇṇa). Because one must maintain it, having made it utterly pure without allowing even a thought-moment of the stain of defilement to arise, it is ‘utterly pure’ (ekantaparisuddha). Therefore, it is polished like a conch shell (saṅkhalikhitaṃ). Hence it is said, ‘like a polished conch shell’ (likhitasaṅkhasadisa). Even ‘dāṭhikā’ (side-whiskers) is taken by that reference and called ‘moustache’ (massu), but the meaning here is not limited to moustache alone. ‘Dyed with dye’ (kasāyena rattāni) means they are ochre-colored (kāsāyāni).

Vaṅgasāṭakoti vaṅgadese uppannasāṭako. Esāti mahākassapatthero. Abhinīhārato paṭṭhāya paṇidhānato pabhuti, ayaṃ idāni vuccamānā. Aggasāvakadvayaṃ upādāya tatiyattā “tatiyasāvaka”nti [V 2.0145] vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassanti bhikkhūnaṃ satasahassañceva saṭṭhisahassāni ca aṭṭha ca sahassāni.

‘Vaṅga cloth’ (vaṅgasāṭaka) means cloth produced in the Vaṅga country. ‘This’ (esa) refers to the Elder Mahākassapa. ‘From the time of aspiration’ (abhinīhārato paṭṭhāya) means from the time of resolve (paṇidhānato pabhuti); this is what is now being spoken of. Because he is the third, taking into account the pair of chief disciples, he is called the ‘third disciple’ (tatiyasāvaka). ‘One hundred and sixty-eight thousand bhikkhus’ (aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassa) means one hundred thousand bhikkhus, sixty thousand, and eight thousand.

Ayañca ayañca guṇoti sīlato paṭṭhāya yāva aggaphalā guṇoti kittento mahāsamuddaṃ pūrayamāno viya kathesi.

Praising the virtues, ‘this virtue and that virtue,’ starting from morality up to the highest fruit, he spoke as if filling the great ocean.

Kolāhalanti devatāhi nibbattito kolāhalo.

‘Uproar’ (kolāhala) means an uproar produced by deities.

Khuddakādivasena pañcavaṇṇā. Taraṇaṃ vā hotu maraṇaṃ vāti mahoghaṃ ogāhanto puriso viya maccherasamuddaṃ uttaranto pacchāpi…pe… pādamūle ṭhapesi bhagavato dhammadesanāya maccherapahānassa kathitattā.

They are of five kinds, beginning with the small one. Like a man plunging into the great flood, thinking, ‘Let it be crossing or death,’ and crossing the ocean of stinginess, he later… placed it at the feet of the Blessed One, because the abandoning of stinginess was taught in the Blessed One’s Dhamma discourse.

Satthu guṇā kathitā nāma hontīti vuttaṃ “satthu guṇe kathentassā”ti. Tato paṭṭhāyāti tadā satthu sammukhā dhammassavanato paṭṭhāya.

It is said, ‘The Teacher’s virtues are indeed spoken of,’ by the phrase ‘of one who speaks the Teacher’s virtues.’ ‘From then onward’ (tato paṭṭhāya) means from that time, from hearing the Dhamma in the Teacher’s presence.

Tathāgatamañcassāti tathāgatassa paribhogamañcassa. Dānaṃ datvā brāhmaṇassa purohitaṭṭhāne ṭhapesi. Tādisasseva seṭṭhino dhītā hutvā.

‘Of the Tathāgata’s couch’ (tathāgatamañcassa) means of the couch used by the Tathāgata. Having given a gift, he established the brahmin in the position of family priest. She became the daughter of just such a wealthy man.

Adinnavipākassāti pubbe katūpacitassa sabbaso na dinnavipākassa. Tassa kammassāti tassa paccekabuddhassa patte piṇḍapātaṃ chinditvā kalalapūraṇakammassa. Tasmiṃyeva attabhāve sattasu ṭhānesu duggandhasarīratāya paṭinivattitā. Iṭṭhakapantīti suvaṇṇiṭṭhakapanti. Ghaṭaniṭṭhakāyāti tassa pantiyaṃ paṭhamaṃ ṭhapitaiṭṭhakāya saddhiṃ ghaṭetabbaiṭṭhakāya ūnā hoti. Bhaddake kāleti īdisiyā iṭṭhakāya icchitakāleyeva āgatāsi. Tena bandhanenāti tena silesasambandhena.

‘Of an action with an ungiven result’ (adinnavipākassa) means of a previously done and accumulated action whose result has not been entirely given. ‘Of that deed’ (tassa kammassa) refers to the deed of cutting off the almsfood in the bowl of that Paccekabuddha and filling it with slime. In that very existence, it recurred as a foul-smelling body in seven places. ‘A row of bricks’ (iṭṭhakapanti) means a row of golden bricks. ‘As for the brick for the wall’ (ghaṭaniṭṭhakāya) means the brick to be fitted with the first brick placed in that row was deficient. ‘At a good time’ (bhaddake kāle) means ‘you have come at the desired time with such a brick.’ ‘By that binding’ (tena bandhanena) means by that connection of cement.

Olambakāti [M 2.0166] muttāmaṇimayā olambakā. Puññanti natthi no puññaṃ taṃ, yaṃ nimittaṃ yaṃ kāraṇā ito sukhumatarassa paṭilābho siyāti attho. Puññaniyāmenāti puññānubhāvasiddhena niyāmena. So ca assa bārāṇasirajjaṃ dātuṃ katokāso.

‘Olambaka’ means pendants made of pearls and gems. ‘Merit’ (puñña) means, ‘There is no merit for us by which there would be a sign or a cause for obtaining something more subtle than this’—this is the meaning. ‘By the principle of merit’ (puññaniyāmena) means by the principle established through the power of merit. And that was an opportunity made to give him the kingdom of Bārāṇasī.

Phussarathanti maṅgalarathaṃ. Uṇhīsaṃ vālabījanī khaggo maṇipādukā setacchattanti pañcavidhaṃ rājakakudhabhaṇḍaṃ[V 2.0146]. Setacchattaṃ visuṃ gahitaṃ. Dibbavatthaṃ sādiyituṃ puññānubhāvacodito “nanu tātā thūla”ntiādimāha.

‘Phussaratha’ means the auspicious chariot. ‘The head-dress, the yak-tail whisk, the sword, the jeweled slippers, and the white parasol’ (uṇhīsaṃ vālabījanī khaggo maṇipādukā setacchatta) are the five royal emblems. The white parasol is taken separately. Urged by the power of merit to adorn himself with divine garments, he said, ‘Father, is this not coarse?’ and so forth.

Pañca caṅkamanasatānīti ettha iti-saddena ādiatthena aggisālādīni pabbajitasāruppaṭṭhānāni saṅgaṇhāti.

‘Five hundred walking paths’ (pañca caṅkamanasatāni)—here, the word ‘iti’ includes, by way of the meaning of ‘and so forth,’ suitable places for renunciates, such as fire halls.

Sādhukīḷitanti ariyānaṃ parinibbutaṭṭhāne kātabbasakkāraṃ vadati.

‘Well played’ (sādhukīḷita) refers to the honor to be performed for the noble ones at the place of their final Nibbāna.

Nappamajji nirogā ayyāti pucchitākāradassanaṃ. Parinibbutā devāti devī paṭivacanaṃ adāsi. Paṭiyādetvāti niyyātetvā. Samaṇakapabbajjanti samitapāpehi ariyehi anuṭṭhātabbapabbajjaṃ. So hi rājā paccekabuddhānaṃ vesassa diṭṭhattā “idameva bhaddaka”nti tādisaṃyeva liṅgaṃ gaṇhi.

‘Were the noble ones not negligent? Are they healthy?’ (nappamajji nirogā ayyā)—this shows the manner of questioning. ‘The deities have attained final Nibbāna’ (parinibbutā devā)—the queen gave this reply. ‘Having prepared’ (paṭiyādetvā) means having sent forth. ‘The ascetic life of a recluse’ (samaṇakapabbajjā) means the going forth to be undertaken by the noble ones whose evil is calmed. For that king, having seen the attire of the Paccekabuddhas, thought, ‘This alone is excellent,’ and adopted just such an appearance.

Tatthevāti brahmalokeyeva. Vīsatime vasse sampatteti āharitvā sambandho. Brahmalokato āgantvā nibbattattā brahmacariyādhikārassa cirakālaṃ saṅgahitattā “evarūpaṃ kathaṃ mā kathethā”tiādimāha.

‘Right there’ (tattheva) means in the Brahma world itself. The connection is made by supplying the phrase ‘when the twentieth year was attained’ (vīsatime vasse sampatte). Because he was reborn after coming from the Brahma world, and because of his long practice of the holy life, he said, ‘How could you speak such a thing?’ and so forth.

Vīsati dharaṇāni “nikkha”nti vadanti. Alabhanto na vasāmīti saññāpessāmīti sambandho.

They call twenty dharaṇas a ‘nikkha’. The phrase ‘Not obtaining it, I will not stay’ (alabhanto na vasāmi) is connected to ‘I will make this known’ (saññāpessāmi).

Itthākaroti itthiratanassa uppattiṭṭhānaṃ. Ayyadhītāti amhākaṃ ayyassa dhītā, bhaddakāpilānīti attho. Pasādarūpena nibbisiṭṭhatāya “mahāgīva”nti paṭimāya sadisabhāvamāha. Tenāha “ayyadhītāyā”tiādi.

‘Itthākara’ means the place where the jewel of a woman arose. ‘The noble daughter’ (ayyadhītā) means the daughter of our lord, that is, Bhaddā Kāpilānī. Because of her surpassing beauty, he mentioned her similarity to the statue called ‘Mahāgīva.’ Therefore, he said, ‘of the noble daughter,’ and so forth.

Samānapaṇṇanti sadisapaṇṇaṃ, kumārassa kumāriyā ca vuttantapaṇṇaṃ. Ito ca etto cāti te purisā samāgamaṭṭhānato magadharaṭṭhe mahātitthagāmaṃ [M 2.0167] maddaraṭṭhe sāgalanagarañca uddissa pakkamantā aññamaññaṃ vissajjentā nāma hontīti “ito ca etto ca pesesu”nti vuttā.

‘Similar leaves’ (samānapaṇṇa) means leaves of the same kind, that is, leaves with the story of the prince and the princess. ‘From here and from there’ (ito ca etto ca)—those men, departing from their meeting place and heading towards the village of Mahātittha in the Magadha country and the city of Sāgala in the Madda country, were sending messages to one another; hence it is said, ‘from here and from there they sent.’

Pupphadāmanti hatthihatthappamāṇaṃ pupphadāmaṃ. Tāni pupphadāmāni. Teti ubho bhaddā ceva pippalikumāro ca. Lokāmisenāti gehassitapemena, kāmassādenāti attho. Asaṃsaṭṭhāti na saṃsaṭṭhā[V 2.0147]. Vicārayiṃsu ghaṭe jalantena viya padīpena ajjhāsayena samujjalantena vimokkhabījena samussāhitacittā. Yantabaddhānīti sassasampādanatthaṃ tattha tattha iṭṭhakadvārakavāṭayojanavasena yantabaddhaudakanikkhamanatumbāni. Kammantoti kasikammakaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ. Dāsagāmāti dāsānaṃ vasanagāmā.

‘Flower garland’ (pupphadāma) means a flower garland as long as an elephant’s trunk. ‘Those’ (tāni) refers to the flower garlands. ‘They’ (te) refers to both Bhaddā and Pippalikumāra. ‘By worldly bait’ (lokāmisena) means by household affection; the meaning is the pleasure of sensual desires. ‘Unassociated’ (asaṃsaṭṭhā) means not mingled. They reflected with minds uplifted by the seed of liberation, blazing with intention like a lamp burning in a pot. ‘Bound by machines’ (yantabaddhāni) means water-lifting devices fastened here and there with bricks, doors, and bolts for the purpose of producing crops. ‘Workplace’ (kammanto) means the place for doing agricultural work. ‘Slave villages’ (dāsagāmā) means the villages where slaves reside.

Osāpetvāti pakkhipitvā. Ākappakuttavasenāti ākāravasena kiriyāvasena ca. Ananucchavikanti pabbajitavesassa ananurūpaṃ. Tassa matthaketi dvedhāpathassa dvidhābhūtaṭṭhāne.

‘Having placed’ (osāpetvā) means having inserted. ‘By means of appearance and gesture’ (ākappakuttavasena) means by way of demeanor and action. ‘Unsuitable’ (ananucchavika) means not appropriate for a renunciate’s garb. ‘At its head’ (tassa matthake) means at the fork of the path, the place where it divides in two.

Etesaṃ saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti nisīdīti sambandho. Sā pana satthu tattha nisajjā edisīti dassetuṃ “nisīdanto panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yā buddhānaṃ aparimitakālasaṅgahitā acinteyyāparimeyyapuññasambhārūpacayanibbattā nirūpitasabhāvabuddhaguṇavijjotitā lakkhaṇānubyañjanasamujjalā byāmappabhāketumālālaṅkatā sabhāvasiddhatāya akittimā rūpakāyasirī, taṃyeva mahākassapassa adiṭṭhapubbaṃ pasādasaṃvaḍḍhanatthaṃ aniggahetvā nisinno bhagavā “buddhavesaṃ gahetvā…pe… nisīdī”ti vutto. Asītihatthaṃ padesaṃ byāpetvā pavattiyā “asītihatthā”ti vuttā. Satasākhoti bahusākho anekasākho. Suvaṇṇavaṇṇo ahosi nirantaraṃ buddharasmīhi samantato samokiṇṇattā. Evaṃ vuttappakārena veditabbā.

The connection is: ‘He sat’ (nisīdi) because ‘it is fitting to gather them’ (etesaṃ saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati). To show that the Teacher's sitting there was of such a kind, it is said, “sitting down, however,” etc. Therein, the physical splendor of the Buddhas—accumulated over an immeasurable time, brought forth from the building up of inconceivable and immeasurable stores of merit, illuminated by the defined, inherent qualities of a Buddha, radiant with the major and minor marks, adorned with a fathom-wide halo and a cranial radiance, naturally perfected and uncontrived—this very beauty, never before seen by Mahākassapa, the Blessed One sat without suppressing, in order to increase his faith. Thus it is said: “assuming the Buddha’s appearance... he sat.” Because it spread out, pervading a space of eighty cubits, it is called “eighty cubits.” “With a hundred branches” means many-branched, of numerous branches. It was golden in color because it was continuously and completely pervaded by the Buddha-rays. It should be understood in the manner thus stated.

Rājagahaṃ nāḷandanti ca sāmiatthe upayogavacanaṃ antarāsaddayogatoti āha “rājagahassa nāḷandāya cā”ti. Na hi me ito aññena satthārā bhavituṃ sakkā diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikaparamatthehi sattānaṃ yathārahaṃ anusāsanasamatthassa aññassa sadevake abhāvato. Na hi me ito aññena sugatena bhavituṃ sakkā sobhanagamanaguṇagaṇayuttassa aññassa abhāvato. Na hi me ito aññena sammāsambuddhena bhavituṃ sakkā sammā sabbadhammānaṃ sayambhuñāṇena abhisambuddhassa abhāvato. Imināti “satthā me, bhante”ti iminā vacanena.

Regarding 'Rājagaha and Nāḷanda', this is a case usage in the sense of relation, due to its connection with the word 'antarā' (between); thus it says 'of Rājagaha and of Nāḷanda'. For it is not possible for me to have another teacher besides this one, since there is no other in the world with its devas capable of instructing beings appropriately regarding welfare in this life, welfare in future lives, and the ultimate good. For it is not possible for me to have another Well-Gone One besides this one, since there is no other endowed with the qualities of excellent going. For it is not possible for me to have another Perfectly Self-Enlightened One besides this one, since there is no other who has perfectly awakened to all phenomena by his own self-originated knowledge. ‘By this’ (iminā) means by this statement, “The Teacher is mine, venerable sir.”

Ajānamānova [M 2.0168] sabbaññeyyanti adhippāyo. Sabbacetasāti sabbaajjhattikaṅgaparipuṇṇacetasā. Samannāgatanti sampannaṃ sammadeva anu anu āgataṃ upagataṃ. Phaleyyāti vidāleyya. Vilayanti vināsaṃ.

The meaning is 'as if not knowing all that is knowable.' 'With all his heart' means with a mind fully perfected in all internal aspects. 'Endowed' means fully and properly attained, step by step. 'May he split' means to cleave asunder. 'Dissolution' means annihilation.

Evaṃ sikkhitabbanti idāni vuccamānākārena. Hirottappassa bahalatā nāma vipulatāti āha “mahanta”nti. Paṭhamataramevāti pageva upasaṅkamanato. Tathā atimānapahīno assa, hiriottappaṃ [V 2.0148] yathā saṇṭhāti. Kusalasannissitanti anavajjadhammanissitaṃ. Aṭṭhikanti tena dhammena aṭṭhikaṃ. Ādito paṭṭhāya yāva pariyosānā savanacittaṃ “sabbaceto”ti adhippetanti āha “cittassa thokampi bahi gantuṃ adento”ti. Tena samodhānaṃ dasseti. Sabbena…pe… samannāharitvā ārambhato pabhuti yāva desanā nipphannā, tāva antarantarā pavattena sabbena samannāhāracittena dhammaṃyeva samannāharitvā. Ṭhapitasototi dhamme nihitasoto. Odahitvāti apihitaṃ katvā. Paṭhamajjhānavasenāti idaṃ asubhesu tasseva ijjhato, itaratthañca sukhasampayuttatā vuttā.

‘Thus should one train’—that is, in the manner now being spoken. The profundity of conscience and moral dread is called greatness; hence it is said, “great.” ‘From the very first’ means even before approaching. So too, he should be one who has abandoned overweening pride, so that conscience and moral dread are firmly established. ‘Dependent on the wholesome’ means dependent on blameless qualities. ‘Desirous’ (aṭṭhika) means desirous of that Dhamma. From the beginning until the end, the listening mind is intended by “with all his heart,” hence it is said, “not allowing even a bit of the mind to wander outward.” With that, the connection is shown. ‘With all…’ and so on—from the beginning of the effort until the teaching is completed, throughout, with every thought of directing one's mind, directing it only to the Dhamma. ‘With ear established’ means his ear is fixed on the Dhamma. ‘Having applied it’ means having closed it off. ‘By way of the first jhāna’—this is with regard to its success in the contemplation of the foul, and elsewhere its connection with happiness is stated.

Saṃsārasāgare paribbhamantassa iṇaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhanti kilesā āsavasabhāvāpādanatoti āha “saraṇoti sakileso”ti. Cattāro hi paribhogātiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ visuddhimaggattaṃ saṃvaṇṇanāsu vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ettha ca bhagavā paṭhamaṃ ovādaṃ therassa brāhmaṇajātikattā jātimānapahānatthamabhāsi, dutiyaṃ bāhusaccaṃ nissāya uppajjanakaahaṃkārapahānatthaṃ, tatiyaṃ upadhisampattiṃ nissāya uppajjanakaattasinehapahānatthaṃ. Aṭṭhame divaseti bhagavatā samāgatadivasato aṭṭhame divase.

For one wandering in the ocean of saṃsāra, the defilements stand in the place of debt because they produce the nature of the taints; hence it is said, 'indebted' (sa-iṇo) means 'with defilements' (sakileso). As for the four kinds of use, etc., whatever should be said about them should be understood in the way stated in the commentaries on the Visuddhimagga. Here, the Blessed One first gave advice to the elder for the sake of abandoning the pride in birth that comes from being of brahmin birth; second, for abandoning the conceit that arises from much learning; third, for abandoning the self-affection that arises from the attainment of acquisitions. 'On the eighth day' means on the eighth day from the day he met the Blessed One.

Maggato okkamanaṃ paṭhamataraṃ bhagavatā samāgatadivaseyeva ahosi. Yadi arahattādhigamo pacchā, atha kasmā pāḷiyaṃ pageva siddhaṃ viya vuttanti āha “desanāvārassā”tiādi. “Sattāhameva khvāhaṃ, āvuso saraṇo, raṭṭhapiṇḍaṃ bhuñji”nti vatvā avasarappattaṃ arahattaṃ pavedento “aṭṭhamiyā aññā udapādī”ti āha. Ayamettha desanāvārassa āgamo. Tato paraṃ bhagavatā attano kataṃ anuggahaṃ cīvaraparivattanaṃ dassento “atha kho, āvuso”tiādimāha.

The initial departure from the path occurred on the very day he met the Blessed One. If the attainment of arahantship came later, then why is it stated in the Pāli as if it were already accomplished? To this, it is said, 'because of the occasion of the discourse,' and so on. Having said, 'For seven days, friend Saraṇa, I ate the almsfood of the country,' then, when the opportunity arose, declaring the attainment of arahantship, he said, 'On the eighth day, final knowledge arose.' This is the source for the occasion of the discourse here. After that, showing the favor done to him by the Blessed One—the exchange of robes—he said, 'Then, friend,' and so on.

Antantenāti [M 2.0169] catugguṇaṃ katvā paññattāya saṅghāṭiyā antantena. Jātipaṃsukūlikena…pe… bhavituṃ vaṭṭatīti etena pubbe jātiāraññakaggahaṇena ca terasa dhutaṅgā gahitā evāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Anucchavikaṃ kātunti anurūpaṃ paṭipattiṃ paṭipajjituṃ. Thero pārupīti sambandho.

"Antantenāti" means by the very edge of the saṅghāṭi robe, which is laid out made fourfold. For one who is by nature a rag-robe wearer... it is fitting to be so. By this, and by the earlier mention of being a forest-dweller by nature, it should be understood that the thirteen ascetic practices are included. "Anucchavikaṃ kātunti" means to undertake a suitable practice. "Thero pārupīti" indicates the connection.

Bhagavato ovādaṃ bhagavato vā dhammakāyaṃ nissāya urassa vasena jātoti oraso. Bhagavato vā dhammasarīrassa mukhato sattatiṃsabodhipakkhiyato jāto. Teneva dhammajātadhammanimmitabhāvopi saṃvaṇṇitoti daṭṭhabbo. Ovādadhammo eva satthārā dātabbato therena ādātabbato [V 2.0149] ovādadhammadāyādo, ovādadhammadāyajjoti attho, taṃ arahatīti. Esa nayo sesapadesupi.

Born by way of the chest (urassa), relying on the Blessed One’s instruction or the Blessed One’s Dhamma-body, he is called 'oraso' (a legitimate son). Or, he is born from the mouth of the Blessed One's Dhamma-body, that is, from the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment. Therefore, it should be understood that his state as one born of Dhamma and created by Dhamma is also described. The Dhamma of instruction is to be given by the Teacher and received by the elder; therefore, he is an heir to the Dhamma of instruction. The meaning is the inheritance of the Dhamma of instruction, of which he is worthy. This same principle applies to the remaining terms.

“Pabbajjā ca parisodhitā”ti vatvā tassā sammadeva sodhitabhāvaṃ byatirekamukhena dassetuṃ, “āvuso, yassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha evanti yathā ahaṃ labhiṃ, evaṃ so satthu santikā labhatīti yojanā. Sīhanādaṃ naditunti etthāpi sīhanādanadanā nāma desanāva, thero satthārā attano katānuggahameva anantarasutte vuttanayena ulliṅgeti, na aññathā. Na hi mahāthero kevalaṃ attano guṇānubhāvaṃ vibhāveti. Sesanti yaṃ idha asaṃvaṇṇitaṃ. Purimanayenevāti anantarasutte vuttanayeneva.

Having said, "The going forth is purified," in order to show that it was properly purified by way of contrast, the words "Friend, for whom..." and so on were spoken. Here, the construction of "thus" is: just as I obtained it, so he obtains it from the Teacher. Regarding "roared a lion's roar," here too, the roaring of the lion's roar is the teaching itself. The elder, in the manner stated in the immediately preceding sutta, only indicates the favor done to him by the Teacher, and not otherwise. For the great elder does not merely display the power of his own virtues. "The rest" means that which is not explained here. "In the former manner" means in the very manner stated in the immediately preceding sutta.

Cīvarasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Cīvarasutta is concluded.

12. Paraṃmaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā

12. Commentary on the Paraṃmaraṇasutta

155. Yathā atītakappe atītāsu jātīsu kammakilesavasena āgato, tathā etarahipi āgatoti tathāgato, yathā yathā vā pana kammaṃ katūpacitaṃ, tathā taṃ taṃ attabhāvaṃ āgato upagato upapannoti tathāgato, sattoti āha “tathāgatoti satto”ti. Etanti “evaṃ hoti bhavati tiṭṭhati sassatisama”nti evaṃ pavattaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ. Atthasannissitaṃ na hotīti diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikaparamatthato sukhanti pasatthasannissitaṃ na hoti. Ādibrahmacariyakanti ettha maggabrahmacariyaṃ adhippetaṃ tassa padhānabhāvato. Tassa pana etaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ ādipaṭipadāmattaṃ [M 2.0170] na hoti anupakārakattā vilomanato ca. Tato eva itarabrahmacariyassapi anissayova. Sesaṃ vuttanayena veditabbaṃ.

155. A 'Tathāgata' is so called because just as he came in past aeons, in past births, on account of kamma and defilements, so too he has come now. Or, in whatever way kamma was performed and accumulated, in that way he has come to, has reached, has been reborn in that very state of existence; thus he is a Tathāgata. He says, "A Tathāgata is a being." "This" refers to the speculative view that proceeds thus: "It is so, it becomes so, it persists, eternal and constant." "It is not connected with the goal" means it is not connected with what is praised as happiness from the perspective of this present life, the next life, and the ultimate truth. Regarding "fundamental to the holy life," here the holy life of the path is intended, due to its pre-eminence. However, this speculative view is not even the initial practice, because it is unhelpful and contrary. For that reason, it is no basis for any other holy life either. The rest should be understood in the manner already stated.

Paraṃmaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Paraṃmaraṇasutta is concluded.

13. Saddhammappatirūpakasuttavaṇṇanā

13. Commentary on the Saddhammappatirūpakasutta

156. Ājānāti heṭṭhimamaggehi ñātamariyādaṃ anatikkamitvāva jānāti paṭivijjhatīti aññā, aggamaggapaññā. Aññassa ayanti aññā, arahattaphalaṃ. Tenāha “arahatte”ti.

156. One knows thoroughly (ājānāti): without transgressing the limit known through the lower paths, one knows and penetrates—this is final knowledge (aññā), the wisdom of the highest path. The fruition of that final knowledge is also called aññā. Therefore, it is said, "in arahantship."

Obhāseti obhāsanimittaṃ. “Cittaṃ vikampatī”ti padadvayaṃ ānetvā sambandho. Obhāseti [V 2.0150] visayabhūte. Upakkilesehi cittaṃ vikampatīti yojanā. Tenāha “yehi cittaṃ pavedhatī”ti. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

"Illuminates" means the sign of illumination. The connection is made by supplying the two words "the mind trembles." When the illumination becomes the object, the mind trembles due to the corruptions—this is the construction. Therefore, it is said, "by which the mind is agitated." This same principle applies to the remaining cases.

Upaṭṭhāneti satiyaṃ. Upekkhāya cāti vipassanupekkhāya ca. Ettha ca vipassanācittasamuṭṭhānasantānavinimuttaṃ pabhāsanaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ obhāso. Ñāṇādayo vipassanācittasampayuttāva. Sakasakakicce saviseso hutvā pavatto adhimokkho saddhādhimokkho. Upaṭṭhānaṃ sati. Upekkhāti āvajjanupekkhā. Sā hi āvajjanacittasampayuttā cetanā. Āvajjanaajjhupekkhanavasena pavattiyā idha “āvajjanupekkhā”ti vuccati. Puna upekkhāyāti vipassanupekkhāva anena samajjhattatāya evaṃ vuttā. Nikanti nāma vipassanāya nikāmanā apekkhā. Sukhumatarakileso vā siyā duviññeyyo.

"Establishment" (upaṭṭhāna) means mindfulness. "And with equanimity" means with insight-equanimity. Here, the illumination (obhāso) is a radiance, a form-object, separate from the mental continuum that arises from the insight-consciousness. Knowledge and the other states are associated only with the insight-consciousness. Determination (adhimokkho), having become distinct in its own function, proceeds as the determination of faith. "Establishment" (upaṭṭhāna) is mindfulness. "Equanimity" refers to the equanimity of advertence. For it is the volition associated with the adverting consciousness. Because it proceeds by way of adverting and overlooking, it is here called "equanimity of advertence." Again, "with equanimity" refers to insight-equanimity itself, so called on account of its neutrality. "Craving" (nikanti) is the desire or longing for insight. Or it may be a very subtle, hard-to-discern defilement.

Imāni dasa ṭhānānīti imāni obhāsādīni upakkilesuppattiyā ṭhānāni upakkilesavatthūni. Paññā yassa paricitāti yassa paññā paricitavatī yāthāvato jānāti. “Imāni nissāya addhā maggappatto phalappatto aha”nti pavattaadhimāno dhammuddhaccaṃ dhammūpanissayo vikkhepo. Tattha kusalo hi taṃ yāthāvato jānanto na ca tattha sammohaṃ gacchati.

"These ten grounds" means these grounds beginning with illumination are occasions and bases for the arising of corruptions. "One whose wisdom is well-practiced" means one whose wisdom is mature and who knows things as they really are. The conceit that arises, "Relying on these, I have surely attained the path and the fruit," is agitation concerning the Dhamma, a distraction that has the Dhamma as its basis. In this matter, the skilled person, knowing it as it really is, does not become confused about it.

Adhigamasaddhammappatirūpakaṃ [M 2.0171] nāma anadhigate adhigatamānibhāvāvahattā. Yadaggena vipassanāñāṇassa upakkileso, tadaggena paṭipattisaddhammappatirūpakotipi sakkā viññātuṃ. Dhātukathāti mahādhātukathaṃ vadati. Vedallapiṭakanti vetullapiṭakaṃ. Taṃ nāgabhavanato ānītanti vadanti. Vādabhāsitanti apare. Abuddhavacanaṃ buddhavacanena virujjhanato. Na hi sambuddho pubbāparaviruddhaṃ vadati. Tattha sallaṃ upaṭṭhapenti kilesavinayaṃ na sandissati, aññadatthu kilesuppattiyā paccayo hotīti.

It is called a counterfeit of the true Dhamma of attainment because it produces conceit about having attained what has not been attained. To the extent that it is a corruption of insight-knowledge, it can also be understood as a counterfeit of the true Dhamma of practice. "Discourse on the elements" refers to the Mahādhātukathā. "Vedalla Piṭaka" means the Vetulla Piṭaka. Some say it was brought from the realm of the Nāgas. Others say it is mere debate-talk. It is not the word of the Buddha because it contradicts the word of the Buddha. For a Perfectly Enlightened One does not speak in a way that is internally contradictory. In it, they establish a dart; the removal of defilements is not seen, but on the contrary, it becomes a condition for the arising of defilements.

Avikkayamānanti vikkayaṃ agacchantaṃ. Tanti suvaṇṇabhaṇḍaṃ.

Avikkayamāna means not going to sale. Tanti means a golden ornament.

Na sakkhiṃsu ñāṇassa avisadabhāvato. Esa nayo ito paresupi.

They were not able to realize it due to the unclarity of their knowledge. This same principle applies in the subsequent cases.

Idāni “bhikkhū paṭisambhidāppattā ahesu”ntiādinā vuttameva atthaṃ kāraṇato vibhāvetuṃ puna “paṭhamabodhiyaṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha paṭipattiṃ pūrayiṃsūti atīte kadā te paṭisambhidāvahaṃ [V 2.0151] paṭipattiṃ pūrayiṃsu? Paṭhamabodhikālikā bhikkhū. Na hi attasammāpaṇidhiyā pubbekatapuññatāya ca vinā tādisaṃ bhavati. Esa nayo ito paresupi. Tadā paṭipattisaddhammo antarahito nāma bhavissatīti etena ariyamaggena āsannā eva pubbabhāgapaṭipadā paṭipattisaddhammoti dasseti.

Now, in order to explain with reasons the meaning already stated, beginning with "the monks had attained the analytical knowledges," the passage beginning "For at the time of the first enlightenment..." was spoken. Here, regarding "they fulfilled the practice": when in the past did they fulfill the practice that brings the analytical knowledges? The monks at the time of the first enlightenment. For such a thing does not happen without a proper aspiration for oneself and merit made in the past. This same principle applies in the subsequent cases as well. By the statement, "Then the true Dhamma of practice will have disappeared," it is shown that the true Dhamma of practice is the preliminary practice which is near to the noble path.

Dvīsūti suttābhidhammapiṭakesu antarahitesupi. Anantarahitameva adhisīlasikkhāyaṃ ṭhitassa itarasikkhādvayasamuṭṭhāpitato. Kiṃ kāraṇāti kena kāraṇena, aññasmiṃ dhamme antarahite aññatarassa dhammassa anantaradhānaṃ vuccatīti adhippāyo. Paṭipattiyā paccayo hoti anavasesato paṭipattikkamassa paridīpanato. Paṭipatti adhigamassa paccayo visesalakkhaṇapaṭivedhabhāvato. Pariyattiyeva pamāṇaṃ sāsanassa ṭhitiyāti adhippāyo.

Dvīsu means even if the Sutta and Abhidhamma Piṭakas were lost. The training in higher virtue remains, since it gives rise to the other two trainings. What is the reason? By what reason is it said that when one dhamma disappears, another dhamma does not disappear?—this is the intention. It is a condition for practice because it fully illuminates the progression of practice. Practice is the condition for attainment because of its nature of penetrating specific characteristics. The texts alone are the measure of the Teaching's duration—this is the meaning.

Nanu ca sāsanaṃ osakkitaṃ pariyattiyā vattamānāyāti adhippāyo. Anārādhakabhikkhūti sīlamattassapi na ārādhako dussīlo. Imasminti imasmiṃ pātimokkhe. Vattantāti “sīlaṃ akopetvā ṭhitā atthī”ti pucchi.

"But is the Dispensation weakened while the texts are still present?"—this is the meaning. "Anārādhaka bhikkhu" means one who is not an accomplisher even of mere virtue, being immoral. "Imasmiṃ" means in this Pātimokkha. "Vattanti" means he asked, "Are there those who remain without violating the precepts?"

Etesūti [M 2.0172] evaṃ mahantesu sakalaṃ lokaṃ ajjhottharituṃ samatthesu catūsu mahābhūtesu. Tasmāti yasmā aññena kenaci atimahantenapi saddhammo na antaradhāyati, samayantarena pana vattabbameva natthi, tasmā. Evamāhāti idāni vuccamānākāraṃ vadati.

"Etesu" means among these four great elements, so vast as to be capable of pervading the entire world. "Tasmā" means because the true Dhamma does not disappear even by any other very great means, much less by anything lesser, therefore. "Evamāha" means he speaks in the manner now being described.

Ādānaṃ ādi, ādi eva ādikanti āha “ādikenāti ādānenā”ti. Heṭṭhāgamanīyāti adhobhāgagamanīyā, apāyadukkhassa saṃsāradukkhassa ca nibbattakāti attho. Gāravarahitāti garukārarahitā. Patissayanaṃ nīcabhāvena patibaddhavuttitā, patisso patissayoti atthato ekaṃ, so etesaṃ natthīti āha “appatissāti appatissayā anīcavuttikā”ti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

"Taking is the beginning; indeed, the beginning is ādika"—thus he says, "by 'ādika,' by taking." "Leading downward" means leading to the lower realms, producing the suffering of the lower realms and the suffering of saṃsāra—this is the meaning. "Devoid of reverence" means lacking respect. Patissayana means a way of life bound by lowliness; patisso and patissaya are one in meaning. "They do not have this"—thus he says, "appatissa means without deference, living without lowliness." The rest is easily understood.

Saddhammappatirūpakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Saddhammappaṭirūpaka Sutta is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

The Sāratthappakāsinī, Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Kassapasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The exposition of hidden meanings in the Commentary on the Kassapa Saṃyutta is completed.

6. Lābhasakkārasaṃyuttaṃ

6. The Saṃyutta on Gains and Honor

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Dāruṇasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Dāruṇa Sutta

157. Thaddhoti [V 2.0152][M 2.0173] kakkhaḷo aniṭṭhassa padānato. Catupaccayalābhoti catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ paṭilābho. Sakkāroti tehiyeva paccayehi susaṅkhatehi pūjanā, so pana atthato sampattiyevāti āha “tesaṃyeva…pe… lābho”ti. Vaṇṇaghosoti guṇakittanā. Antarāyassa anativattanato antarāyiko anatthāvahattā.

157. "Thaddho" means harsh, because it gives what is undesirable. "Catupaccayalābho" is the acquisition of the four requisites. "Sakkāro" means honoring with those very well-prepared requisites, which in essence is indeed attainment—hence it is said, "the gain of those very…(requisites)." "Vaṇṇaghoso" is the proclamation of virtues. It is an obstacle (antarāyiko) because of not overcoming danger and because it brings harm.

Dāruṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Dāruṇa Sutta is concluded.

2. Baḷisasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Baḷisa Sutta

158. Baḷisena carati, tena vā jīvatīti bāḷisiko. Tenāha “baḷisaṃ gahetvā caramāno”ti. Āmisagatanti āmisūpagataṃ āmisapatitaṃ. Tenāha “āmisamakkhita”nti. Bhinnādhikaraṇānampi bāhiratthasamāso hotevāti āha “āmise cakkhudassana”nti. Ayo vuccati sukhaṃ, tabbidhuratāya anayo, dukkhanti āha “dukkhaṃ patto”ti. Assāti etena. Kattuatthe hi etaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Yathā kilesā vattanti, evaṃ pavattamāno puggalo kilesavippayogo na hotīti vuttaṃ “yathā kilesamārassa kāmo, evaṃ kattabbo”ti.

158. A `bāḷisiko` (fisherman) is one who `baḷisena carati, tena vā jīvati`, moves with a hook or lives by it. Therefore it is said, "moving while carrying a hook." "Āmisagata" means approached by bait, fallen upon bait—thus, "smeared with bait." Even when the components have a different locus, an external compound can still be formed—thus, "seeing with the eye for bait." "Ayo" is said to be happiness; its lack is "anayo," meaning suffering—thus, "attained suffering." `Assā`ti: this is a genitive case used in the sense of the agent. Just as defilements proceed, so a person proceeding thus is not separated from defilements—it is said, "as is the desire of Māra in the form of the defilements, so must it be done."

Baḷisasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Baḷisa Sutta is concluded.

3-4. Kummasuttādivaṇṇanā

3–4. Commentary on the Kumma Sutta and Others

159-160. Aṭṭhikacchapā vuccanti yesaṃ kapālamatthake tikhiṇā aṭṭhikoṭi hoti, tesaṃ samūho aṭṭhikacchapakulaṃ. Macchakacchapādīnaṃ sarīre lambantī papatatīti papatā, vuccamānākāro [V 2.0153] ayakaṇṭako. Ayakosaketi [M 2.0174] ayomayakosake. Kaṇṇikasallasaṇṭhānoti attanikāpanasallasaṇṭhāno. Ayakaṇṭakoti ayomayavaṅkakaṇṭako. Nikkhamati ettha athāvarato. Pavesitamatto hi so. Idāni tvaṃ “amhāka”nti na vattabbo. Ito anantarasutteti catutthasuttamāha.

159–160. "Aṭṭhikacchapā" refers to those whose skulls have sharp bone-points; their group is called the "aṭṭhikacchapakula." "Papatā" means that which hangs or falls from the bodies of fish, turtles, and so on—this refers to the type of thing called an "ayakaṇṭako" (iron thorn). "Ayakosake" means in an iron sheath. "Kaṇṇikasallasaṇṭhāno" refers to the shape of a barbed dart for self-entrapment. "Ayakaṇṭako" means an iron hooked-thorn. "Nikkhamati" here means emerging from an unfixed place, for it is merely inserted. Now, you should not be spoken of as "ours." The sutta immediately following this refers to the fourth sutta.

Kummasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kumma Sutta and Others is concluded.

5. Mīḷhakasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Mīḷhaka Sutta

161. Mīḷhakāti evaṃ itthiliṅgavasena vuccamānā. Gūthapāṇakāti gūthabhakkhapāṇakā. Antoti kucchiyaṃ.

161. "Mīḷhakā" is spoken thus in the feminine gender. "Gūthapāṇakā" means creatures that eat excrement. "Anto" means in the belly.

Mīḷhakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Mīḷhaka Sutta is concluded.

6. Asanisuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Asani Sutta

162. “Ime lābhasakkāraṃ anāharantā jighacchādidukkhaṃ pāpuṇantū”ti evaṃ na sattānaṃ dukkhakāmatāya evamāhāti ānetvā sambandho. Anantadukkhaṃ anubhoti aparāparaṃ uppajjanakaakusalacittānaṃ bahubhāvato.

162. The connection is made by bringing in the following: he said, "May these beings, not receiving gain and honor, experience hunger and other pains," not out of a desire for the suffering of beings. One experiences endless suffering because of the abundance of unwholesome thoughts that arise again and again.

Asanisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Asani Sutta is concluded.

7. Diddhasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Diddha Sutta

163. Acchavisayuttāti vā diddhe gatena gatadiddhena. Tenāha “visamakkhitenā”ti.

163. "Acchavisayuttā" means gone with what is smeared, gone smeared. Therefore, it is said, "smeared with poison."

Diddhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Diddha Sutta is concluded.

8. Siṅgālasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Siṅgāla Sutta

164. Jarasiṅgālotveva [M 2.0175] vuccati sarīrasobhāya abhāvato. Sarīrassa uggatakaṇṭakattā ukkaṇṭakena nāma. Phuṭatīti phalati bhijjati.

164. It is called a "Jarasiṅgāla" (old jackal) because of the lack of bodily beauty. Because its body has projecting thorns, it is named "Ukkaṇṭaka." "Phuṭati" means it bursts, it breaks apart.

Siṅgālasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Siṅgāla Sutta is concluded.

9. Verambhasuttavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Verambha Sutta.

165. Kāyaṃ [V 2.0154] na rakkhati nāma chabbīsatiyā sāruppānaṃ pariccajanato. Vācaṃ na rakkhati nāma rāgasāmantā ca kodhasāmantā ca yāva nicchāraṇato.

165. 'Does not guard the body' means by abandoning the twenty-six suitable things. 'Does not guard speech' means from the vicinity of lust and anger up to the point of utterance.

Verambhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Verambha Sutta is concluded.

10. Sagāthakasuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Sutta with Verses.

166. “Yassa sakkariyamānassā”ti ettha asakkārena cūbhayanti asakkārena ca ubhayañca, kadāci sakkārena, kadāci asakkārena kadāci ubhayenāti attho. Tenāha “asakkārenā”tiādi. Satatavihārānaṃ sampattiyā sātatikoti āha “arahatta…pe… sukhumadiṭṭhī”tiādi. Tathā hi sā “vajirūpamañāṇa”nti vuccati. Āgatattāti phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjituṃ tassā pubbaparikammaṃ upagatattā.

166. In the phrase 'For one who is honored': here, the meaning is sometimes with honor, sometimes with dishonor, and sometimes with both. Therefore, it is said, 'with dishonor,' and so on. Because of the attainment of constant abidings, he is continuous; it is said, 'arahantship... and so on... with subtle view,' and so on. For that is called 'the knowledge like a diamond.' 'Because of having arrived' means because of having undertaken the preliminary work for attaining the attainment of fruition.

Sagāthakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sutta with Verses is concluded.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Chapter is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1-2. Suvaṇṇapātisuttādivaṇṇanā

1–2. The Commentary on the Suvaṇṇapāti Sutta and Others.

167-168. Cāletuṃ na sakkoti sīlapabbatasannissitattā. Aññaṃ vā kiccaṃ karoti pageva sīlassa chaḍḍitattā. Tatiyādīsu apubbaṃ natthi.

167–168. One cannot be shaken, being established on the mountain of virtue. Or one performs another task, let alone abandoning virtue. In the third and subsequent suttas, there is nothing new.

Suvaṇṇapātisuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suvaṇṇapāti Sutta and Others is concluded.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Chapter is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

1. Mātugāmasuttavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Mātugāma Sutta.

170. Yaṃ [V 2.0155][M 2.0176] visabhāgavatthu purisassa cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhātuṃ sakkotīti vuccati, tato visesato lābhasakkārova sattānaṃ cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhātuṃ sakkotīti dassento bhagavā “na tassa, bhikkhave”tiādimavocāti dassento “na tassā”tiādimāha.

170. To show that, more than that which is called a disparate object capable of overwhelming a man's mind, gain and honor in particular are capable of overwhelming the minds of beings, the Blessed One said, 'Not that, monks,' and so on. To explain this, the commentary says, 'Not for her,' and so on.

Mātugāmasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Mātugāma Sutta is concluded.

2. Kalyāṇīsuttavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Kalyāṇī Sutta.

171. Dutiyaṃ uttānameva, tasseva atthassa kevalaṃ janapadakalyāṇīvasena vuttaṃ.

171. The second sutta is self-evident; it is simply the same meaning stated in terms of the 'belle of the country'.

Kalyāṇīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kalyāṇī Sutta is concluded.

3-6. Ekaputtakasuttādivaṇṇanā

3–6. The Commentary on the Ekaputtaka Sutta and Others.

172-175. Saddhāti ariyamaggena āgatasaddhā adhippetāti āha “sotāpannā”ti.

172–175. By 'faith' is meant the faith that comes by way of the noble path; therefore, it is said, 'stream-enterers'.

Ekaputtakasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Ekaputtaka Sutta and Others is concluded.

7. Tatiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Third Samaṇabrāhmaṇa Sutta.

176. Evamādīti ādi-saddena bāhusaccasaṃvarasīlādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Lābhasakkārassa samudayaṃ uppattikāraṇaṃ samudayasaccavasena dukkhasaccassa uppattihetutāvasena.

176. In the phrase 'and so on,' by the word 'so on' should be understood the inclusion of great learning, restraint, virtue, and so on. The origin of gain and honor is the cause of their arising, both in the sense of the truth of origination and in the sense of being the cause for the arising of the truth of suffering.

Tatiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Third Samaṇabrāhmaṇa Sutta is concluded.

8. Chavisuttavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Chavi Sutta.

177. Lābhasakkārasiloko [V 2.0156][M 2.0177] narakādīsu nibbattentoti idaṃ tannissayaṃ kilesagaṇaṃ sandhāyāha. Nibbattentoti nibbattāpento. Imaṃ manussaattabhāvaṃ nāseti manussattaṃ puna nibbattituṃ appadānavasena. Tasmāti duggatinibbattāpanato idha maraṇadukkhāvahanato ca.

177. When it is said, 'Gain, honor, and fame cause rebirth in hell and other such states,' this is said with reference to the mass of defilements that are dependent on them. 'Cause rebirth' (nibbattento) means 'causing to be reborn' (nibbattāpento). It destroys this human existence by not allowing for rebirth as a human again. Therefore, this is said because it causes rebirth in a woeful state and because it brings the suffering of death in this very life.

Chavisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chavi Sutta is concluded.

9. Rajjusuttavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Rajju Sutta.

178. Kharā pharusā chaviādīni chindane samatthā.

178. 'Harsh and rough' means capable of cutting the skin and so forth.

Rajjusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Rajju Sutta is concluded.

10. Bhikkhusuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Bhikkhu Sutta

179. Taṃ sandhāyāti diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārassa okāsābhāvaṃ sandhāya.

179. ‘With reference to that’ means with reference to the absence of an opportunity for dwelling happily in this very life.

Bhikkhusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Bhikkhu Sutta is concluded.

Tatiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Third Chapter is concluded.

4. Catutthavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter

1-4. Bhindisuttādivaṇṇanā

1–4. The Explanation of the Bhindi Sutta and Others

180-183. Devadatto sagge vā nibbatteyyātiādi parikappavacanaṃ. Na hi paccekabodhiyaṃ niyatagatiko antarā maggaphalāni adhigantuṃ bhabboti. Soti anavajjadhammo. Assāti devadattassa. Samucchedamagamā katūpacitassa mahato pāpadhammassa balena tasmiṃ attabhāve samucchedabhāvato, na accantāya. Akusalaṃ nāmetaṃ abalaṃ, kusalaṃ viya na mahābalaṃ, tasmā tasmiṃyeva attabhāve tādisānaṃ puggalānaṃ atekicchatā, aññathā sammattaniyāmo viya micchattaniyāmo accantiko [M 2.0178] siyā. Yadi evaṃ vaṭṭakhāṇukajotanā kathanti? Āsevanāvasena, tasmā [V 2.0157] yathā “sakiṃ nimuggo nimuggo eva bālo”ti vuttaṃ, evaṃ vaṭṭakhāṇukajotanā. Yādise hi paccaye paṭicca puggalo taṃ dassanaṃ gaṇhi, tathā ca paṭipanno, puna acintappativatte paccaye patitato sīsukkhipanamassa na hotīti na vattabbaṃ.

180–183. The statement ‘Would Devadatta be reborn in heaven?’ and so forth is a speculative utterance. For one whose destiny is fixed for Paccekabodhi, it is not possible to attain the paths and fruits in the interim. ‘He’ refers to one with blameless qualities. ‘His’ refers to Devadatta. ‘Came to utter destruction’ means that due to the power of the great evil deed he had done and accumulated, there was utter destruction in that very existence, but not permanently. This unwholesome deed is weak; it is not as greatly powerful as a wholesome deed. Therefore, for such persons in that very existence, there is no remedy. Otherwise, just as the right fixed destiny is permanent, so would the wrong fixed destiny be permanent. If so, how is the explanation of the simile of the turning post to be understood? It is by way of repeated practice. Therefore, just as it is said, ‘Once submerged, the fool is indeed submerged,’ so it is with the explanation of the simile of the turning post. For, regarding whatever conditions a person relies on to grasp that view and acts accordingly, it should not be said that there is no raising of his head again when he falls upon conditions that inconceivably revert.

Bhindisuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Bhindi Sutta and others is concluded.

5. Acirapakkantasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Acirapakkanta Sutta

184. Kāle sampatteti gabbhassa paripākagatattā vijāyanakāle sampatte. Potanti assatariyā puttaṃ. Etanti “gabbho assatariṃ yathā”ti etaṃ vacanaṃ.

184. ‘When the time has come’ means when the fetus has matured and the time for giving birth has arrived. ‘Foal’ means the offspring of a she-mule. ‘This’ refers to this statement: ‘as a fetus does to a she-mule’.

Acirapakkantasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Acirapakkanta Sutta is concluded.

6. Pañcarathasatasuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Pañcarathasata Sutta

185. Abhiharīyatīti abhihāro, bhattaṃyeva abhihāro bhattābhihāroti āha “abhiharitabbaṃ bhatta”nti. Macchapittanti vāḷamacchapittaṃ. Pakkhipeyyunti uragādinā osiñceyyuṃ.

185. ‘It is brought forward,’ thus it is an offering (`abhihāro`). An offering of food is a `bhattābhihāro`; therefore, it is said, ‘food to be brought forward.’ ‘Fish gall’ means the gall of a fierce fish. ‘They would throw in’ means they would sprinkle it with snakes and so forth.

Pañcarathasatasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Pañcarathasata Sutta is concluded.

7-13. Mātusuttādivaṇṇanā

7–13. The Explanation of the Mātu Sutta and Others

186-187. Mātupi hetūti attano mātuyā uppannaanatthāvahassa pahānahetupi. Ito paresūti “pitupi hetū”ti evamādīsu.

186–187. ‘Even for the mother’s sake’ means for the sake of abandoning what is harmful that has arisen on account of one’s own mother. ‘In the following cases’ means in such phrases as ‘even for the father’s sake’ and so on.

Mātusuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Mātu Sutta and others is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

Of the Sāratthappakāsinī, the Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya

Lābhasakkārasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The exposition of the hidden meanings in the explanation of the Lābhasakkāra Saṃyutta is concluded.

7. Rāhulasaṃyuttaṃ

7. The Rāhula Saṃyutta

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1-8. Cakkhusuttādivaṇṇanā

1–8. The Explanation of the Cakkhu Sutta and Others

188-195. Ekavihārīti [V 2.0158][M 2.0179] catūsupi iriyāpathesu ekākī hutvā viharanto. Vivekaṭṭhoti vivittaṭṭho, tenāha “nissaddo”ti. Satiyā avippavasantoti satiyā avippavāsena ṭhito, sabbadā avijahanavasena pavatto. Ātāpīti vīriyasampannoti sabbaso kilesānaṃ ātāpanaparitāpanavasena pavattavīriyasamaṅgībhūto. Pahitattoti tasmiṃ visesādhigame pesitacitto, tattha ninno tappabbhāroti attho. Hutvā abhāvākārenāti uppattito pubbe avijjamāno paccayasamavāyena hutvā uppajjitvā bhaṅguparamasaṅkhātena abhāvākārena. Aniccanti niccadhuvatābhāvato. Uppādavayavantatāyāti khaṇe khaṇe uppajjitvā nirujjhanato. Tāvakālikatāyāti taṅkhaṇikatāya. Vipariṇāmakoṭiyāti vipariṇāmavantatāya. Cakkhuñhi upādāya vikārāpajjanena vipariṇamantaṃ vināsaṃ paṭipīḷaṃ pāpuṇāti. Niccapaṭikkhepatoti niccatāya paṭikkhipitabbato lesamattassapi anupalabbhanato. Dukkhamanaṭṭhenāti nirantaradukkhatāya dukkhena khamitabbato. Dukkhavatthukaṭṭhenāti nānappakāradukkhādhiṭṭhānato. Satatasampīḷanaṭṭhenāti abhiṇhatāpasabhāvato. Sukhapaṭikkhepenāti sukhabhāvassa paṭikkhipitabbato. Taṇhāgāho mamaṃkārabhāvato. Mānagāho ahaṃkārabhāvato. Diṭṭhigāho “attā me”ti vipallāsabhāvato. Virāgavasenāti virāgaggahaṇena. Tathā vimuttivasenāti vimuttiggahaṇena.

188–195. ‘Dwelling alone’ means dwelling as a solitary being in all four postures. ‘Secluded’ means being in a secluded place; therefore he said, ‘without sound.’ ‘Not departing from mindfulness’ means established by not departing from mindfulness, proceeding by way of constant non-abandonment. ‘Ardent’ means endowed with energy, that is, possessed of the energy that proceeds by way of burning and tormenting all defilements. ‘Of resolute self’ means one whose mind is directed toward attaining that distinction; the meaning is that one is inclined and devoted to that goal. ‘Having come to be, it passes away’ means that, not existing before its arising, it comes to be through a conjunction of conditions, and then ceases by way of non-existence, which is characterized as cessation upon dissolution. ‘Impermanent’ means because of the absence of permanence and stability. ‘Because it has arising and passing away’ means because it arises and ceases from moment to moment. ‘Because of its temporariness’ means because it is momentary. ‘Because it ends in change’ means because it possesses change. For the eye, being dependent, through the onset of alteration and undergoing change, reaches destruction and oppression. ‘Because of the rejection of permanence’ means because permanence is to be rejected, since not even a trace of it is found. ‘Suffering in the sense of being undesirable’ means because of its incessant painfulness, it must be endured with difficulty. ‘Because it is a basis for suffering’ means because it is the foundation for various kinds of suffering. ‘Because of its nature of constant oppression’ means because of its nature of continuous affliction. ‘By the rejection of pleasure’ means because the state of pleasure is to be rejected. ‘The grip of craving’ is from the state of ‘mine-making.’ ‘The grip of conceit’ is from the state of ‘I-making.’ ‘The grip of views’ is from the deluded state of ‘this is my self.’ ‘By way of dispassion’ means by the grasping of dispassion. ‘Likewise by way of liberation’ means by the grasping of liberation.

Pasādāva gahitā dvārabhāvappattassa adhippetattā. Sammasanacāracittaṃ dvārabhūtamanoti adhippāyo.

Only the sensitive faculties are taken because they are intended as having attained the state of a door. The meaning is that the mind that wanders in comprehension is the mind that has become a door.

Chaṭṭhe ārammaṇe tebhūmakadhammā sammasanacārassa adhippetattā. Yathā paṭhamasutte pañca pasādā gahitā, na sasambhāracakkhuādayo, evaṃ [M 2.0180] tatiyasutte na pasādavatthukacittameva gahitaṃ. Na [V 2.0159] taṃsampayuttā dhammā. Evañhi avadhāraṇaṃ sātthakaṃ hoti aññathā tena apanetabbassa abhāvato. Sabbatthāti sabbesu catutthasuttādīsu. Javanappattāti javanacittasaṃyuttā.

In the sixth object, phenomena of the three planes are intended for the wandering of comprehension. Just as in the first sutta the five sensitive faculties are taken, not the eye and so forth together with their components, so in the third sutta, it is not that only the mind based on the sensitive faculty is taken, nor are the associated mental factors. For in this way, the specification is meaningful; otherwise, there would be nothing to be excluded by it. ‘In all cases’ refers to all instances, such as in the fourth sutta and so forth. ‘Having reached javana’ means associated with javana-citta.

Cakkhusuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Cakkhu Sutta and others is concluded.

9. Dhātusuttavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Discourse on Elements

196. Ākāsadhātu rūpaparicchedatāya rūpapariyāpannanti adhippāyena “sesāhi rūpa”nti vuttaṃ. Nāmarūpanti tebhūmakaṃ nāmaṃ rūpañca kathitaṃ.

196. The space element is included in form because it delimits form; with this intention it is said, “the remaining, indeed, are form.” ‘Name-and-form’ refers to name and form in the three planes of existence.

Dhātusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Discourse on Elements is concluded.

10. Khandhasuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Discourse on the Aggregates.

197. Sabbasaṅgāhikaparicchedenāti dhammasaṅgaṇhanapariyāyena. Idhāti imasmiṃ sutte. Tebhūmakāti gahetabbā sammasanacārassa adhippetattā.

197. By "comprehensive inclusion" is meant by way of a method of gathering all phenomena. "Here" means in this discourse. "Pertaining to the three planes" should be understood, because it is intended as the sphere of reviewing contemplation.

Khandhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Aggregates is concluded.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Chapter is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter.

11. Anusayasuttavaṇṇanā

11. The Commentary on the Discourse on Underlying Tendencies.

200. Dutiyavagge attanoti āyasmā rāhulo attano saviññāṇakaṃ kāyaṃ dasseti. Parassāti parassa aviññāṇakakāyaṃ dasseti. Parasantāne vā arūpe dhamme aggahetvā rūpakāyameva gaṇhanto vadati. Apare “asaññasattānaṃ attabhāvaṃ sandhāya tathā vutta”nti vadanti. Purimenāti “imasmiṃ saviññāṇake kāye”ti iminā padena. Pacchimenāti “bahiddhā”ti iminā padena. Ete kilesāti ete [M 2.0181] diṭṭhitaṇhāmānasaññitā kilesā. Etesu vatthūsūti ajjhattabahiddhāvatthūsu. Samma…pe… passatīti pubbabhāge vipassanāñāṇena sammasanavasena, maggakkhaṇe abhisamayavasena suṭṭhu attapaccakkhena ñāṇena passati.

200. In the Second Chapter, by "oneself," the Venerable Rāhula indicates his own conscious body. By "another's," he indicates another's unconscious body. Or, without grasping the formless phenomena in another's continuum, he speaks, taking only the physical body. Others say, "It was said thus with reference to the state of existence of non-percipient beings." By "the former," it means by the phrase "in this conscious body." By "the latter," it means by the phrase "externally." By "these defilements," it means these defilements designated as views, craving, and conceit. By "in these bases," it means in the internal and external bases. By "rightly… sees," it means that in the preliminary stage, one sees by way of thorough investigation with insight knowledge, and at the moment of the path, one sees thoroughly by way of direct realization with knowledge as personal, direct experience.

Anusayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Underlying Tendencies is concluded.

12. Apagatasuttavaṇṇanā

12. The Commentary on the Discourse on Removal.

201. “Ahameta”nti [V 2.0160] ahaṃkārādīnaṃ anavasesappahānena accantameva apagataṃ.

201. By 'removed,' it means completely removed through the abandoning of I-making and so forth without remainder.

Apagatasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Removal is concluded.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Chapter is concluded.

Dvīsūti paṭhamavaggādīsu. Desanāya asekkhabhūmiyā desitattā asekkhabhūmi kathitā. Paṭhamoti paṭhamavaggo “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā”tiādinā āyācantassa, dutiyo anāyācantassa therassa ajjhāsayavasena kathito. Vimuttiparipācanīyadhammā nāma vivaṭṭasannissitā saddhindriyādayo. Tena pana vipassanāya kathitattā kathitā evāti. Taṃtaṃdesanānusārena hi thero te dhamme paripākaṃ pāpesi. Tathā hi bhagavā dutiyavaggaṃ anāyācitopi desesi.

By 'in the two,' it means in the first chapter and the next. Because the teaching was delivered at the level of the non-trainee, the level of the non-trainee is spoken of. The first chapter was spoken for the one requesting with, "Good, venerable sir, Blessed One," etc., while the second was spoken in accordance with the disposition of the elder, who did not request it. The qualities that ripen liberation are the faculties of faith and so on, which are dependent on the rolling back of saṃsāra. And because they are spoken of in relation to insight, they are thus spoken of. For, in accordance with those respective teachings, the elder brought those qualities to maturity. Indeed, the Blessed One taught the second chapter even without being requested.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

Of the Sāratthappakāsinī, the Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Rāhulasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Rāhula Saṃyutta is concluded.

8. Lakkhaṇasaṃyuttaṃ

8. The Connected Discourses with Lakkhaṇa.

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter.

1. Aṭṭhisuttavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Discourse on Bones.

202. Āyasmā [V 2.0161][M 2.0182] ca lakkhaṇotiādīsu “ko nāmāyasmā lakkhaṇo, kasmā ca ‘lakkhaṇo’ti nāmaṃ ahosi, ko cāyasmā moggallāno, kasmā ca sitaṃ pātvākāsī”ti taṃ sabbaṃ pakāsetuṃ “yvāya”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Lakkhaṇasampannenāti purisalakkhaṇasampannena.

202. In the phrases such as, "And the Venerable Lakkhaṇa," to explain all of it—"Who is this Venerable Lakkhaṇa? Why was he named 'Lakkhaṇa'? And who is the Venerable Moggallāna? And why did he manifest a smile?"—the passage beginning with "yvāyaṃ" is commenced. By "endowed with marks," it means endowed with the marks of a great man.

Īsaṃ hasitaṃ “sita”nti vuccatīti āha “mandahasita”nti. Aṭṭhisaṅkhalikanti nayidaṃ aviññāṇakaṃ aṭṭhisaṅkhalikamattaṃ, atha kho eko petoti āha “petaloke nibbatta”nti. Ete attabhāvāti petattabhāvā. Na āpāthaṃ āgacchantīti devattabhāvā viya na āpāthaṃ āgacchanti pakatiyā. Tesaṃ pana ruciyā āpāthaṃ āgaccheyyuṃ manussānaṃ. Dukkhābhibhūtānaṃ anāthabhāvadassanapadaṭṭhānā karuṇāti āha “kāruññe kattabbe”ti. Attano ca sampattiṃ buddhañāṇassa ca sampattinti paccekaṃ sampattisaddo yojetabbo. Tadubhayaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “taṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha attano sampattiṃ anussaritvā sitaṃ pātvākāsīti padaṃ ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Dhammadhātūti sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ sandhāya vadati. Dhammadhātūti vā dhammānaṃ sabhāvo.

A slight laugh is called a 'smile,' hence it is said, 'a gentle smile.' By 'a chain of bones,' this is not a mere inanimate chain of bones, but rather a single peta; hence it is said, 'reborn in the world of petas.' By 'these are their states of existence,' it means the states of existence of petas. By 'they do not come into range,' it means that, like the states of existence of devas, they do not naturally come into range. Yet, by their own inclination, they might come into the range of humans. For those overwhelmed by suffering, seeing their helplessness is the proximate cause for compassion; hence it is said, 'when compassion is to be shown.' 'And his own accomplishment, and the accomplishment of the Buddha's knowledge'—the word 'accomplishment' should be applied to each separately. To clarify both, the passage beginning with 'for that...' was spoken. There, the phrase 'having recollected his own accomplishment, he manifested a smile' should be brought in and connected. By 'Dhamma-element,' he speaks with reference to the knowledge of omniscience. Or, 'Dhamma-element' is the intrinsic nature of phenomena.

Itaroti lakkhaṇatthero. Upapattīti jāti. Upapattisīsena hi tathārūpaṃ attabhāvaṃ vadati. Lohatuṇḍakehīti lohamayeheva tuṇḍakehi. Carantīti ākāsena gacchanti. Acchariyaṃ vatāti garahacchariyaṃ nāmetaṃ. Cakkhubhūtāti sampattadibbacakkhukā, lokassa cakkhubhūtāti evaṃ vā ettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

By 'the other,' it means the Elder Lakkhaṇa. By 'rebirth,' it means birth. For he speaks of such a state of existence under the heading of 'rebirth.' By 'with iron beaks,' it means with beaks made of iron. By 'they roam,' it means they go through the sky. By 'Oh, what a marvel!,' this is a marvel of reproach. By 'have become eyes,' it means those who have attained the divine eye; or, the meaning here should be understood as 'have become the eye for the world'.

Yatrāti hetuatthe nipātoti āha “yatrāti kāraṇavacana”nti. Aññatra hi “yatra hi nāmā”ti attho vuccati. Appamāṇe sattanikāye te ca kho vibhāgena kāmabhavādibhede bhave, nirayādibhedā [V 2.0162] gatiyo, nānattakāyanānattasaññiādiviññāṇaṭṭhitiyo, tathārūpe sattāvāse ca sabbaññutaññāṇañca me upanetuṃ paccakkhaṃ karontena.

By 'yatra,' it is a particle in the sense of cause; hence he said, "'Yatra' is a word expressing a reason." For elsewhere, the meaning is expressed as "where indeed by name." ...by me, who brings near and makes directly perceptible the knowledge of omniscience concerning the immeasurable host of beings, and indeed, by division, the various existences such as the sensual realm, the destinations with their distinctions such as hell, the stations of consciousness such as those with diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, and such abodes of beings.

Goghātakoti [M 2.0183] gunnaṃ abhiṇhaṃ hananako. Tenāha “vadhitvā vadhitvā”ti. Tassāti gunnaṃ vadhakakammassa. Aparāpariyakammassāti aparāpariyavedanīyakammassa. Balavatā goghātakakammena vipāke dīyamāne aladdhokāsaṃ aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ tasmiṃ vipakkavipāke idāni laddhokāsaṃ “avasesakamma”nti vuttaṃ. Paṭisandhīti pāpakammajanitā paṭisandhi. Kammasabhāgatāyāti kammasadisabhāvena. Ārammaṇasabhāgatāyāti ārammaṇassa sabhāgabhāvena sadisabhāvena. Yādise hi ārammaṇe pubbe taṃ kammaṃ tassa ca vipāko pavatto, tādiseyeva ārammaṇe idaṃ kammaṃ imassa vipāko ca pavattoti katvā vuttaṃ “tasseva kammassa vipākāvasesenā”ti. Bhavati hi taṃsadisepi tabbohāro yathā “so eva tittiro, tāniyeva osadhānī”ti. Nimittaṃ ahosīti pubbe katūpacitassa petūpapattinibbattanavasena katokāsassa tassa kammassa nimittabhūtaṃ idāni tathā upaṭṭhahantaṃ tassa vipākassa nimittaṃ ārammaṇaṃ ahosi. Soti goghātako. Aṭṭhisaṅkhalikapeto jāto kammasarikkhakavipākatāvasena.

By 'cow-slaughterer,' it means one who frequently kills cows. Hence it is said, "having killed and killed." By 'of that,' it means of the kamma of killing cows. By 'of kamma to be experienced in a subsequent existence,' it means of kamma whose result is to be experienced in some subsequent existence. When the result was being produced by the powerful kamma of cow-slaughtering, the kamma to be experienced in a subsequent existence did not get an opportunity. Now, having obtained an opportunity in that ripened result, it is called 'residual kamma.' By 'rebirth-linking,' it means the rebirth-linking generated by unwholesome kamma. By 'due to the correspondence of the kamma,' it means due to the similar nature of the kamma. By 'due to the correspondence of the object,' it means due to the corresponding nature, the similar nature, of the object. For in whatever kind of object that kamma and its result previously occurred, it is because this kamma and its result now occur in the very same kind of object that it was said, "by the remainder of the result of that very kamma." For this designation is used even for something similar, as in 'that very partridge, those very herbs.' 'A sign arose' means: that which now appeared in such a way, having become a sign of that kamma previously performed and accumulated, which had been given the opportunity to generate rebirth as a peta, became the object as a sign of its result. By 'he,' it means the cow-slaughterer. He was born as a peta that is a chain of bones, due to the result being a likeness of the kamma.

Aṭṭhisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Bones is concluded.

2. Pesisuttavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Discourse on the Lump of Flesh.

203. Gomaṃsapesiyo katvāti gāviṃ vadhitvā vadhitvā gomaṃsaṃ phāletvā pesiyo katvā. Sukkhāpetvāti kālantaraṃ ṭhapanatthaṃ sukkhāpetvā. Sukkhāpiyamānānaṃ maṃsapesīnañhi vallūrasamaññā.

203. By 'having made lumps of cow meat,' it means having repeatedly killed a cow, having cut up the cow meat, and having made lumps. By 'having dried,' it means having dried it for the purpose of storing it for some time. Indeed, 'vallūra' is the designation for lumps of meat that are being dried.

Pesisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Lump of Flesh is concluded.

3. Piṇḍasuttavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Discourse on the Lump.

204. Nippakkhacammeti vigatapakkhacamme.

204. By 'a hide without feathers,' it means a hide from which the feathers have been removed.

4. Nicchavisuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Discourse on the Skinless One.

205. Urabbhe hanatīti orabbhiko. Eḷaketi aje.

205. “He kills sheep,” therefore he is a sheep-butcher. “Eḷaka” means goats.

5. Asilomasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Asilomasutta.

206. Nivāpapuṭṭheti [V 2.0163][M 2.0184] attanā dinnanivāpena posite. Asinā vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇanto.

206. “Nivāpapuṭṭha” means nourished with bait given by oneself. Repeatedly killing with a sword and selling.

6. Sattisuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Sattisutta.

207. Ekaṃ miganti ekaṃ dīpakamigaṃ.

207. “Ekaṃ migaṃ” means a spotted deer.

7. Usulomasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Usulomasutta.

208. Kāraṇāhīti yātanāhi. Ñatvāti kammaṭṭhānaṃ ñatvā.

208. “Kāraṇāhi” means by torments. “Ñatvā” means having known the meditation subject.

8. Sūcilomasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Sūcilomasutta.

209. Suṇoti pūretīti sūto, assadamakādiko.

209. “Because he hears and fulfills, he is a sūta; a horse-tamer, or the like.”

9. Dutiyasūcilomasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Second Sūcilomasutta.

210. Pesuññūpasaṃhāravasena ito sutaṃ amutra, amutra vā sutaṃ idha sūcetīti sūcako. Anayabyasanaṃ pāpesi manusseti sambandho.

210. By way of slander, he reports what is heard here elsewhere, or what is heard elsewhere here, thus he is an informer. The connection is that he leads people to misfortune and ruin.

10. Kumbhaṇḍasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Kumbhaṇḍasutta.

211. Vinicchayāmaccoti raññā aḍḍakaraṇe ṭhapito vinicchayamahāmatto. So hi gāmajanakāyaṃ kūṭeti vañcetīti gāmakūṭakoti vuccati. Keci “tādiso eva gāmajeṭṭhako gāmakūṭako”ti vadanti. Samena bhavitabbaṃ, “dhammaṭṭho”ti vattabbato. Rahassaṅge nisīdanavasena visamā nisajjāva ahosi.

211. “Vinicchayāmacca” means a deciding magistrate appointed by the king to judge cases. He oppresses and deceives the villagers, hence he is called a village-oppressor. Some say, “Such a one is indeed the village headman, the village-oppressor.” One should be even-handed, as one should be called “righteous.” Because of his practice of sitting in secret, his very sitting became uneven.

Kumbhaṇḍasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kumbhaṇḍasutta is concluded.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the First Chapter is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter.

1. Sasīsakasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Sasīsakasutta.

212. Phusantoti [V 2.0164][M 2.0185] theyyāya phusanto.

212. “Phusanto” means touching with thieving intent.

3. Nicchavitthisuttavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Nicchavitthisutta.

214. Mātugāmo sassāmiko attano phasse anissaro. Vaṭṭitvāti bhassitvā aparaṃ gantvā.

214. A woman who has a husband has no control over her own bodily contact. “Vaṭṭitvā” means having spoken and then gone elsewhere.

4. Maṅgulitthisuttavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Maṅgulitthisutta.

215. Maṅganavasena ulatīti maṅguli, virūpabībhacchabhāvena pavattatīti attho. Tenāha “virūpaṃ duddasikaṃ bībhaccha”nti.

215. “Because it moves by way of infatuation, it is ‘maṅguli’; the meaning is that it proceeds in a deformed and disgusting manner. Therefore, it is said: ‘deformed, difficult to look at, disgusting.’”

5. Okilinīsuttavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Okilinīsutta.

216. Uddhaṃ uddhaṃ agginā pakkasarīratāya uppakkaṃ. Heṭṭhato paggharaṇavasena kilinnasarīratāya okilinī. Ito cito ca aṅgārasamparikiṇṇatāya okirinī. Tenāha “sā kirā”tiādi. Aṅgāracitaketi aṅgārasañcaye. Sarīrato paggharanti asuciduggandhajegucchāni sedagatāni. Tassa kira raññoti tassa kāliṅgassa rañño. Nāṭakinīti nacce adhikatā itthī. Sedanti sedanaṃ, tāpananti attho.

216. Upwards, because the body is roasted by fire, it is scorched. From below, by way of oozing, because the body is drenched, she is an ‘okilinī.’ Here and there, because of being completely strewn with embers, she is an ‘okirinī.’ Therefore, it is said, “she indeed,” and so on. “Aṅgāracitake” means on a heap of embers. From the body ooze impure, foul-smelling, and disgusting secretions. “Tassa kira rañño” means of that king of Kāliṅga. “Nāṭakinī” means a woman skilled in dancing. “Seda” means torment; the meaning is burning.

Okilinīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Okilinīsutta is concluded.

6. Asīsakasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Asīsakasutta.

217. Asīsakaṃ kabandhaṃ hutvā nibbatti kammāyūhanakāle tathā nimittaggahaṇaparicayato.

217. He was reborn as a headless trunk at the time of the accumulation of kamma, owing to his familiarity with grasping the sign in that way.

7-11. Pāpabhikkhusuttādivaṇṇanā

7-11. Commentary on the Pāpabhikkhusutta and others.

218-222. Lāmakabhikkhūti [V 2.0165][M 2.0186] hīnācāratāya lāmako, bhikkhuvesatāya, bhikkhāhārena jīvanato ca bhikkhu. Cittakeḷinti cittaruciyaṃ taṃ taṃ kīḷanto. Ayamevāti bhikkhuvatthusmiṃ vuttanayo eva.

218-222. “Lāmakabhikkhu” means one who is base because of inferior conduct, and a bhikkhu because of his appearance and his living on alms-food. “Cittakeḷi” means playing with this and that according to the mind’s fancy. “Ayameva” means the very same method as stated in the section on bhikkhus.

Pāpabhikkhusuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Pāpabhikkhusutta and others is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

The Sāratthappakāsinī, Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Lakkhaṇasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Lakkhaṇa Saṃyutta Commentary, Exposition of Hidden Meaning, is concluded.

9. Opammasaṃyuttaṃ

9. The Simile Saṃyutta.

1. Kūṭasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Kūṭa Sutta.

223. Kūṭaṃ [V 2.0166][M 2.0187] gacchantīti kūṭacchiddassa anupavisanavasena kūṭaṃ gacchanti. Yā ca gopānasiyo gopānasantaragatā, tāpi kūṭaṃ āhacca ṭhānena kūṭaṅgamā. Duvidhāpi kūṭe samosaraṇā. Kūṭassa samugghātena vināsena bhijjanena. Avijjāya samugghātenāti avijjāya accantameva appavattiyā. Tena ca mokkhadhammādhigamena tadanurūpadhammādhigamo dassito. Appamattāti pana iminā tassa upāyo dassito.

223. ‘They go to the summit’ means they go to the summit by way of entering the opening of the summit. And those rafters that are set between the rafters also reach the summit by their position, becoming summit-goers. Both kinds converge at the summit. By the uprooting, destruction, and breaking of the summit. ‘By the uprooting of ignorance’ means by the complete non-occurrence of ignorance. And by that, through the attainment of the state of liberation, the attainment of a corresponding state is shown. But by this word ‘heedful,’ the means to that is shown.

Kūṭasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kūṭa Sutta is concluded.

2. Nakhasikhasuttavaṇṇanā

2. The commentary on the Nakhasikha Sutta.

224. Evaṃ appakā yathā nakhasikhāya āropitapaṃsu, sugatisaṃvattaniyassa kammassa appakattā evaṃ devesupīti hīnūdāharaṇavasena vuttaṃ. Appatarā hi sattā ye devesu jāyanti, tañca kho kāmadevesu. Itaresu pana vattabbameva natthi.

224. Just as the dust placed on a fingernail is little, so too are deeds conducive to a good destination—this is said by way of a lesser example, because of the scarcity of kamma conducive to a good destination even among the devas. For fewer are the beings who are born among the devas, and that too only among the devas of the sense-sphere. As for the others, there is nothing to be said.

Nakhasikhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Nakhasikha Sutta is concluded.

3. Kulasuttavaṇṇanā

3. The commentary on the Kula Sutta.

225. Vidhaṃsayanti viheṭhayanti. Vaḍḍhitāti bhāvanāpāripūrivasena paribrūhitā. Punappunaṃ katāti bhāvanāya bahulīkaraṇena aparāparaṃ pavattitā yuttayānaṃ viya katāti yathā yuttaṃ ājaññarathaṃ chekena sārathinā adhiṭṭhitaṃ yathāruci pavattati, evaṃ yathāruci pavattiyā gamitā. Patiṭṭhānaṭṭhenāti adhiṭṭhānaṭṭhena. Vatthu viya katā sabbaso upakkilesavisodhanena suvisodhitamariyādaṃ viya katā. Adhiṭṭhitāti paṭipakkhadūrībhāvato subhāvitabhāvena avikampaneyyatāya ṭhapitā[V 2.0167]. Samantato citāti sabbabhāgena bhāvanūpacayaṃ gamitā. Tenāha “suvaḍḍhitā”ti[M 2.0188]. Suṭṭhu samāraddhāti mettābhāvanāya matthakappattiyā sammadeva sampāditā.
