225. ‘They destroy’ means they harass. ‘Developed’ means brought to full growth through the perfection of development. ‘Done again and again’ means made frequent through repeated development; ‘made like a yoked vehicle’ means that just as a well-yoked thoroughbred chariot, controlled by a skilled charioteer, proceeds as desired, so it is guided to proceed according to desire. ‘As a foundation’ means by way of resolve. ‘Made like a ground’; ‘made like a well-purified boundary’ by the complete cleansing of all defilements. ‘Established’ means fixed so as to be unshakeable due to being well-developed, with opposition driven away. ‘Piled up all around’ means brought to the accumulation of development in every way. Therefore it is said, ‘well-developed.’ ‘Well undertaken’ means perfectly accomplished, having reached the summit in the development of loving-kindness.

Kulasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kula Sutta is concluded.

4. Okkhāsuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Okkhā Sutta.

226. Mahāmukhaukkhalīnanti mahāmukhānaṃ mahantakoḷumbānaṃ sataṃ. Paṇītabhojanabharitānanti sappimadhusakkarādīhi upanītapaṇītabhojanehi paripuṇṇānaṃ. Tassāti pāṭhassa. Goduhanamattanti godohanavelāmattaṃ. Taṃ pana kittakaṃ adhippetanti āha “gāviyā”tiādi. Sabbasattesu hitapharaṇanti anodhisomettābhāvanamāha – mettacittaṃ appanāppattaṃ bhāvetuṃ sakkotīti adhippāyo. Tampi tato yathāvuttadānato mahapphalataranti.

226. ‘Of great-mouthed cooking pots’ means a hundred large bowls for great-mouthed ones. ‘Filled with excellent food’ means filled with the finest foods brought forth, such as ghee, honey, and sugar. ‘Of that’—so the reading. ‘Merely the time for milking a cow’ means only the time for milking a cow. But how much is intended by that? He says, ‘of a cow,’ and so forth. ‘Pervading with welfare for all beings’ refers to the development of boundless loving-kindness—the meaning is that one is capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness that has attained absorption. Even that is more fruitful than the aforementioned giving.

Okkhāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Okkhā Sutta is concluded.

5. Sattisuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Dart Sutta.

227. Agge paharitvāti tiṇhaphalasattiyā agge hatthena vā muṭṭhinā vā pahāraṃ datvā. Kappāsavaṭṭiṃ viyāti pahatakappāsapiṇḍaṃ viya. Niyyāsavaṭṭiṃ viyāti phalasaṇṭhānaṃ niyyāsapiṇḍaṃ viya. Ekato katvāti kalikādibhāvena vīsatiṃsapiṇḍāni ekajjhaṃ katvā. Alliyāpento piṇḍaṃ karonto. Paṭileṇetīti paṭilīnayati nāmeti. Alliyāpento te dvepi dhārā ekato samphusāpento. Paṭikoṭṭetīti paṭipaharati. Tattha khaṇḍaṃ viya niyyāso. Kappāsavaṭṭanakaraṇīyanti vihatassa kappāsassa paṭisaṃharaṇavasena bandhanadaṇḍaṃ. Pavattentoti kappāsassa saṃvellanavasena pavattento.

227. ‘Having struck at the tip’ means striking the tip of a sharp-bladed spear with the hand or fist. ‘Like a ball of cotton’ means like a lump of beaten cotton. ‘Like a ball of resin’ means like a lump of resin having the shape of a fruit. ‘Having made as one’ means making twenty or thirty lumps together in the form of buds. ‘Causing to adhere’ means forming a lump. ‘He bends back’ means he causes to lie back, he bends. ‘Causing to adhere’ means causing those two streams to touch together. ‘He strikes back’ means he strikes back. There, the resin is like a fragment. ‘The means for rolling the cotton’ refers to the binding stick for gathering together scattered cotton. ‘Causing to proceed’ means causing it to roll by rolling up the cotton.

Sattisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Satti Sutta is concluded.

6. Dhanuggahasuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Dhanuggaha Sutta.

228. Daḷhadhanunoti [M 2.0189] thirataradhanuno. Idāni tassa thiratarabhāvaṃ paricchedato dassetuṃ “daḷhadhanū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dvisahassathāmanti palānaṃ dvisahassathāmaṃ. Vuttamevatthaṃ pākaṭataraṃ katvā dassetuṃ “yassā”tiādimāha. Tattha yassāti dhanuno. Āropitassāti jiyaṃ āropitassa. Jiyābaddhoti jiyāya baddho. Pathavito muccati, etaṃ “dvisahassathāma”nti veditabbaṃ[V 2.0168]. Lohasīsādīnanti kāḷalohatambalohasīsādīnaṃ. Bhāroti purisabhāro, so pana majjhimapurisassa vasena edisaṃ tassa balaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Uggahitasippā dhanuvedasikkhāvasena. Ciṇṇavasībhāvā lakkhesu avirajjhanasarakkhepavasena. Kataṃ rājakulādīsu upagantvā asanaṃ sarakkhepo etehīti katūpasanāti āha “rājakulādīsu dassitasippā”ti.

228. ‘Of a strong bow’ means of an exceedingly strong bow. Now, to show its exceedingly strong nature by way of definition, ‘a strong bow’ and so forth is said. Here, ‘having the strength of two thousand’ means having the strength of two thousand palas. To show this same meaning more clearly, he said ‘of which’ and so forth. Here, ‘of which’ refers to the bow. ‘Of which has been strung’ means of which the string has been fitted. ‘Bound by the string’ means bound by the string. It is released from the ground; this should be understood as ‘having the strength of two thousand.’ ‘Of lead and other metals’ refers to black iron, copper, lead, and other metals. ‘A load’ means a man’s load, but its strength should be seen as such in relation to a man of medium build. ‘Those who have grasped the art’ means by way of training in the science of the bow. ‘Those who have attained mastery through practice’ means by way of releasing arrows without missing the targets. ‘Those by whom the shooting has been done, having approached royal courts, etc.’ is the meaning of ‘katūpasana’; thus he says, ‘those who have demonstrated their art in royal courts, etc.’

“Bodhisatto cattāri kaṇḍāni āharī”ti vatvā tameva atthaṃ vitthārato dassento “tadā kirā”tiādimāha. Tattha javissāmāti dhāvissāma. Aggi uṭṭhahīti sīghapatanasantāpena ca sūriyarasmisantāpassa āsannabhāvena ca usumā uṭṭhahi. Pakkhapañjarenāti pakkhajālantarena.

Having stated, ‘The Bodhisatta brought four arrows,’ and in order to show that same meaning in detail, he said ‘then, it is said’ and so forth. Here, ‘we will speed’ means ‘we will run.’ ‘Fire arose’ means heat arose from the heat of the swift fall and from the nearness of the heat of the sun’s rays. ‘With a cage of wings’ means with the space between the web of wings.

Nivattitvāti “nippayojanamidaṃ javana”nti nivattitvā. Pattakaṭāhena otthaṭapatto viyāti pihitapatto viya ahosi, vegasā patanena nagarassa upari ākāsassa nirikkhaṇaṃ ahosi. Sañcāritattā anekahaṃsasahassasadiso paññāyi seyyathāpi bodhisattassa dhanuggahakāle sarakūṭādidassane.

‘Having turned back’ means turning back, thinking, ‘This running is useless.’ ‘Like a bowl covered by a pot-lid’ means he was like a covered bowl; due to falling with speed, there was a looking up at the sky above the city. Because of moving about, he appeared like many thousands of swans, just as in the seeing of the arrow-tips and so forth at the time the Bodhisatta took up the bow.

Dukkaranti tassa adassanaṃ sandhāyāha, na attano patanaṃ. Sūriyamaṇḍalañhi atisīghena javena gacchantampi paññāsayojanāyāmavitthataṃ attano vipulatāya pabhassaratāya ca sattānaṃ cakkhussa gocarabhāvaṃ gacchati, javanahaṃso pana tādisena sūriyena saddhiṃ javena gacchanto na paññāyeyya. Tasmā vuttaṃ “na sakkā tayā passitu”nti. Cattāro akkhaṇavedhino. Gantvā gahite sotuṃ ghaṇḍaṃ piḷandhāpetvā sayaṃ puratthābhimukho nisinno. Puratthimadisābhimukhaṃ gatakaṇḍaṃ sandhāyāha “paṭhamakaṇḍeneva saddhiṃ uppatitvā”ti. Te cattāri kaṇḍāni ekakkhaṇeyeva khipiṃsu.

‘Difficult,’ he said, referring to its invisibility, not to his own fall. For even the sun’s disk, though moving with exceedingly swift speed and extending fifty leagues in length and width, becomes an object of the eye for beings due to its vast size and radiance. But a swift goose, moving with the same speed as such a sun, would not be visible. Therefore, it was said, ‘It is not possible for you to see him.’ Four archers who can pierce in an instant. Having gone, taken their positions, listened for the sound, put on the bell, and sat down facing east. Referring to the arrow that went towards the eastern direction, he said, ‘having flown up together with the first arrow.’ They shot those four arrows in a single moment.

Āyuṃ [M 2.0190] saṅkharoti etenāti āyusaṅkhāro. Yathā hi kammajarūpānaṃ pavatti jīvitindriyapaṭibaddhā, evaṃ attabhāvassa pavatti tappaṭibaddhāti. Bahuvacananiddeso pana pāḷiyaṃ ekasmiṃ khaṇe anekasatasaṅkhassa jīvitindriyassa upalabbhanato. Taṃ jīvitindriyaṃ. Tato yathāvuttadevatānaṃ javato sīghataraṃ khīyati ittarakhaṇattā. Vuttañhetaṃ –

‘By this one conditions life,’ hence ‘life-formation.’ Just as the continuity of kamma-born matter is dependent on the life faculty, so the continuity of individual existence is dependent on that. The plural designation in the Pāli text is due to the fact that in a single moment hundreds of life faculties are found. That is the life faculty. It wastes away more quickly than the speed of the aforementioned deities, due to its extremely brief momentariness. For it is said—

“Jīvitaṃ attabhāvo ca, sukhadukkhā ca kevalā;

Ekacittasamāyuttā, lahuso vattate khaṇo”ti. (mahāni. 10);

‘Life and individual existence, and all pleasure and pain, are conjoined with a single mind-moment; the moment passes swiftly.’

Bhedoti [V 2.0169] bhaṅgo. Na sakkā paññāpetuṃ tatopi ativiya ittarakhaṇattā.

‘Breaking’ means dissolution. It is impossible to describe it, because its momentariness is even more exceedingly brief than that.

Dhanuggahasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Dhanuggaha Sutta is concluded.

7. Āṇisuttavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Āṇi Sutta.

229. Aññe rājāno ca bhāgaṃ gaṇhantā ime viya dasabhāgaṃ gaṇhantīti tesamayaṃ anugati paññāyati. Mahājanassa ānayanato ānakoti āha “evaṃladdhanāmo”ti. Idāni taṃ ādito paṭṭhāya āgamanānukkamaṃ dassetuṃ “himavante kirā”tiādimāha. Kareṇunti kareṇukaṃ, hatthininti attho. Sakkariṃsūti anatthapariharaṇavasena pasatthūpahāravasena ca pūjesuṃ. Otarīti kuḷīradahaṃ pāvisi. Paṭikkamitvā ṭhapanavasena apakkamitvā pati.

229. Other kings, taking a portion, take a tenth part like these; thus their imitation is known. Because it brings a great multitude, it is called 'ānaka'; thus he said, 'it was so named.' Now, to show its sequence of arrival from the beginning, he said, 'Indeed, in the Himalayas...' and so on. 'Kareṇu' means 'kareṇuka,' that is, 'a female elephant.' 'Sakkariṃsu' means they worshipped by way of averting misfortune and by way of excellent offerings. 'Otarī' means he entered the Kuḷīra Lake. Having returned, by way of placing it, having departed, it fell.

Suvaṇṇarajatādimayanti kismiñci chidde suvaṇṇamayaṃ, kismiñci rajatamayaṃ, kismiñci phalikamayaṃ āṇiṃ ghaṭayiṃsu bandhiṃsu. Pubbe pharitvā tiṭṭhantassa dvādasa yojanāni pamāṇo etassāti dvādasayojanappamāṇo, saddo. Athassa anekasatakāle gacchante antosālāyampi dukkhena suyyittha āṇisaṅghāṭamattattā.

Made of gold, silver, and so on: into some hole they fashioned and fastened a golden peg, into another a silver peg, and into another a crystal peg. Previously, while it stood pervading, its sound had a measure of twelve yojanas, thus it was of twelve-yojana measure. Then, after many hundreds of years had passed, even inside the hall it was heard with difficulty because it was merely a mass of pegs.

Gambhīrāti agādhā dukkhogāḷhā. Sallasuttañhi “animittamanaññāta”ntiādinā pāḷivasena gambhīraṃ, na atthagambhīraṃ. Tathā hi tattha tā tā gāthā duviññeyyarūpā tiṭṭhanti, duviññeyyaṃ ñāṇena dukkhogāhanti katvā “gambhīra”nti [M 2.0191] vuccati. Pubbāparampettha kāsañci gāthānaṃ duviññeyyatāya dukkhogāhameva, tasmā taṃ pāḷivasena “gambhīra”nti vuttaṃ “pāḷivasena gambhīrā sallasuttasadisā”ti. Iminā nayena “atthavasena gambhīrā”ti ettha attho veditabbo. Mahāvedallasuttassa atthavasena gambhīratā pākaṭāyeva. Lokaṃ uttaratīti lokuttaro, navavidhaappamāṇadhammo, so atthabhūto etesaṃ atthīti lokuttarā. Tenāha “lokuttaraatthadīpakā”ti. Sattasuññatadhammamattamevāti sattena attanā suññataṃ kevalaṃ dhammamattameva. Uggahetabbaṃ pariyāpuṇitabbanti ca liṅgavacanavipallāsena vuttanti āha “uggahetabbe ca pariyāpuṇitabbe cā”ti. Kavitāti kavino kammaṃ kavikatā. Yassa pana yaṃ kammaṃ, taṃ tena katanti vuccatīti āha “kavitāti kavīhi katā”ti. Itaraṃ “kāveyyā”ti padaṃ, kabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. “Kabba”nti ca kavinā vuttanti attho. Tenāha “tasseva vevacana”nti. Cittakkharāti vicitrākāraakkharā. Sāsanato bahibhūtāti na sāsanāvacarā. Tesaṃ sāvakehīti “buddhānaṃ sāvakā”ti [V 2.0170] apaññātānaṃ yesaṃ kesañci sāvakehi. Anuggayhamānāti na uggayhamānā savanadhāraṇaparicayaatthūpaparikkhādivasena anuggayhamānā. Antaradhāyanti adassanaṃ gacchanti.

'Deep' means unfathomable, difficult to plunge into. Indeed, the Sallasutta is deep by way of its text, beginning with 'animittamanaññāta,' but not deep by way of its meaning. For there, those various verses stand in forms difficult to understand; and because what is difficult to understand is hard to grasp with knowledge, it is called 'deep.' And here, the connection between the beginning and end of some verses is difficult to understand, making it hard to grasp; therefore, it is called 'deep' by way of its text, as stated: 'Deep by way of its text, like the Sallasutta.' In this way, the meaning of 'deep by way of meaning' should be understood here. The profundity of the Mahāvedallasutta in terms of meaning is quite evident. 'Transcending the world' (lokuttara) is so called because it transcends the world; it is the ninefold immeasurable dhamma. That which is the essential meaning exists for these, hence they are called 'lokuttarā.' Therefore, he said: 'illuminators of the transcendent meaning.' 'Merely the dhamma of emptiness regarding a being' means: empty of a being or self, just the bare phenomena alone. And 'to be learned and to be mastered' is said with an inversion of gender and number; therefore he said: 'to be learned and to be mastered' (in plural form). 'Kavitā' is the work of a poet, what is made by a poet. Whatever work is done by someone, it is said to be 'done by them'; therefore, he said: 'Kavitā is what is made by poets.' The other term, 'kāveyya,' means 'kabba.' And 'kabba' means 'what is said by the poet.' Therefore, he said: 'it is a synonym of that.' 'Cittakkharā' means letters of various forms. 'Outside the teaching' means not belonging to the teaching. 'By their disciples' means by the disciples of any of those who are not known as 'disciples of the Buddhas.' 'Not being taken up' means not being taken up by way of listening, memorizing, practicing, investigating the meaning, and so on. 'They disappear' means they vanish from sight.

Āṇisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Āṇisutta is concluded.

8. Kaliṅgarasuttavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Kaliṅgarasutta

230. Kaliṅgaraṃ vuccati khuddakadārukhaṇḍaṃ, taṃ upadhānaṃ etesanti kaliṅgarūpadhānā. Licchavī pana khadiradaṇḍaṃ upadhānaṃ katvā tadā vihariṃsu. Tasmā vuttaṃ “khadiraghaṭikāsū”tiādi. Pakativijjusaññito natthi etesaṃ khaṇo vijjhaneti akkhaṇavedhino tato sīghataraṃ vijjhanato. “Akkhaṇa”nti vijju vuccati ittarakhaṇattā. Akkhaṇobhāsena lakkhaṇavedhakā akkhaṇavedhino. Anekadhā bhinnassa vālassa vijjhanena vālavedhino. Vālekadeso hi idha “vālo”ti gahito.

230. 'Kaliṅgara' is said to be a small piece of wood; because they have that as a support, they are 'kaliṅgarūpadhānā.' The Licchavis, however, having made a stick of khadira wood their support, lived thus at that time. Therefore, it is said, 'in the khadira-sticks,' and so on. There is no moment for them in piercing that is as long as ordinary lightning, thus they are 'akkhaṇavedhino' (instantaneous piercers), because they pierce even faster than that. 'Akkhaṇa' is said to be lightning, due to its brief moment. Those who pierce a target in the flash of a moment are 'akkhaṇavedhino.' They are 'vālavedhino' (hair-piercers) because they pierce a hair that has been split in many ways. Indeed, here a single part of a hair is taken as 'vāla.'

Bahudeva divasabhāgaṃ padhānānuyogato uppannadarathaparissamavinodanatthaṃ nhāyitvā. Te sandhāyāti te tathārūpe padhānakammikabhikkhū sandhāya. Idaṃ idāni vuccamānaṃ atthajātaṃ vuttaṃ porāṇaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Ayampi dīpoti [M 2.0192] tambapaṇṇidīpamāha. Padhānānuyuñjanavelāya nivedanavasena tattha tattha ekajjhaṃ pahataghaṇḍinigghoseneva ekaghaṇḍinigghoso, tattha tattha paṇṇasālādīsu vasantānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasena ekapadhānabhūto. Nānāmukhoti anurādhapurassa pacchimadisāyaṃ eko vihāro, pilicchikoḷinagarassa puratthimadisāyaṃ. Ubhayattha pavattaghaṇḍisaddā antarāpavattaghaṇḍisaddehi missetvā osaranti. Kalyāṇiyaṃ pavattaghaṇḍisaddo tathā nāgadīpe.

Having bathed to relieve the fatigue and weariness arising from application to striving for a great part of the day. 'Referring to them' means referring to such monks engaged in the practice of striving. This collection of meanings, now being explained, was stated in the ancient commentary. 'This island also' means he speaks of the island of Tambapaṇṇi. At the time of engaging in striving, by way of announcement, the sound of a single bell was like the sound of a bell struck simultaneously in various places; on account of the monks dwelling in leaf huts and so on in those various places, it became a single place of striving. 'Nānāmukha' refers to a monastery to the west of Anurādhapura, and another to the east of the city of Pilicchikoḷi. The sounds of the bells ringing in both places, mingling with the sounds of bells ringing in between, spread out. The sound of the bell ringing in Kalyāṇi was likewise in Nāgadīpa.

Kaliṅgarasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kaliṅgarasutta is concluded.

9. Nāgasuttavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Nāgasutta

231. Atikkantavelanti bhattānumodanaupanisinnakathāvelato atikkantavelaṃ. Asambhinnenāti sarasampattito asambhinnena, sarassa uccāraṇasampattiṃ aparihāpetvāti attho. Aparisuddhāsayatāya neva guṇavaṇṇāya na ñāṇabalāya hoti. Tanti taṃ tathā paccayānaṃ paribhuñjanaṃ, taṃ tathā micchāpaṭipajjanaṃ.

231. ‘Beyond the proper time’ means beyond the time for the meal’s appreciation and the conversation when seated. ‘Unbroken’ means unbroken in the accomplishment of tone; that is, without diminishing the accomplishment of tone in utterance. Due to an impure intention, it is neither for the praise of virtues nor for the power of knowledge. ‘That’ means that partaking of requisites in such a way, that wrong practice in such a way.

Nāgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Nāgasutta is concluded.

10. Biḷārasuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Biḷārasutta

232. Gharānaṃ [V 2.0171] sandhīti gharena gharassa sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ. Saha malena vattatīti samalaṃ. Gehato gāmato ca nikkhamanacandanikaṭṭhānaṃ. Saṅkāraṭṭhānanti saṅkārakūṭaṃ. Keci “sandhisaṅkārakūṭaṭṭhāna”nti vadanti. Vuṭṭhānanti āpannaāpattito, na kilesato vuṭṭhānaṃ, suddhante adhiṭṭhānaṃ. Taṃ pana yathāāpannāya āpattiyā “desanā”tveva vuccatīti āha “desanā paññāyatī”ti.

232. 'The junction of houses' means the place where one house is connected to another. 'With dirt' (samalaṃ) is so called because it exists together with dirt. The place near the exit-gate from a house or a village. 'A place for refuse' means a refuse heap. Some say 'a place of junctions and refuse heaps.' 'Rising' means rising from an offense one has fallen into, not rising from defilements; at the end of the purification, it is a determination. But that, according to the offense that has been committed, is called simply 'confession'; therefore he said, 'a confession is made known'.

Biḷārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Biḷārasutta is concluded.

11. Siṅgālasuttavaṇṇanā

11. The Commentary on the Siṅgālasutta

233. Ettakampīti [M 2.0193] iminā jarasiṅgālena laddhabbaṃ cittassādamattampi na labhissati sakalameva kappaṃ sabbaso avīcijālāhi nirantaraṃ jhāyamānatāya niccadukkhāturabhāvato.

233. 'Not even this much' means he will not obtain even the slight satisfaction of mind that this old jackal obtains, because for an entire aeon he will be continuously burning in the flames of Avīci, being completely afflicted by constant suffering.

Siṅgālasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Siṅgālasutta is concluded.

12. Dutiyasiṅgālasuttavaṇṇanā

12. The Commentary on the Second Siṅgālasutta

234. Katajānananti katūpakārajānanaṃ. Kataveditāti tasseva paresaṃ pākaṭakaraṇavasena jānanameva. Ācāramevāti katāparādhameva.

234. ‘One who knows what is done’ means knowing the help that was done. ‘One who acknowledges what is done’ means knowing it by way of making it manifest to others. ‘One’s conduct alone’ means the offense done.

Dutiyasiṅgālasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Siṅgālasutta is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

The Sāratthappakāsinī, Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Opammasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Exposition of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Opammasaṃyutta is concluded.

10. Bhikkhusaṃyuttaṃ

10. The Bhikkhusaṃyutta

1. Kolitasuttavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Kolitasutta

235. Sāvakānaṃ [V 2.0172][M 2.0194] ālāpoti sāvakānaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ uddissa ālāpo. Buddhehi sadisā mā homāti buddhāciṇṇaṃ samudācāraṃ akathentehi sāvakehi, “āvuso bhikkhave”ti ālapitā bhikkhū, “āvuso”ti paṭivacanaṃ denti, na, “bhante”ti. Dutiyajjhāne vitakkavicārā nirujjhanti tesaṃ nirodheneva tassa jhānassa uppādetabbato. Yesaṃ nirodhāti yesaṃ vacīsaṅgārānaṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ nirujjhanena suvikkhambhitabhāvena saddāyatanaṃ appavattiṃ gacchati kāraṇassa dūrato passambhitattā. Ariyoti niddoso. Parisuddho tuṇhībhāvo, na titthiyānaṃ mūgabbataggahaṇaṃ viya aparisuddhoti adhippāyo. Paṭhamajjhānādīnīti ādi-saddena tatiyajjhānādīni saṅgaṇhāti.

235. ‘Addressing the disciples’ means an address directed towards a fellow monastic. ‘May we not be like the Buddhas’ refers to disciples who do not speak of the customary practices of the Buddhas. Monks who are addressed by such disciples as ‘friends, bhikkhus,’ reply with ‘friend,’ not ‘venerable sir.’ In the second jhāna, initial and sustained thought cease, for that jhāna is to be produced precisely through their cessation. ‘By whose cessation’ means that by the cessation, the thorough suppression, of those verbal formations—initial and sustained thought—the sound base becomes inactive, because its cause has been calmed from afar. ‘Noble’ means faultless. The silence is pure; the meaning is that it is not impure like the heretics’ undertaking of the vow of muteness. ‘First jhāna, etc.’: by the word ‘etc.’ it includes the third jhāna and so on.

Ārammaṇabhūtena vitakkena saha gatā pavattāti vitakkasahagatāti āha “vitakkārammaṇā”ti. Vitakkārammaṇatā ca saññāmanasikārānaṃ sukhumaārammaṇaggahaṇavasena daṭṭhabbā. Tenāha “na santato upaṭṭhahiṃsū”ti. Na paguṇaṃ sammadeva vasībhāvassa anāpāditattā. Saññāmanasikārāpīti tatiyajjhānādhigamāya pavattiyamānā saññāmanasikārāpi hānabhāgiyāva ahesuṃ, na visesabhāgiyā. Sammā ṭhapehīti bahiddhā vikkhepaṃ pahāya sammā ajjhattameva cittaṃ ṭhapehi. Ekaggaṃ karohīti teneva vikkhepapaṭibāhanena avihatamānasatāya cittasamādhānavasena ekaggaṃ karohi. Āropehīti īsakampi bahumpi apatitaṃ katvā kammaṭṭhānārammaṇe āropehi. Dutiyaaggasāvakabhūmiyā pāripūriyā āyasmā mahābhiñño, na yathā tathāti āha “mahābhiññatanti chaḷabhiññata”nti. Iminā upāyenāti iminā “atha kho maṃ, āvuso”tiādinā vuttena upāyena. Vaḍḍhetvāti uttari uttari visesabhāgiyabhāvāpādanena samādhiṃ paññañca brūhetvā brūhetvā.

Because it occurs together with initial thought that has become its object, it is ‘accompanied by initial thought’; hence it is said, ‘having initial thought as its object.’ And this state of having initial thought as an object should be understood in the sense of perception and attention grasping a subtle object. Therefore, it is said, ‘they did not present themselves peacefully to me.’ Not skillfully, because mastery had not been properly attained. ‘Perception and attention too’: even the perception and attention occurring for the attainment of the third jhāna were conducive to decline, not to distinction. ‘Establish it rightly’ means: having abandoned external distraction, rightly establish the mind internally. ‘Make it one-pointed’ means: make it one-pointed by means of concentration of mind, with an undisturbed mind, by warding off that same distraction. ‘Lift it up’ means: having made what has fallen away, whether a little or a lot, not fallen, raise it up to the meditation object. For the fulfillment of the stage of the second chief disciple, the venerable one possessed great direct knowledge, not just in any way; thus it is said, ‘“great direct knowledge” means the six direct knowledges.’ ‘By this method’ means by the method stated beginning with ‘Then, friend...’ ‘Having developed’ means: having repeatedly cultivated concentration and wisdom by bringing about states conducive to distinction more and more.

Kolitasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kolita Sutta is concluded.

2. Upatissasuttavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Upatissa Sutta

236. Atiuḷārampi [V 2.0173][M 2.0195] sattaṃ vā saṅkhāraṃ vā sandhāya vuttaṃ sabbatthameva sabbaso chandarāgassa suppahīnattā. Jānanatthaṃ pucchati satthuguṇānaṃ ativiya uḷāratamabhāvato.

236. ‘Even the most sublime’ is said in reference to a being or a formation, because desire and lust have been thoroughly abandoned in every way and in all respects. He asks for the sake of knowing, because of the exceedingly sublime nature of the Teacher’s qualities.

Upatissasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Upatissa Sutta is concluded.

3. Ghaṭasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Ghaṭa Sutta

237. Pariveṇaggenāti pariveṇabhāgena. Keci “ekavihāreti ekacchanne ekasmiṃ āvāse”ti vadanti. Teti te dvepi therā. Pāṭiyekkesu ṭhānesūti visuṃ visuṃ ṭhānesu. Nisīdantīti divāvihāraṃ nisīdanti. Oḷāriko nāma jāto parittadhammārammaṇattā tassa. Teti thero bhagavā ca.

237. ‘Pariveṇaggena’ means by a section of the monastery. Some say, ‘“in a single dwelling” means in a single residence, under one roof.’ ‘Te’ means those two elders. ‘Pāṭiyekkesu ṭhānesu’ means in separate places. ‘Nisīdanti’ means they sit for the day’s abiding. He has become what is called ‘gross’ because his object is a limited teaching. ‘Te’ means the elder and the Blessed One.

Paripuṇṇavīriyoti catukiccasādhanavasena sampuṇṇavīriyo. Paggahitavīriyoti īsakampi saṅkocaṃ anāpajjitvā pavattitavīriyo. Upanikkhepanamattassevāti samīpe ṭhapanamattasseva.

‘Paripuṇṇavīriyo’ means one whose energy is complete with regard to accomplishing the four tasks. ‘Paggahitavīriyo’ means one whose energy is exerted without falling into even a little contraction. ‘Upanikkhepanamattasseva’ means merely the act of placing it nearby.

Catubhūmakadhammesu labbhamānattā paññāya “catubhūmakadhamme anupavisitvā ṭhitaṭṭhenā”ti vuttaṃ. Lakkhitabbaṭṭhena samādhi eva samādhilakkhaṇaṃ. Evaṃ vipassanālakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Aññamaññassāti aññassa aññassa nānālakkhaṇāti veditabbaṃ. Aññassāti itarassa. Dhuranti vahitabbabhāraṃ. Dvīsupi etesūti samādhilakkhaṇavipassanālakkhaṇesu sammāsambuddho nipphattiṃ gato.

Because wisdom is obtainable in the phenomena of the four planes, it is said, ‘in the sense that it stands having entered the phenomena of the four planes.’ In the sense of being that which should be marked, concentration itself is the characteristic of concentration. Thus, the characteristic of insight should be understood. ‘Aññamaññassa’ should be understood as the various characteristics of one and the other. ‘Aññassa’ means of the other. ‘Dhuraṃ’ means the burden to be carried. In both of these—the characteristic of concentration and the characteristic of insight—the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One has reached completion.

Ghaṭasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Ghaṭa Sutta is concluded.

4. Navasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Navaka Sutta

238. Abhicetasi nissitā ābhicetasikā. Paṭipakkhavidhamanena abhivisiṭṭhaṃ cittaṃ abhicittaṃ. Yasmā jhānānaṃ taṃsampayuttaṃ cittaṃ nissāya paccayo hotiyeva, tasmā “nissitāna”nti vuttaṃ. Nikāmalābhīti yathicchitalābhī[M 2.0196]. Yathāparicchedenāti yathākatena kālaparicchedena. Vipulalābhīti appamāṇalābhī. “Kasira”nti hi parittaṃ vuccati, tappaṭipakkhena [V 2.0174] akasiraṃ appamāṇaṃ. Tenāha “paguṇajjhānoti attho”ti. Sithilamārabbhāti sithilaṃ vīriyārambhaṃ katvāti atthoti āha “sithilaṃ vīriyaṃ pavattetvā”ti.

238. Dependent on the higher mind (abhicetasi), thus ābhicetasikā. The higher mind (abhicittaṃ) is the mind that is distinguished by the destruction of opposing states. Because it is indeed a condition dependent on the mind associated with the jhānas, it is therefore said to be ‘dependent.’ ‘Nikāmalābhī’ means one who obtains at will. ‘Yathāparicchedena’ means according to the established time-limit. ‘Vipulalābhī’ means one who obtains immeasurably. ‘Kasira’ means limited; its opposite, akasira, means immeasurable. Therefore it is said, ‘the meaning is “skilled in jhāna.”’ ‘Sithilamārabbhā’ means having made a slack effort; therefore it is said, ‘having exerted slack energy.’

Navasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Navaka Sutta is concluded.

5. Sujātasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Sujāta Sutta

239. Aññāni rūpānīti paresaṃ rūpāni. Atikkantarūpoti attano rūpasampattiyā rūpasobhāya atikkamitvā ṭhitarūpo, sucirampi velaṃ olokentassa tuṭṭhiāvaho. Dassanassa cakkhussa hitoti dassanīyo. Pasādaṃ āvahatīti pāsādiko. Chavivaṇṇasundaratāyāti chavivaṇṇassa ceva sarīrasaṇṭhānassa ca sobhanabhāvena.

239. ‘Aññāni rūpāni’ means the forms of others. ‘Atikkantarūpo’ means one whose form stands having surpassed others through his own accomplishment of form and beauty of form, bringing delight to one who gazes even for a very long time. Beneficial (hita) to the eye (cakkhussa) which sees (dassanassa), thus ‘lovely to see’ (dassanīyo). It brings (āvahati) confidence (pasādaṃ), thus ‘inspiring confidence’ (pāsādiko). ‘Chavivaṇṇasundaratāya’ means by the beauty of both the skin-complexion and the physical form.

Sujātasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sujāta Sutta is concluded.

6. Lakuṇḍakabhaddiyasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Lakuṇḍakabhaddiya Sutta

240. Virūpasarīravaṇṇanti asundarachavivaṇṇañceva asundarasaṇṭhānañca. Pamāṇavasenāti sarīrappamāṇavasena. Icchiticchitanti attanā icchiticchitaṃ. Mahāsārajjanti mahanto maṅkubhāvo.

240. ‘Virūpasarīravaṇṇa’ means both an unattractive skin-complexion and an unattractive physical form. ‘Pamāṇavasena’ means according to the body’s measure. ‘Icchiticchitaṃ’ means what is desired by oneself. ‘Mahāsārajjaṃ’ means great diffidence.

Guṇe āvajjetvāti attanā jānanakaniyāmena satthuno kāyaguṇe ca cārittaguṇe ca āvajjetvā manasi katvā.

‘Guṇe āvajjetvā’ means ‘having reflected on the qualities’—that is, having considered and taken to mind the Teacher’s bodily qualities and qualities of conduct by way of one’s own knowing.

Yojanāvaṭṭanti yojanaparikkhepaṃ.

‘Yojanāvaṭṭaṃ’ means a circumference of a yojana.

“Kāyasmī”ti gāthāsukhatthaṃ niranunāsikaṃ katvā niddesoti vuttaṃ “kāyasmi”nti. Akāraṇaṃ kāyappamāṇanti sarīrappamāṇaṃ nāma appamāṇaṃ, sīlādiguṇāva pamāṇanti adhippāyo.

The explanation ‘kāyasmiṃ’ is said to be made without the nasalization, as ‘kāyasmi,’ for the sake of metrical ease in the verse. ‘The measure of the body is not the determining factor’: the meaning is that the measure of the body is no true measure; rather, qualities such as virtue are the measure.

Lakuṇḍakabhaddiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Lakuṇḍakabhaddiya Sutta is concluded.

7. Visākhasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Visākha Sutta

241. Purassa [M 2.0197] esāti porī, cāturiyayuttatā. Tenāha “puravāsīna”ntiādi. Sā pana [V 2.0175] dutavilambitakhalitavasena appasannalūkhatādidosarahitā hotīti āha “pura…pe… vācāyā”ti. Asandiddhāyāti muttavācāya. Tenāha “apalibuddhāyā”tiādi. Na elaṃ dosaṃ galetīti anelagalā, avirujjhanavācā. Tenāha “niddosāyā”ti. Catusaccassa pakāsakā, na kadāci saccavimuttāti āha “catusaccapariyāpannāyā”ti. Tā hi cattāri saccāni paricchijja āpādenti paṭipādenti pavattenti. Tenāha “cattāri saccāni amuñcitvā pavattāyā”ti. Dhajo nāma sabbadhammehi samussitaṭṭhena.

241. ‘Purassa esā’ (she is of the city), thus ‘porī’ (urbane), which is endowment with cleverness. Therefore it is said, ‘of the city-dwellers,’ etc. Moreover, because it is free from faults such as being unpleasant and rough by way of being swift, slow, or faltering, it is said, ‘urbane... speech.’ ‘Asandiddhāya’ means with clear speech. Therefore it is said, ‘unconfused,’ etc. ‘Na elaṃ dosaṃ galeti’ (does not swallow a fault), thus ‘anelagalā’ (flawless-throated), which means non-contradictory speech. Therefore it is said, ‘faultless.’ Because it illuminates the four truths and is never devoid of truth, it is said, ‘included within the four truths.’ For they, having defined the four truths, bring them about, establish them, and set them in motion. Therefore it is said, ‘proceeding without abandoning the four truths.’ A ‘banner’ (dhajo) is so called in the sense of being raised high by all good qualities.

Visākhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Visākha Sutta is concluded.

8. Nandasuttavaṇṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Nanda Sutta

242. Āraññikotiādīsu araññakathāsīsena senāsanapaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ dhutaṅgānaṃ, piṇḍapātakathāsīsena piṇḍapātapaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ, paṃsukūlikasīsena cīvarapaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ, taggahaṇeneva vīriyanissitadhutaṅgassa ca samādāya vattanaṃ dīpitanti veditabbaṃ. Āgatena bhagavatā aparabhāge kathitaṃ.

242. In ‘forest-dweller,’ etc., the ascetic practices connected with lodging are indicated under the heading of talk on the forest; those connected with almsfood under the heading of talk on almsfood; and those connected with robes under the heading of the rag-robe wearer. And it should be understood that by the taking up of those, the undertaking and practice of the ascetic practice dependent on energy is also shown. This was spoken later by the Blessed One who had come.

Nandasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Nanda Sutta is concluded.

9. Tissasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Tissa Sutta

243. Bhaṇḍakanti pattacīvaraṃ. Nisīdiyeva vattassa asikkhitattā. Tujjanatthena vācā eva sattiyoti āha “vācāsattīhī”ti.

243. 'Bhaṇḍaka' means bowl and robe. He just sat down, because he was untrained in proper conduct. Speech is indeed a dart in the sense of piercing. Thus he said, 'with darts of speech.'

Vācāya sannitodakenāti vacanasaṅkhātena samantato niccaṃ katvā upatudanato sannitudakena. Vibhattialopena so niddeso. Tenāha “vacanapatodenā”ti.

'Vācāya sannitodakena' means 'by the goad of speech,' in the sense of being constantly pricked all around by what is termed speech. That designation is by way of elision of the case ending. Therefore, it is said, 'by the goad of words.'

Uccakule jāti etassāti jātimā, brahmajātiko isi. Mātaṅgoti caṇḍālo. Tatthāti kumbhakārasālāyaṃ. Okāsaṃ yāci [M 2.0198] kumbhakāraṃ. Mahantaṃ disvā āha – “paṭhamataraṃ paviṭṭho pabbajito”ti. Tatthevāti tassāyeva sālāya dvāraṃ nissāya dvārasamīpe. Meti mayā. Khama mayhanti mayhaṃ aparādhaṃ khamassu. Teti tayā. Puna teti tava. Gaṇhi uggantuṃ appadānavasena. Tenāha “nāssa uggantuṃ adāsī”ti. Pabujjhiṃsūti niddāya pabujjhiṃsu pakatiyā pabujjhanavelāya upagatattā.

One whose birth is in a high family is 'jātimā,' a sage of brahmin birth. 'Mātaṅga' means a caṇḍāla. 'Tattha' means in the potter's workshop. He asked the potter for space. Seeing the great one, he said, 'The renunciate entered first.' 'Tattheva' means right there, near the door, relying on the door of that very workshop. 'Me' means 'by me.' 'Khama mayhaṃ' means 'forgive my offense.' 'Te' means 'by you.' Again, 'te' means 'your.' He took it in the sense of not giving leave to go forth. Therefore, it is said, 'He did not allow him to go forth.' 'Pabujjhiṃsu' means they awoke from sleep, because it was the usual time for waking up.

Chavoti [V 2.0176] nihīno. Anantamāyoti vividhamāyo māyāvī.

'Chavo' means low, degraded. 'Anantamāyo' means one with various deceits, deceitful.

Soti mattikāpiṇḍo. “Sattadhā bhijjī”ti etthāyamadhippāyo – yaṃ tena tāpasena pāramitāparibhāvanasamiddhāhi nānāvihārasamāpattiparipūritāhi sīladiṭṭhisampadādīhi susaṅkhatasantāne mahākaruṇādhivāse mahāsatte bodhisatte ariyūpavādakammaṃ abhisapasaṅkhātaṃ pharusavacanaṃ pavattitaṃ, taṃ mahāsattassa khettavisesabhāvato tassa ca ajjhāsayapharusatāya diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ hutvā sace so mahāsattaṃ na khamāpeti, taṃ kakkhaḷaṃ hutvā vipaccanasabhāvaṃ jātaṃ, khamāpite pana mahāsatte payogasampattipaṭibāhitattā avipākadhammataṃ āpajjati ahosikammabhāvato. Ayañhi ariyūpavādapāpassa diṭṭhadhammavedanīyassa ca dhammatā. Yaṃ taṃ bodhisattena sūriyuggamananivāraṇaṃ kataṃ, ayaṃ bodhisattena diṭṭho upāyo. Tena hi ubbāḷhā manussā bodhisattassa santike tāpasaṃ ānetvā khamāpesuṃ. Sopi ca mahāsattassa guṇe jānitvā tasmiṃ cittaṃ pasādesi. Yaṃ panassa matthake mattikāpiṇḍassa ṭhapanaṃ tassa sattadhā phālanaṃ kataṃ, taṃ manussānaṃ cittānurakkhaṇatthaṃ. Aññathā hi ime pabbajitā samānā cittassa vasaṃ vattanti, na pana cittamattano vase vattāpentīti mahāsattampi tena sadisaṃ katvā gaṇheyyuṃ, tadassa nesaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti. Patirūpanti yuttaṃ.

'So' means a lump of clay. 'May it break into seven pieces'—this is the intention here: that the harsh speech, called a curse, which was uttered by that ascetic as an act of reproaching a noble one against the great being, the Bodhisatta—who, in his well-prepared continuum, was a dwelling place of great compassion, perfected by the development of perfections, replete with various attainments of meditative states, and endowed with the excellence of morality and views, etc.—that speech, due to the special nature of the great being as a field of merit and the harshness of the ascetic's intention, was to be experienced in this very life. If that ascetic did not have the great being forgive him, it would become harsh and of a nature to ripen. But when the great being was made to forgive, due to being obstructed by the successful act of forgiveness, it became non-resultant, due to its nature as a defunct deed. This indeed is the nature of the evil of reproaching a noble one, that it is to be experienced in this very life. That which was done by the Bodhisatta to prevent the sunrise—this was a method seen by the Bodhisatta. Then, the agitated people brought the ascetic to the Bodhisatta and made him seek forgiveness. And he, knowing the virtues of the great being, placed confidence in him. The placing of the lump of clay on his head and its breaking into seven pieces was for the sake of protecting the people's minds. Otherwise, they might take even the great being to be similar to him, thinking, 'These renunciates follow the sway of the mind, and do not bring the mind under their own control,' and that would be for their long-term harm and suffering. 'Patirūpa' means suitable, appropriate.

Tissasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Tissa Sutta is concluded.

10. Theranāmakasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Sutta Named Thera

244. Atīte khandhapañcaketi atīte attabhāve. Chandarāgappahānenāti chandarāgassa accantameva jahanena. Pahīnaṃ nāma hoti anapekkhapariccāgato. Paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ nāma hoti sabbaso chaḍḍitattā. Tayo [M 2.0199] bhaveti iminā upādiṇṇakadhammānaṃyeva gahaṇaṃ. Sabbā khandhāyatanadhātuyo cāti iminā upādiṇṇānampi anupādiṇṇānampi dvidhā pavattalokiyadhammānaṃ gahaṇaṃ avisesetvā vuttattā. Viditaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā ṭhitaṃ pariññābhisamayavasena. Tesvevāti tebhūmakadhammesu eva. Anupalittaṃ amathitaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ taṇhādiṭṭhisaṃkilesābhāvato. Tadeva sabbanti heṭṭhā tīsupi padesu idha sabbaggahaṇena gahitaṃ tebhūmakavaṭṭaṃ. Jahitvāti pahānābhisamayavasena. Taṇhā khīyati etthāti taṇhakkhayasaṅkhāte nibbāne vimuttaṃ. Tamahanti taṃ uttamapuggalaṃ ekavihāriṃ brūmi taṇhādutiyassa abhāvato. Ettha ca pariññāpahānābhisamayakathanena itarampi abhisamayaṃ atthato kathitamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

244. 'Atīte khandhapañcake' means in a past existence. 'Chandarāgappahānenā' means by the complete abandoning of desire and lust. 'Pahīnaṃ' is so called from its being an abandonment without longing. 'Paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ' is so called from being utterly discarded. 'Tayo bhava' (three existences) means by this, the grasping of only phenomena that are clung to. 'Sabbā khandhāyatanadhātuyo' (all aggregates, sense bases, and elements) means by this, the grasping of worldly phenomena that occur in two ways, both clung to and not clung to, because it is stated without distinction. 'Viditaṃ' means made clear and established through the mode of full understanding and realization. 'Tesveva' means in the phenomena of the three realms alone. 'Anupalittaṃ amathitaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ' (unstained, untainted, undefiled) means due to the absence of the defilements of craving and wrong view. 'Tadeva sabbaṃ' (that very all) refers to the cycle of the three realms, which is included here by the term 'all' in the three passages below. 'Jahitvā' (having abandoned) means through the realization of abandonment. 'Taṇhā khīyati ettha' (craving is destroyed here) refers to liberation in Nibbāna, which is known as the destruction of craving. 'Tamahaṃ' (that one) refers to that supreme person, whom I call 'dwelling alone' because of the absence of a second, namely craving. And here, it should be understood that by the statement of the realization of full understanding and abandonment, other aspects of realization too are spoken of in meaning.

Theranāmakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sutta Named Thera is concluded.

11. Mahākappinasuttavaṇṇanā

11. Commentary on the Mahākappina Sutta

245. Mahākappinoti [V 2.0177] pūjāvacanametaṃ yathā “mahāmoggallāno”ti. Tathārūpanti “buddho dhammo”tiādikaṃ guṇavisesavantapaṭibaddhaṃ. Sāsananti desantarato āgatavacanaṃ. Jaṅghavāṇijāti jaṅghacārino vāṇijā. Kiñci sāsananti apubbapavattidīpakaṃ kiñci vacananti pucchi. Pīti uppajji yathā taṃ suciraṃ katābhinīhāratāya paripakkañāṇassa. Aparimāṇaṃ guṇassa aparimāṇato sabbaññuguṇaparidīpanato, sesaratanadvaye niyyānikabhāvadīpanato diṭṭhisīlasāmaññena saṃhatabhāvadīpanatoti vattabbaṃ. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjamāne apāyadukkhato saṃsāradukkhato ca apatante dhāretīti dhammo. Suparisuddhadiṭṭhisīlasāmaññena saṃhatoti saṅghoti. Ratanattho pana tiṇṇampi sadiso evāti.

245. 'Mahākappina' is an honorific term, just like 'Mahāmoggallāna.' 'Tathārūpa' means connected with one possessing special qualities such as 'Buddha, Dhamma,' etc. 'Sāsana' means a message that has come from another country. 'Jaṅghavāṇija' means merchants who travel on foot. 'Kiñci sāsana' means he asked for some statement illuminating an unprecedented occurrence. Joy arose, as is fitting for one whose wisdom is matured due to long-cultivated aspiration. It should be said that it is immeasurable because of the immeasurability of the qualities, because it illuminates the qualities of the Omniscient One, because it illuminates the liberating nature of the remaining two jewels, and because it illuminates the state of being united through the commonality of view and virtue. The Dhamma is so called because it holds back one who practices as instructed from falling into the suffering of the lower realms and the suffering of saṃsāra. The Sangha is so called because it is united through the commonality of supremely pure view and virtue.

Navasatasahassāni adāsi devī. Tumheti rājiniṃ gāravena bahuvacanena vadati. Rāgoti anugacchantarāgo.

The queen gave nine hundred thousand. 'Tumhe' is spoken to the queen respectfully, in the plural. 'Rāga' means subsequent lust.

Janiteti kammakilesehi nibbattite. Kammakilesehi pajātattā pajāti pajāsaddo janitasaddena samānatthoti āha – “janite, pajāyāti attho”ti. Aṭṭhahi vijjāhīti ambaṭṭhasutte (dī. ni. 1.278) āgatanayena. Tattha hi vipassanāñāṇamanomayiddhīhi saha cha abhiññā “aṭṭha vijjā”ti āgatā[M 2.0200]. Tapati paṭipakkhavidhamanena vijjotati, taṃ sūriyassa virocananti āha – “tapatīti virocatī”ti. Jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā samāhitena cittena vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā nisinnoti āha – “duvidhena jhānena jhāyamāno”ti. Sabbamaṅgalagāthāti sabbamaṅgalāvirodhī gāthāti vadanti. Tathā hi vadanti –

'Janita' means produced by kamma and defilements. Because of being born from kamma and defilements, 'pajāti' (offspring) is synonymous with 'janita' (produced); thus he said, 'janite means pajāyati.' 'With eight knowledges'—as mentioned in the Ambaṭṭha Sutta (Dī. Ni. 1.278) in the manner described there. There, indeed, insight knowledge along with the six higher knowledges and mind-made power are referred to as 'eight knowledges.' 'Tapati' means it shines by dispelling opposing forces; that is the sun's radiance. Thus he said, 'tapatīti means virocatī.' Having attained jhāna, having developed insight with a concentrated mind, having attained fruition attainment, one sits—thus he said, 'meditating with twofold jhāna.' 'Sabbamaṅgalagāthā' (all-auspicious verses)—they say these are verses that do not contradict all auspiciousness. Indeed, they say—

“Maṅgalaṃ bhagavā buddho, dhammo saṅgho ca maṅgalaṃ;

Sabbesampi ca sattānaṃ, sa puññavitamaṅgala”nti.

The Blessed One, the Buddha, is a blessing; the Dhamma and the Sangha are blessings; and for all beings, that merit is the supreme blessing.

Pūjaṃ kāretvā ekaṃ agārikadhammakathikaṃ upāsakaṃ āha. Ettha ca “jhāyī tapatī”ti iminā ārammaṇūpanijjhānānaṃ gahitattā dhammaratanaṃ gahitameva. “Brāhmaṇo”ti iminā saṅgharatanaṃ gahitameva. Buddharatanaṃ pana sarūpeneva gahitanti.

Having performed the worship, he addressed a lay Dhamma speaker. And here, by 'the meditator, the ardent one,' the Dhamma jewel is indeed included, because the meditative absorptions on the object are included. By 'the Brahmin,' the Sangha jewel is indeed included. But the Buddha jewel is included in its own form.

Mahākappinasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Mahākappina Sutta is concluded.

12. Sahāyakasuttavaṇṇanā

12. The Commentary on the Sahāyaka Sutta

246. Sammā [V 2.0178] saṃsandanavasena eti pavattatīti sameti, sammādiṭṭhiādi. Sammā cirarattaṃ cirakālaṃ sameti etesaṃ atthīti cirarattaṃsametikā. Tenāha “dīgharatta”ntiādi. Idāni imesanti etarahi etesaṃ. Ayaṃ sāsanadhammo ajjhāsayato payogato ca sammā saṃsandati sameti, tasmā majjhe bhinnaṃ viya samameva na visadisaṃ. Kiñca tato eva buddhena bhagavatā paveditadhammavinaye etesaṃ paṭipattisāsanadhammo sobhati virocatīti attho. Ariyappavediteti ariyena sammāsambuddhena sammadeva pakāsite ariyadhamme. Sammadeva samucchedapaṭippassaddhivinayānaṃ vasena suṭṭhu vinītā sabbakilesadarathapariḷāhānaṃ vūpasamena.

246. It is called 'sameti' because it flows and proceeds correctly by way of proper connection—right view and so on. For them, it correctly comes together for a long time; hence, they are 'cirarattaṃsametikā'—those for whom it has come together for a long time. Therefore, he said, 'for a long time,' and so on. Now, 'imesaṃ' means 'at present' or 'of these.' This teaching of the Dispensation converges and connects correctly in terms of inclination and practice; therefore, even if it appears broken in the middle, it is uniform and not disparate. Furthermore, in this very Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Blessed Buddha, the practice-teaching of these shines and radiates—this is the meaning. 'In the one proclaimed by the Noble One' means in the Noble Dhamma rightly expounded by the Noble One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Truly well-trained by way of the discipline of eradication and tranquilization, through the subsiding of all defilements, distress, and burning.

Sahāyakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sahāyaka Sutta is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

From the Sāratthappakāsinī, the Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Bhikkhusaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The exposition of the hidden meanings in the Commentary on the Bhikkhu Saṃyutta is concluded.

Niṭṭhitā ca sāratthappakāsiniyā

And thus is concluded from the Sāratthappakāsinī,

Saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya nidānavaggavaṇṇanā.

the Commentary on the Nidāna Section of the Saṃyutta Nikāya.
